# Changelog

All notable changes to this repository are documented here. Format loosely
follows Keep a Changelog; versioning follows Semantic Versioning.

## [1.636.0] — 2026-11-01

### Changed
- `.claude/skills/agentic-delivery/references/red-gate-triage.md`, admission section: guidance for a gap in admission scoped to a change's own specs. A PR that a train dropped for a failing spec can return after a fix push that touches other files; the spec is no longer selected, and the PR breaks the next train on the same spec. Admission should also run, on the PR merged onto the base, every spec named in the PR's earlier drop records (so drop records must name the failing spec ids) and a capped hot set of specs that refused two or more PRs in the last seven days; a failure among them is triaged with the same solo re-runs as any train red, and a base-red one is subtracted, never charged to the PR. Not yet implemented in `train_land.sh`, which records no spec ids per drop and selects no hot set.

### Added
- Eval `admission-reruns-prior-drop-and-hot-specs` in `.claude/skills/agentic-delivery/evals/evals.json`.

size-budget-raise: .claude/skills/agentic-delivery/references/red-gate-triage.md 29039→30007 prior-drop and hot-set admission paragraph

### Fixed
- `ready()` in `.claude/skills/agentic-delivery/scripts/flow_alarm.py` counted the train's own progress marker (the `perun/train-stage` status that `merge_train.py stage` posts pending on each PR it queued) as a check, so every PR a train had queued read as not ready. The stop-starting cap and the `symptom` alarm then undercounted the waiting queue exactly while a train was running, and the cap let new work start that it should have held. `ready()` now skips the marker in any state, with the same rule `landing_watchdog.green()` uses; any other pending status still blocks, and a PR whose only status is the marker has no check. Tests: `python3 scripts/test_flow_alarm.py` adds one case (a PR the train queued or dropped stays ready, also with the script's own directory off `sys.path`; another pending status blocks; the cap counts the train's queue).

### Added
- At the cap, the stop-starting hook (`.claude/skills/agentic-delivery/scripts/flow_alarm.py`) now lets through one lone `gh pr create` of a branch already pushed to origin when its diff against `origin/<base>` holds only throughput paths and fewer than `PERUN_THROUGHPUT_OPEN` (default 2) such PRs are open. The hook used to deny test-runtime cuts and CI parallelism along with everything else, and the only override was the free-text `# priority:` marker, which a project may restrict to a human approver, so the work that would shorten the queue waited behind it. The exemption is a grant: whatever the hook cannot judge keeps the deny. It judges a command only when its words start `gh pr create` (or `new`) and hold no operator (`;`, `&&`, `|`, `&`, a newline, a redirect, a heredoc), no word holding a `$`, `*`, `?`, `[`, `{` or backtick (the shell may expand it into other words, and quotes are not seen, so a quoted title with one of them keeps the deny too), no word that starts `#`, no `-R`, `-H`, `--repo` or `--head`, and no bundled or joined short option (`-dB`, `-Brelease`). A command that switches branch, pushes or changes directory first, a second create, a body built with `$(...)`, a brace word that expands into a later `--base` or `--repo`, a glob that expands into a file named like an option, a comment that looks like an option, and a PR for another repo or head are therefore denied. The base is the last `--base V`, `--base=V` or `-B V`, else `origin/HEAD`; a `gh-merge-base` branch config with any non-empty value and no `--base` keeps the deny. The changed files are `git diff --name-only` from the merge base of `HEAD` and `origin/<base>`, read in the hook's `cwd` with rename detection, `diff.relative` and submodule hiding turned off, so a product file moved into `tests/` or a submodule bump still counts. `HEAD` must be the one commit that `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` points at, with no other remote ref there, so the ledger name is the head name the PR will have; an unpushed branch, or a pushed copy ahead of or behind `HEAD`, is not judged. `git remote` must list no remote but `origin`, and every value of `remote.origin.gh-resolved` (written by `gh repo set-default`) must be `base`, or none set: gh opens the PR on its own base repo and prefers a remote named `upstream`, so with another remote or another default repo the diff read against `origin/<base>` may not be the PR's diff, and the deny stands. Remote names, ref names and config values are compared whole, split only at a newline (config values at a NUL, since a value may hold a newline): git allows U+0085, U+2028 and Unicode spaces in a name, so `origin` plus one of them is another remote or ref. The default paths are test directories and files, CI config and test-runner config; `PERUN_THROUGHPUT_PATHS` (comma-separated globs) replaces them. Below the cap, and with `# priority:`, nothing changes.
- The deny stands, as before, for an empty diff, a path outside the list, a git call that fails or takes over 5 seconds, and any error while judging (only reading the queue still fails open). A grant is appended to `<git-common-dir>/perun-throughput.jsonl`, and the exempt PRs open are the ledger branches among the open PRs' head names, which the single `gh pr list` call now also returns (`headRefName`), so there is no second `gh` call.
- Every deny is appended to `<git-common-dir>/perun-flow-denials.jsonl` as `{"at","class","ready","cap"}`: class `throughput-cap` when only the exempt cap blocked a judged branch, else `work`. The log holds no file names or command text, and a write error is ignored.

### Changed
- The deny message names the exemption as a lone `gh pr create` (body in `--body-file`) of a branch already pushed to origin, while fewer than N such PRs are open, with N the parsed `PERUN_THROUGHPUT_OPEN`; when that value is not a number the clause is left out. The module docstring said `Side effects: none (read-only)`, which would now be an over-claim; it names the two appends and the judging rules. `.claude/skills/agentic-delivery/references/flow-guards.md` gains two sentences on the exemption and the denial log.
- Limits, listed once in the script docstring: the globs match names, not contents (a CI-config edit passes whatever it changes, and `spec/`, `*.spec.*` and `test_*.py` can name product files, so narrow the list with `PERUN_THROUGHPUT_PATHS`); only creation is judged; the ledger is local; two sessions can race for the last slot; a `GH_REPO` exported in the shell is not seen; with more than 100 open PRs an exempt PR can fall outside the list.
- Tests: `python3 scripts/test_flow_alarm.py` goes from 22 to 68 tests. The new `Throughput` class runs the hook against a throwaway repo under a hermetic git environment (no user config, a fixed identity, no repo search above the temp dir) with a fake `gh`; every grant case pushes its branch first. It covers each shape above (bundled and joined options, another repo or head, two creates, a branch switch, push or `cd` first, an expansion, a substitution, a heredoc, a comment, a line continuation, a brace word, a glob word, a second remote, a remote or ref name that only looks like `origin`, a default repo set to another repo or to several values, a repeated or empty `--base`, a configured merge base with one value or several), an unpushed branch, a pushed copy behind or ahead of `HEAD`, a second remote ref, `diff.relative` and a submodule under a hiding config, the exempt cap, the path list and the denial log, and the message with a number and with a value that is not one. The existing tests now run in a plain temp dir, so they neither touch the real repo nor write its denial log.
size-budget-raise: .claude/skills/agentic-delivery/references/flow-guards.md 2105→2684 two sentences on the throughput exemption and the denial log

### Fixed
- `green()` in `.claude/skills/agentic-delivery/scripts/landing_watchdog.py` judged every status in a PR's check rollup, including the train's own progress marker (the `perun/train-stage` status: pending while a run is queued, gating or landing, failure after a skipped or failed run), while `merge_train.py` judges check runs only. A PR left in a dead run, or skipped once, therefore stopped counting as a green PR waiting, and every signal built on that count undercounted it. That one status is now ignored, both when judging the checks and when testing that the PR has any; any other pending status still blocks.
- `ci_head` in `train_land.sh` had the same defect, and it is a pre-existing one, not a regression of this change: it judged the whole rollup including the train's own marker, so after a skipped, failed or deferred train, where the marker is failure or error, the solo re-ride escape (a PR that rode trains without landing is landed alone once its own checks pass) could never see an all-green rollup for exactly the PRs it exists for, and never fired. It now drops the marker before judging, still requires at least one remaining check, and still reads a lookup or parse failure as not green.

### Added
- Run liveness in `landing_watchdog.py`: the rate alarms say "slow" but could not tell a slow train from a dead one. The probe now also reads the train's progress markers from the open PRs (stage = first word of the status description, time = its `at=<epoch>` else the status creation time, expected run time = `eta<=Ns` else 60 min; a marker with no stage word or no time is skipped) and the time of the newest commit on the default branch's first-parent line (a landing; a time more than 5 minutes ahead of the clock is ignored). The last train activity is the newest of every marker, whatever its run, and that landing; an outcome beats a live marker at the same second. Two warn-only messages come from it, a stuck line and a clause on the stall line, with the same throttle, cache, hook and `check` CLI, failing open.
- "Train run stuck: run R posted <stage> on K PRs X min ago (expected <= Y min), no outcome since. Check the train runner, not the PRs." fires only when the last train activity is itself a queued, gating or landing marker older than 1.5 times its expected time; it names that marker's run and stage and counts the PRs carrying the same run and stage. A run id comes from each `merge_train.py stage` call rather than from a whole train, so markers are not grouped by run: any newer marker or landing supersedes an older live one, which keeps a dead run's marker on a PR no later train re-posted from alarming for ever.
- " No train run in X min: start the train or check its runner." is a clause on the existing stall line (0 merged in the window with green PRs waiting), not a line of its own. It is added when markers exist, the last activity is not a live marker, and it is older than the larger of 1.5 times its expected time and the check window, with X counted from that last activity (a landing counts, so a healthy repo with an old skipped marker on an open PR stays quiet). A repo with no marker, or whose last marker is a fresh outcome, gets the plain stall line.
- A parsed `eta` is capped at 24 hours, so a made-up eta cannot hide a dead run for ever, and an `at=` more than 5 minutes ahead of the clock is not trusted: the status creation time is used instead (the marker is skipped when there is none), so a future stamp cannot mute the alarms.
- `gh pr list --json statusCheckRollup` exports a status's context, state and start time but not its description (checked on gh 2.99), and the stage, run id and time live in the description. So when that list shows a train marker, one extra `gh api graphql` call reads the markers of the open PRs into the default branch; with no marker listed there is no extra call, a failed or unreadable reply reads as no markers (silent), and the call shares the 15-minute throttle. The tests exercise it through a fake `gh`; it has not yet been run against a live repository.
- Decision effect: `landing_watchdog.py expect 'train_size>=N' [--hours H]` records a decision in `<git-common-dir>/perun-decisions.jsonl` (env `PERUN_DECISIONS` overrides; N and H are whole numbers >= 1, H defaults to 24, anything else exits 2 with usage). The first argument is quoted everywhere it is shown, because an unquoted `>=` is a shell redirect: bash runs the command without it and leaves a stray file named `=N`. While the newest unexpired decision is unmet, that is, at least two trains that began after it carried a median of fewer than N PRs, the hook adds "Decision not in effect: train_size>=N set X h ago; the K trains since carried a median of M PRs. Check that the runner reads it." A met or expired decision, fewer than two trains since, a ledger record without a time, and a missing or unreadable file are silent, so a decision the runner never applied no longer reads as a slow train.
- `train_yield.py record` takes an optional last argument, the epoch second the train began, and stamps each ledger line with `"start"` as well as `"at"` (the time the line was written, at the end of the train). `train_land.sh` takes the start epoch once, next to its elapsed-time clock, and passes it from its exit trap. The new `sizes_since(path, at)` returns the PR counts of the trains that began at or after a time, falling back to `"at"` for a record with no start, so a train that began before a decision and ended after it is not judged against it. A record written before the stamps never counts as after a decision, and the existing readers (`report`, `solo`, the yield alarm) ignore the new keys.
- Known limits, stated in the script's docstring: markers come only from the current heads of open PRs, so a re-push or a close in the middle of a run drops one; the creation-time fallback is the post time, not the run start; any landing supersedes a live marker, so a hand merge, or a landing stage that hangs after its first merge, silences the stuck line (the stall line still fires once nothing merges for the window); `train_size` reads the local ledger only, so trains run on another host are not seen.
- `fanout-host-sizing.md` shows one example each of the stuck line, the stall line with its idle clause, and the decision line, next to the yield and merge-rate alarms.

### Changed
- Tests: `scripts/test_landing_watchdog.py` covers a pending train marker beside a passing check run (green) and another pending status (not green), the marker parser (eta cap, future stamp, missing creation time), the one-call marker fetch and its fail-open paths, the newest-commit time in the probe, stuck at 1.5 times the expected time plus and minus a minute (with an eta and with the default), supersession by a newer marker of another run and by a landing, a healthy repo with an old skipped marker, the idle clause and where it does not appear, tuples from older callers, the `expect` parser, its quoted form run through a shell, and an unmet, met, one-train, expired, untimed and started-before-the-decision case, through the hook and the CLI. `scripts/test_train_yield.py` covers the `"start"` and `"at"` stamps and `sizes_since`, and `scripts/test-train-solo-port.sh` covers the start stamp and a solo landing beside a failure or pending marker (a marker alone stays not green).

## [1.635.0] — 2026-11-01

### Fixed
- The stop-starting hook in `.claude/skills/agentic-delivery/scripts/flow_alarm.py` denied any Bash command whose raw text matched `gh pr create`, so at the cap a `grep`, an `echo`, a commit message or an issue body that only named the command was blocked, while a quoted or escaped form such as `gh pr "create"` or `g\h pr create` was not matched at all. A command now counts as naming it when its text, in any case and also read with quotes and backslashes removed and backslash-newline joined, contains `gh pr create`, wherever it sits (in code, in a comment or in a heredoc body). A command that names it is denied (exit 2 at the cap) unless every command in it is a known text tool (echo, printf, cat, grep, rg, head, tail, git and similar, and `gh` outside `pr create`, `pr new` and `api`). A failed `gh`, a timeout and unparseable hook JSON still allow, and `# priority: <reason>` still overrides.
- Every step that drops text before parsing now keeps the text when the input is ambiguous (keep means deny). A `#` is dropped as a comment, and a heredoc body as data, only when the text before it is provably shell code: no open quote, `$'..'`, `${..}`, `$[..]`, `((..))`, backtick or earlier comment, and the one open quote accepted is the `"$(` of a heredoc commit message. A backslash-newline is joined only where a shell joins it, not at the end of a comment. A heredoc needs one plain or fully quoted delimiter word without a backslash, and a delimiter line; a command with no delimiter line is denied, and so is one whose body holds `$(` or a backtick under an unquoted delimiter, whose operator line opens a `(`, a backtick or a quote after the marker (the shell reads it across the body lines), or whose body or operator line holds `)` inside a `$(` (an older shell can end the substitution there). A heredoc beside a comment is not stripped at all: the command is read again with every body in place, so each body line and its delimiter line must pass as commands (a `#` inside a body is data and does not count as the comment).
- A command that holds the text may use `git` only for the log, show, diff, grep, status, blame, commit and add subcommands, in every `git` segment of it, so `git rebase --exec`, `git bisect run`, `git submodule foreach`, `git apply` (a patch can write a config that a later `git` runs), `-c alias.*`, `git grep -O` (also bundled, as in `-nOcmd`), `--output` (it writes a file), `-p`, `--config-env` and any option before the subcommand other than `-C DIR` deny, and so does a `git` word that holds `$` or `{` (an expansion can build an option: `o=--output=gc` then `git log ... $o` writes a config that a later `git status` runs), except the message after `commit -m` or `-am`. These rules, and the file-write rule below, read the whole command, so a mention that sits only in a comment or a heredoc body counts as the text: `git rebase --exec '...' # gh pr create` is denied.
- `gh` is a text tool only outside `pr create`: a `pr` followed anywhere by `create`, its alias `new` or an expansion (`gh pr -R o/r create`, `gh pr --repo=o/r create`, `gh pr new --fill`, `gh -R o/r pr new`), and `gh` with an `api` word (it can open a pull request), an `alias`, `config` or `extension` word, or a `$`, `*`, `?`, `[` or `{` among its first two words, deny. So do `rg --pre` and `rg --hostname-bin`, a `gh` word that spells `create` through an expansion (`create$x`, `create{,}`, `create*`), an unquoted backtick and `$'..'` quoting. The command word must be a listed name exactly, so `./echo` and `/bin/echo` are other programs and deny.
- A variable set before a command passes only when its name is inert: `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`, `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`, `GIT_AUTHOR_DATE`, `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME`, `GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL`, `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE`, `LANG`, `LC_*`, `TZ` and `NO_COLOR`. Any other name, such as `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF`, `GIT_EDITOR`, `GIT_CONFIG_*` or `PAGER`, is denied, bare or before a command, because an editor, a pager, a config entry or an external diff makes a tool run its value. `printf -v` (any `printf` whose first word is an option or expands) and an expansion that assigns (`${NAME:=..}`) deny for the same reason.
- Operators are read one at a time, so a redirect that follows a newline or `;` skips its own target and no longer hands the next word to the allowlist as a command. A command that names the text and writes a file (an output redirect to anything but `/dev/null` or a file descriptor, including `| cat > file`) is denied, and so is a file written beside a heredoc body that holds the text. `tee` and `uniq` are not on the allowlist.
- Still passing, and named in the hook docstring: `$(which gh) pr create`, `${GH} pr create`, `gh${IFS}pr create`, `gh $'pr' create` and `gh pr cre{a,}te` (the text is not in the command), a script written by an editor tool and run later, a `gh` alias or extension that is already installed (it runs under its own name), and another allowed tool's own exec flag that the hook does not list. Over-denied, the safe direction: a `#` that cannot be proven to start a comment (for example a quoted `#` before a heredoc), a single-quoted backtick or `$(`, a `(`, backtick or open quote after a heredoc marker, a backslash in a delimiter word, a `)` in a heredoc body inside `$(`, a `gh` word with `$`, `*`, `?`, `[` or `{` among its first two (its own `{owner}` placeholder), a mention-only pipeline through a command outside the allowlist, a non-read `git` subcommand such as `push` beside a mention (also one only in a comment), a heredoc written to a file beside a mention, a comment beside a heredoc, an assignment of a variable that is not inert, `printf -v`, `${x:=..}`, a `$` or `{` in a `git` word other than a `commit -m` message (`git log "$base"..HEAD`, `git -C "$dir" log`), and a command word that is a path. This is a flow alarm, not a security boundary.

### Changed
- Tests: `python3 scripts/test_flow_alarm.py` goes from 10 to 22 tests. The new `Gate` class checks 35 commands that only name the command (exit 0 at the cap), 48 shapes that run it and that the old substring test denied on the raw text (exit 2), 125 deny probes (exit 2) that run it, write it where a later command runs it, hide it from a step that drops text before parsing, or spell it in another case, and 26 commands that only name it and are denied anyway (the safe direction). Further tests pin the git subcommand rule, the inert-variable rule, the file-write rule, the residuals above that still pass (5 shapes) and the unparseable-text case.

### Added
- `reaper_lint.py` gains the rule `LINUX_ONLY_NO_PREFLIGHT`: a command line whose command word is `setsid`, `flock` or `timeout` with at least one argument (the first word after shell keywords, `sudo`, `nohup`, `env`, `time`, `nice`, `exec`, `xargs`, `command`, `stdbuf`, `ionice`, `chrt`, `taskset`, `NAME=value` and a Makefile recipe's leading `@`, `-` or `+`), or that has a bare `/proc/<path>` word or redirect source, fires when the file has no platform preflight. A stock macOS install has none of those tools and no procfs, so a gate that calls one exits 127 or reads nothing there and posts FAIL for a check that never ran. A preflight anywhere in the file clears the line: `command -v`, `type`, `hash` or `which` naming that tool; any `uname`; `$OSTYPE` or `${OSTYPE`; a `-e`, `-d`, `-r`, `-f`, `-s` or `-x` test on a path (a `/proc` path clears `/proc`, a path to the tool clears the tool); the tool run as its own probe (`--version` or `--help` as its only argument, or `true` or `:` as its whole payload, as in `timeout 1 true`). Only commands are read: heredoc bodies, multi-line quoted strings, `package.json` text outside `scripts`, text after a `$(...)` inside double quotes, arithmetic, Makefile and justfile assignments, and `/proc` as a `find` operand, a `grep`, `sed` or `awk` pattern, or a word `echo` or `printf` prints do not fire. YAML files, hook configs included, are skipped (a CI step runs on its runner's OS) and the usual `# reaper-lint: allow <reason>` marker suppresses a line. The docstring names the residuals, among them `sh -c` strings, `find -exec` tails, option-argument wrappers such as `nice -n 10`, a preflight in a sourced file or a wrapper function, and preflight clearing that is file-wide and blind to mentions.
- `lang-shell.md` gains one bullet, "A gate that calls a Linux-only tool turns red on macOS for a check that never ran", after the `env` bullet; it ends by routing to the rule.

### Changed
- A repo that opted in to the gate (`DCR_REAPER_LINT=1`) and has an unguarded Linux-only call goes red on upgrade, until it adds a preflight or a `# reaper-lint: allow <reason>` marker.
- Tests: `python3 .claude/skills/deep-code-review/scripts/reaper_lint.py --selftest` (already run by CI) goes from 90 to 185 cases: each Linux-only tool and `/proc` shape that fires, each preflight form that clears it (a tool self-probe included), the command-word handling (wrappers, `NAME=value`, a Makefile recipe's `@`, `-` and `+`, a `for` word list, a `grep` argument, a quote split at `$(`), and each non-command the rule leaves quiet (heredoc and multi-line string bodies, JSON prose, text after a quoted `$(...)`, arithmetic, Makefile and justfile assignments, `/proc` as a pattern, `find` operand or printed word). Every earlier case keeps its result.

size-budget-raise: .claude/skills/deep-code-review/references/lang-shell.md 9249→9885 one bullet on a gate that calls a Linux-only tool

### Fixed
- Nothing bounded a test's run time, so a test that never returned spun a core until someone killed it, and parallel runs stacked up. `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` now runs each test under a wall-clock bound, `PERUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_S` seconds (default 900; a missing, non-numeric or non-positive value, or one longer than 9 digits, means 900). A test that outlives it is killed and fails like any other failing test, printing `run-ci-tests: FAIL <test> (timed out after <secs>s)`. The alarm kills the test's own process, not child processes it started, so a caller that pipes the runner's output waits for those; a test that arms its own alarm replaces the runner's.
- `scripts/test_security_gates_corpus.py` now bounds each guard check to 5 seconds, and so do the in-process Python blocks of `scripts/test-destructive-guard.sh`. A check that never returns (catastrophic regex backtracking, say) is a `FAIL` line naming the case or block instead of a hang: the corpus test moves on to the next case, and a destructive-guard block skips the rest of its checks. The destructive-guard test's selftest and hook calls are bounded by the runner only. The privacy-gate call in the Python test has a 120 second timeout, and a timeout is a `FAIL` line, not a traceback (the gate's own child processes are not stopped). Every existing case keeps its result.

### Changed
- Tests: `scripts/test_security_gates_corpus.py` checks its own bound against a catastrophic regex, and the new `scripts/ci-tests.d/run-ci-tests-timeout.sh` covers the runner bound: a test that sleeps far past `PERUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_S=2` fails promptly with the timed-out line and its own process is gone, and a bad value falls back to 900.

### Changed
- The commit-tier gate row in agentic-delivery's `references/roles.md` now asks for a `Tests: X/X` count only when a suite printed it on the staged tree. When the suites run later, in a merge train or in CI, the line reads `Tests: none (<where they run>)`: a count copied from an older tree, another branch or the suite's size is an over-claim. The hand-back check (`handback.py`) reads such a line, a `Tests: none (<place>)` with a non-empty parenthetical, as a stated no-run, so that one line is enough; a bare `Tests: none` still fails, and digits inside the parenthetical are no count. A new eval, `tests-line-only-from-a-run`, pins the rule.

## [1.634.0] — 2026-11-01

### Fixed
- `lane_resume_nudge.py` no longer tells the coordinator to resume a lane that went idle long ago. It compared a new lane's description with every subagent meta file in the session, however old, so in a session that ran for days it could name a lane whose last activity was days earlier. It now skips a lane whose last activity is older than `LANE_RESUME_MAX_AGE_H` hours (default 6; a missing, non-numeric or non-positive value means 6). Last activity is the mtime of the lane's `agent-<id>.jsonl` beside its meta file when that exists, else the meta file's own mtime; a lane whose mtime cannot be read is skipped. The nudge stays advisory only and still fails open.

### Changed
- Tests: `python3 .claude/skills/agentic-delivery/scripts/lane_resume_nudge.py --selftest` (already run by CI) goes from 6 to 11 cases. The new cases pin a 7 h old jsonl as silent even when the meta file is fresh, a 5 h old jsonl as advising even when the meta file is old, a lane with no jsonl and a 7 h old meta file as silent, the env var both narrowing and widening the window, and a non-numeric, `nan`, zero, negative or empty value acting as 6.

## [1.633.0] — 2026-10-31

### Fixed
- A handback that says the lane is waiting on its background tests now blocks the stop (exit 2) in every mode but `off`, including the default `warn`, instead of only adding a `systemMessage` and letting the lane end with its work unverified. The reason on stderr tells the lane to wait in this turn (a local process: `lane_guard.py wait --pid <pid> --timeout <s>`) and hand back the result, or to hand back `status=UNVERIFIED` naming what is still pending (for example a remote check). The text is a claim, not evidence, so the block is bounded: it does not fire when the hook input has no `agent_id` (the counter has nothing to key on, so the note stays), when it has `stop_hook_active` true, or when the first status line of the handback reads UNVERIFIED (so the way out above cannot loop; a later `UNVERIFIED:` line or `- unverified:` field does not exempt a handback whose first status line is VERIFIED); otherwise it fires at most `MAX_BLOCKS` (3) times per agent id, counted in a `.wait` file beside the lane's other state files, and a state file that cannot be written means no block. Where no block applies the `systemMessage` stays and the stop goes through. The push, commit, background and dirty-worktree holds still run first and win. The `background_guard` policy text, the `handback_cap.py` docstring and the lane preamble now say so.

### Changed
- Tests: `python3 .claude/skills/agentic-delivery/scripts/handback_cap.py --selftest` (already run by CI) goes from 117 to 130 cases. Two of the new cases pin the first-status-line rule: a wait claim after a VERIFIED first status line is still blocked when a later line reads `UNVERIFIED: ...` or `- unverified: ...`. The rest pin the block text, the bound, the no-`agent_id`, `stop_hook_active`, UNVERIFIED-first, mode `off` and verified-handback paths. `scripts/test_bg_wait_claim.py` now runs its flag cases with `stop_hook_active` true, the bound past which a waiting claim is only flagged.

### Added
- Three bundled semgrep rules in `.claude/skills/deep-code-review/templates/semgrep-taint/js.yml` for defect classes the taint rules leave unflagged. Each carries the same test-path exclusions as `hardcoded-credential-compare`.
- `perun.js.fetch-no-timeout` (INFO): `fetch(url)` or `fetch(url, {...})` with no `signal` key inside a Next.js route handler (`export async function GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE`), a pages API `export default async function handler`, or an `app.get|post|put|patch|delete|all("/path", ..., fn)` callback. Any `signal:` value, an options spread, a fetch outside a handler and a `cache.get("key", fn)` callback stay clean. Ceiling: handlers are matched by shape, so a const-arrow export or a handler passed by name is not seen.
- `perun.js.auth-cookie-flags` (WARNING): a cookie whose literal name has session, sess, sessid, sessionid, phpsessid, sid, token, auth, authtoken or jwt as a whole word (split at punctuation and camelCase boundaries, so `authToken`, `connect.sid` and `next-auth.session-token` match and `authorized`, `tokenizer_mode` and `assessment` do not; names holding csrf or xsrf are skipped), set positionally or as one options object through `<x>.cookie`, `<x>.setCookie`, `cookies().set`, `(await cookies()).set`, a variable bound by `X = await cookies()` or `X = cookies()` in an enclosing block (`const jar = await cookies(); jar.set(...)`) or `<x>.cookies.set` on any receiver not named below, with `httpOnly` missing or the literal `false`, or `secure` missing or the literal `false`. `ctx.cookies.set`, `context.cookies.set`, `event.cookies.set`, `this.cookies.set` and a bare `cookies.set` are reported only for a literal `httpOnly: false` or `secure: false`: the cookies library behind Koa's `ctx.cookies` documents `httpOnly` as true by default and `secure` as true by default over HTTPS, and SvelteKit documents both as true by default (`secure` false in development). Any other `httpOnly` or `secure` value passes, and a clear (an empty value, `maxAge: 0` or `expires: new Date(0)`) and a `req.cookies.set` or `request.cookies.set` call are skipped. Ceiling: options must be an object literal, and a bare `cookies.set` also covers other frameworks whose defaults were not checked, so their missing flags are not reported.
- `perun.js.cors-credentials-any-origin` (WARNING): `cors({...})` or `register(cors, {...})` with `credentials: true` and `origin: true`, `origin: /.*/` or a callback that always allows (`cb(null, true)`, `cb(null, origin)` or `cb(null, !!origin)`), or a function that copies `req.get|header("origin")` or `headers.get("origin")` (directly or through a variable) into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` while it sets `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` to `"true"` or `true`, unless an `if` on a `.has`, `.includes` or `.test` call encloses or precedes the set call. A literal `origin: "*"` is not reported, because the cors packages send a literal `*` and browsers refuse it on credentialed requests. The `req.headers.origin` handler shape is left to the default pack's express `cors-misconfiguration` rule, which already flags it. Ceiling: any such `if` counts as an allowlist check whatever it tests.
- Test: `scripts/test_semgrep_js_gaps.py`, registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/semgrep-js-gaps.sh`, runs annotated fictional fixtures (a `ruleid` or `ok` comment marks the next line) through semgrep with the bundled rules only, plus copies under test paths that must stay clean. Offline checks of severity, exclusions and the key regexes run where semgrep is absent.

## [1.632.0] — 2026-10-31

### Fixed
- `handback_cap.py`'s background-work block text no longer says "You own it until it exits". The scan matches any test or build whose cwd is in the lane's worktree, and that process may have been started by someone else working in the same worktree. The text now says what the lane can do (wait for the pid with `lane_guard.py wait --pid <pid> --timeout <s>`, or stop it if this lane started it) and that the hold ends on its own after `HANDBACK_PUSH_MAX_S` (30 minutes by default) at most, as the push and commit hold text already did.
- A hold's window now restarts once its condition is gone. `_hold` keeps the first block's time as the mtime of the lane's `.push`, `.bg` or `.dirty` state file and nothing removed that file, so after one block that was more than 30 minutes old, a later push or commit, background run or dirty tree in the same lane was released at once instead of being held for a fresh window. `check()` now removes the lane's state file (new `_release`, which ignores `OSError`) for each hold whose check found no such condition, so the next block opens a fresh `HANDBACK_PUSH_MAX_S` window. `check()` also no longer returns at the first hold that blocks: the push or commit, background and dirty-worktree checks are all evaluated before it returns 2, so the reset also happens while a higher hold blocks (for example: a dirty-worktree hold opened more than 30 minutes ago, the tree cleaned while a commit is still running, the commit ending, the tree dirtied again, and the lane is held again for a fresh window). The first hold that blocks still wins in the same order (push or commit, background, dirty) with the same text, a lower hold is still never started on a call where a higher one blocks, and a blind lower check now prints its `COULD_NOT_CHECK` line before that hold's text. A check that could not run (`COULD_NOT_CHECK`) keeps the hold, and a condition that stays live past the window is still released, so a stuck process cannot trap the lane. The dirty-worktree hold goes through the same `_hold` and gets the same reset.

### Changed
- The `_push_running` docstring and the comment above `PUSH_RE` now state a known limit: `ps` prints argv without quoting, so a space inside a `-c` value or a `-C` path splits it (`git -c user.name=Jane Smith commit`, `git -C /acme/my repo commit`), `PUSH_RE` does not match, and that push or commit is not held (the check fails open and does not print `COULD_NOT_CHECK`). The behaviour is unchanged; it is now documented and pinned.
- Test: `python3 .claude/skills/agentic-delivery/scripts/handback_cap.py --selftest` (already run by CI) goes from 83 to 117 cases. Ten of the new ones fail on the previous code (107 of 117 passed there): each of the push, background and dirty-worktree holds starting a fresh window when the condition clears and returns (old first block, condition gone, condition back, held again); the background and dirty holds doing the same when a higher hold blocks while their own condition is gone, including their state file being removed; and the background hold text naming the way out rather than ownership. The other twenty-four pin behaviour that already held: the first block and the release after the window for each of the three holds, a condition that clears and passes, a hold whose scan could not run keeping its state file, a lower hold opening its first block, the first hold that blocks winning (push or commit, then background, then dirty) with no lower hold started, `_skip_pids` skipping the hook's ancestors and descendants (a synthetic process table, hook then child then a grandchild `git commit`) while an unrelated `git commit` pid is still counted, the same through `_push_running`, and three `known-limit-*` cases (a `-c` value with a space and a `-C` path with a space are not held, a `-c` value without one is). Each of the three keep-on-`None` cases fails when its scan's `None` is treated as empty (`if not running`, `elif not bg`, `elif not dirty`).

### Changed
- The privacy gate (`scripts/ci-gates.sh privacy`) now runs one prefilter pass before its per-pattern scan: a single `grep -IlE -D skip -f` over every banlist pattern at once, in the same 1000-file batches, lists the only files any pattern can match, and the existing per-pattern greps read just those files. A clean tree is therefore read once instead of once per pattern, which shortens the gate on large trees. The hit set is unchanged: hits are still attributed per pattern with the content withheld, the empty-input ERE probe still runs first so the pattern list holds only valid patterns, the `secret_scan.py` pass is untouched, and a prefilter grep error fails closed (it never reads as "no candidates"). The candidate list is newline-delimited, so a tree holding a path with a newline in its name skips the prefilter and falls back to the full per-pattern scan, which keeps the hit set unchanged there too. The new `scripts/test-privacy-prefilter.sh` pins the unchanged hit set against an independent one-grep-per-pattern oracle, the one-pass cost on a clean tree, that the per-pattern greps see only listed files, both fail-closed paths (an invalid ERE and a prefilter error), and that a hit in a file whose name holds a newline still blocks.

### Changed
- When semgrep reports errors on some of the files it scanned, the `review_checks.sh` tool hub now names those files instead of only saying the scan was partial. Each file with an error is a `not-checked` row (its path, line 0, and the error type and level), at most 20 per 200-file semgrep call, followed by one row with the path `.` that counts the rest and names the first path left out, so two calls with equal error counts keep one such row each instead of the closing dedup of identical `not-checked` rows merging them into one. An error that carries no path stays counted and gets no row. The `review_checks: partial: semgrep ran but reported errors (...)` line on stderr keeps its text and now ends with the error counts, for example `(3 error(s) on 2 of 40 scanned file(s): PartialParsing (warn) x2, Syntax error (error) x1; see not-checked rows)`. The type is semgrep's `type` string, or the first element when it is a list. A warn-level parse error still makes the scan partial and is never read as clean. Whether a scan is partial or not run is decided on the findings alone, before these rows are added, so the "not run" cases (errors on every scanned file, or an error with no path and no findings) are unchanged and name no file. The header comment of `review_checks.sh` now matches.
- The closing summary on stderr no longer counts `not-checked` rows as findings: `review_checks: N findings; ...` counts every other row, and a separate line, `review_checks: K not-checked row(s) (surface a tool did not cover, not findings)`, gives the number of `not-checked` rows and appears only when there are any. The line that reports how many rows are on lines the diff adds still counts every row.
- Test: `scripts/test-review-checks-semgrep-partial.sh` (registered as `scripts/ci-tests.d/review-checks-semgrep-partial.sh`) runs the hub against a stub semgrep that answers each call with its own fictional JSON. It covers a warn-level `PartialParsing` on 1 of 3 files (one row for that path, the counts on the partial line, the finding row unchanged), 25 errored files (20 rows plus the summary row, counts ordered by count), two semgrep calls (200 and 30 files) with equal error counts (two summary rows and two partial lines), the findings count and the separate `not-checked` line, several errors on one file, errors with no path, the "not run" cases, and odd error shapes (a null or string entry, a missing type or level, a path that is not a string, a control character in a path) that must not void the chunk's findings.

## [1.631.0] — 2026-10-31

### Fixed
- `handback_cap.py` now holds a lane's hand-back while a `git commit` from its worktree is still running, not only a `git push`. A background commit with a slow pre-commit hook was not held, so a lane could hand back before its commit existed. The process match is `git [-c k=v] [-C dir] [--opt] push|commit` on a process whose argv[0] is `git`, alone or behind `env VAR=...` or `perl -e 'alarm 30; exec @ARGV'`, so a wrapped `perl -e 'alarm 30; exec @ARGV' git commit -m x` counts while a `claude -p` lane brief, a shell string or a `grep` that only names `git commit` does not, and both words now end with `(?![\w-])`: `git commit-tree`, `git commit-graph`, `git push-x` and `git log --grep commit` do not match (the old `push\b` ending did match `push-x`). The block text reads "A git push or commit from this worktree is still running (its pre-push or pre-commit hook may take 15+ minutes)" and no longer says the lane owns the process (it may belong to another process in the same checkout), read-only agent types (review, investigat, audit, explore) are never held for a live push or commit, the hold still ends after 30 minutes (`HANDBACK_PUSH_MAX_S`), and an unreadable process table still prints `COULD_NOT_CHECK` and passes. The `BACKGROUND WORK` docstring and the `templates/lane-preamble.md` line that describes the rule say push or commit too.
- `handback_cap.py`'s live push or commit check no longer counts its own ancestors. It read `ps -axo pid=,command=` and skipped only its own pid, so a headless `claude -p "<brief that mentions git commit>"` host (the brief is in its argv, its cwd is the lane worktree) looked like a live commit and held every hand-back until the 30-minute cap. It now reads `pid=,ppid=,command=` through `_ps_table` and skips the hook, its ancestors and its descendants with the same `_skip_pids` helper the background-work scan uses; a `git commit` that is not an ancestor still holds. A process table that parses to no rows now prints `COULD_NOT_CHECK` and passes, as an unreadable one does.
- Test: `python3 .claude/skills/agentic-delivery/scripts/handback_cap.py --selftest` (already run by CI) gains cases for a plain `git commit`, `git -C <dir> commit`, a wrapped commit (quoted and as `ps` prints it), a live commit held for its own worktree but not for the checkout that contains it, and no match for `commit-tree`, `commit-graph`, `push-x` and `git log --grep commit`. Five of them (the positive commit cases and `push-x`) fail on the previous regex, so 64 of 69 passed; all 69 pass now. The `ps` mock now emits the `pid ppid command` rows the check reads, and four more cases cover a parent and a grandparent whose argv holds `git commit` (not counted, even with its cwd in the worktree), an unrelated `git commit` (still counted) and a process table that parses to no rows (`COULD_NOT_CHECK`, not a pass as `False`); the two ancestor cases and the empty-table case fail on the previous check, so 70 of 73 passed. Ten more cases cover the argv[0] match (a sibling `claude -p` brief, a `zsh -c` string and a `grep` that name `git commit` are not held; plain, `env`-wrapped, perl-wrapped and path-qualified `git commit` and `git push` are), read-only agent types (not held) and the hold text (no ownership claim); six of them fail on the check before them, so 77 of 83 passed; all 83 pass now.

### Added
- `merge-queue-worktrees.md` gains the section "Around the heavy slot: cheap checks before the wait, a settled base after the grant" next to "A heavy slot guards the contended stage, not the whole train", which is unchanged. Three rules: run the cheap, fast-failing preconditions (mergeability, receipts present, base fresh, lint) before queueing for a heavy slot; compose the tested union after the grant, once the previous holder's landing has settled (landed or abandoned) and with a wait bounded to one landing; end the stage early when the base moves on a path the union touches (this decides only when to abort, and landing still needs the proven base). The slot stays scoped to the contended stage, widened only by that wait and the compose. A closing paragraph says what the shipped scripts do (`train_land.sh` waits out a landing train's push lock once, at train start; `land_train.sh` only warns on a moved base for a non-split train) and what is doctrine only (recompose after the grant, a mid-stage head compare).
- `pipeline-optimizer.md` gains two bullets under "Gate cost, feeder order and ready-PR age": a rerun of only the failing tests merges into the original run's receipt (full count, each failure replaced by its rerun result, both runs' raw count strings kept beside it, same tree only) and never replaces it, because a smaller receipt makes the next full-count gate force a second full run; and a pre-merge check pool at 0 workers fails silently, so alarm on worker count 0 while ready work waits (no shipped script reads a pool's worker count, and `landing_watchdog.py` is the natural home).
- Test: five eval cases in `.claude/skills/agentic-delivery/evals/evals.json` covering the five rules: `rerun-receipt-merged-not-replaced` and `rerun-receipt-after-fix-commit-needs-full-run` (the rerun rule, on the same tree and on a different tree), `stale-union-built-before-previous-landing-settled` (compose after the grant, with the early end as one expectation), `zero-worker-check-pool-alarm` and `cheap-preconditions-before-heavy-slot`. The rules are doctrine plus evals, not new scripts: a moved base only draws a WARN at land time for non-split trains, and nothing checks it mid-stage.

### Added
- `route_auth_map.py` reads TypeScript type-argument route registrations (`app.post<{ Params: { id: string }; Body: Widget }>("/path/:id", h)`, also on `.all`, `.use` and `.addHook`) through a bounded balanced `<...>` scan: the angle brackets must balance within 2000 characters, no `;`, `&&` or `||` may stand outside brackets, and a `(` must follow. A file whose only registrations are typed is now scanned, and a comparison such as `x.get < y && f(z)` is not a route.
- A Fastify root hook now reads `auth=root-hook`. `x.addHook("onRequest"|"preHandler"|"preValidation"|"preParsing", fn)` on a receiver bound to a `Fastify(...)` call, at any depth (a factory function included), counts when `fn` (inline, or through the same-file declarations it names) can answer 401/403 or names an identity check; `onSend`, `onRoute` and `onListen` never count. It covers what the hook file wires onto that receiver after the hook, in source order and within the block that holds the hook: the routes of a scanned file it passes to `x.register(plugin, opts)` or calls as `fn(x, ...)` with the instance as the first argument (`fn` imported from that file by a relative path), and the non-GET routes declared on that receiver in the hook's own file. A route above the hook, a module that is imported but never registered or called, a call with another instance, and a routes file with any wiring site the hook does not cover stay HIGH.
- What a root hook covers is read from the `if` statements of the hook text up to and including its first refusal. A negated path test with a bare `return` (`if (!req.url.startsWith("/acme-api/")) return;`, also `req.routeOptions.url?.startsWith(...)`) is a scope: only routes under it are covered. A positive path test with a bare `return`, written in the condition or through a same-file declaration it names (`PUBLIC_PATHS.includes(url)`), is an allow-list entry: a route under it keeps its own evidence. A path in the condition of a refusing `if` is a scope, and a `!` before it covers nothing. A quoted path anywhere else (a role table the hook reads, a path test after the refusal) says nothing, and a route-registration literal never counts.
- A root hook's path literals are read by the operator that tests them. A `startsWith` allow-list entry lets through every route whose raw path starts with it, as JavaScript does (`if (req.url.startsWith("/acme-api/health")) return;` also lets `/acme-api/healthz` through, so that route stays HIGH); `===` and `==` against a plain name or member chain (`req.url`) name that path only, whether they allow-list it or scope it (`if (req.url === "/acme-api/admin") return reply.code(403).send();` covers `/acme-api/admin` and not `/acme-api/admin/users`); any other test (`includes`, a collection, a regex, `!==`, or `===`/`==` against a call or an index such as `req.url.slice(0, 15)` or `path.dirname(req.url)`) allow-lists by raw prefix and scopes by the exact path. Known limit: a string `includes` or `endsWith` allow-list entry also lets through a route that only contains or ends with its literal (`/acme-api/health` next to an `endsWith("/health")` entry), and that route can still read covered. A `startsWith` scope still covers the routes under it, by path segment.
- A bare return before the first refusal under a condition that is neither a path test nor an identity check (an identity call, or a comparison with a secret-looking value) is a bypass, and the hook then covers nothing; `done()` and `next()` count as bare returns. Conditions are not evaluated, so a bypass OR-ed with a path test still reads as the path test; the script docstring lists the other limits.
- The refusal test that makes a Next middleware or a Fastify hook count as a gate also reads `.code(401|403)`, `statusCode = 401|403`, `.unauthorized(` and `.forbidden(`.

### Fixed
- `tenant_scope_check.py` no longer crashes with `IndexError` on a file whose last character is a backslash inside an open string; `route_auth_map.py` reads files through the same masker.

### Changed
- The `review_checks.sh` tool hub now also hands zizmor the Dependabot config (`.github/dependabot.yml` or `.yaml`) and GitHub Actions action manifests (`action.yml` or `action.yaml`, in any directory the hub does not exclude: `node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, ...), not only workflow files, so findings such as `dependabot-cooldown` in a Dependabot config and `template-injection` or `unpinned-uses` in a composite action reach the report instead of never being scanned. Routing is by file name: other YAML such as `config/app.yml` still goes nowhere, and actionlint still reads workflow files only. A changed `action.yml` that is not a GitHub Actions manifest and is the only file zizmor is given makes it collect no input; the run reports that as `NOT RUN: zizmor (exit 3)` with a not-checked row, never as clean. The zizmor row of `references/tool-hub.md` says the same.
- The scanner JSON reader now starts at the first line that begins with `[` or `{`, not at the first bracket anywhere in the output. zizmor logs each path it audits (`INFO audit: zizmor: completed ./x/[]/action.yml`) before its JSON, and the hub merges that log into the file the reader parses, so a bracket in a changed path could hide findings: `pkgs/[id]/action.yml`, `x/{}/action.yml` or a workflow named `[id].yml` made the whole batch unparseable (not run), and `x/[]/action.yml` read as an empty list, so zizmor counted as run with no findings. Those paths now yield their findings.
- Test: `scripts/test-review-checks-zizmor-routes.sh` (registered as `scripts/ci-tests.d/review-checks-zizmor-routes.sh`) runs the hub with a zizmor shim on a hermetic PATH that logs each audited path to stderr before its JSON, as zizmor does. It checks that the Dependabot config (`.yml` and `.yaml`), a nested `.github/actions/setup/action.yml`, a root `action.yaml` and manifests under `x/[]/` and `x/[id]/` are each handed to zizmor and yield a row on that file, and that the files zizmor receives are exactly the workflows (`.yml` and `.yaml`) plus those, so a nested workflow, `sub/.github/dependabot.yml`, `docs/dependabot.yml`, `config/app.yml`, `config/reaction.yml` and `docs/action.yml.md` are not routed. Every case fails on the previous script.
