### Added
- Committed personal-data check. New built-in `committed_personal_data.py` (stdlib only) counts the distinct email-shaped strings in every tracked file, plain binary data (sqlite, pickles) included, and reports a file with 10 or more as one `email-addresses` row: path and count only, never an address, a domain or a line. gitleaks, trufflehog and semgrep look for secrets, so a committed export of real people's addresses passed all of them clean. Not counted: the reserved example and test names (example.com, .net and .org with their subdomains, `.test`, `.example`, `.invalid`, `.localhost`), noreply forms, the ssh account `git@` of git remotes (`git@host:org/repo.git`, `ssh://git@host/org/repo`) and image asset-scale names (`icon@2x.png`, `icon@1.5x.png`, `icon@2x-dark.png`, for png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, avif, svg, pdf, ico, bmp, tif, tiff, heic, heif and apng). `--include-reserved` counts them so tests can use fictional example.com fixtures. Flags: `--threshold N` and `--repo-threshold N` (each 1 to 100000), `--strict` (exit 1 when a file or the repository total is flagged; the default is advisory, exit 0), `--stdin` (scan the listed paths instead of every tracked file), `--max-bytes N` (1 to 1 GiB, default 32 MiB; a larger file is scanned over its first bytes and a not-checked row says so). It exits 2 when `git ls-files` fails or a flag is out of range, never a silent pass and never a traceback.
- Addresses spread thin are summed. A leak of one address per file never reaches the per-file threshold, so the distinct addresses of all the scanned files that stay below it are also counted together, and a total of 50 or more (`--repo-threshold`) gives one `email-addresses` row with the path `.` ("69 distinct email addresses across 75 file(s) ..."). A file already reported is left out of the total, an address repeated across files counts once, and in diff mode only the changed files are counted. `--threshold 1` lists the files behind the row. The default 50 is five times the file threshold. The audit behind this check found about 850 addresses; this repository holds 69 distinct ones in 75 files that each stay below 10 (60 of them under docs/bench), so its own `--full` run shows the row as a lead. A default of 100 would stay quiet here but would miss a spread of 50 to 99 addresses.
- Compressed and columnar files do not pass silently, for exactly these formats. A file that stays under the threshold gets a `not-checked` row (path and format, never a value) when it is parquet (`PAR1` at the start and the end, or `PARE` at both for an encrypted footer), an Arrow IPC file (`ARROW1` at both ends), ORC (`ORC` at the start and before the last byte), zip (also docx, xlsx, jar), gzip, zstd, xz, 7z, lz4 frame, bzip2, Avro, PDF, or a zlib stream (a valid header whose data decodes). Parquet, Arrow and ORC need their footer, so a text file that merely begins with "PAR1" or "ORC" gets no row, and neither does a file too short to hold both magics (a bare "PAR1") or text whose first two bytes pass the zlib header check by chance. Every other format (brotli, snappy, rar, Arrow IPC streams, raw deflate, ORC 0.11 files, which lack the end magic) is read as plain bytes and can pass clean, as can UTF-16 text and obfuscated forms (`[at]`, `%40`); names are not detected. A file at or above the threshold is reported as usual, as a lower bound.
- Wired into `review_checks.sh` as the built-in `committed-data` step, right after `invisible-chars`: it scans the changed files in diff mode and every tracked file under `--full`, skips the paths every step skips (node_modules, vendor, build dirs) plus third_party/, Pods/, bower_components/ and *.min.js, as `invisible-chars` does, and is listed under "analyzers ran". A missing script gives one not-checked row. Rows are not tagged `likely-fixture`, because a real address in a fixture is still a leak. The `method-situational.md` analyzer list names the step with its `.` and `not-checked` rows.
- Threshold 10, measured rather than guessed: 5 x 8 MiB of seeded random bytes held 2 email-shaped strings (0.05 per MB); across this repository's 93,711 tracked files at this commit the most distinct non-reserved addresses in one file is 6 (75 files hold any, none is a recognised container), so 10 flags nothing here while a threshold of 5 would flag 3 files (two bench outputs and this check's own unit test); a whole-tree run took 3 to 7 s. A data export holds dozens to thousands. Contributor lists (AUTHORS, .mailmap) reach 10 by design and show up as leads for the reviewer. `--threshold` tunes it.
- New tests `scripts/test_committed_personal_data.py` (31 unit tests, one skipped on macOS: they cover the container rows for every format above, real gzip, bzip2, xz, zlib and PDF data, footerless and overlapping magics and zlib lookalikes, the `git@` and asset-scale names, the repository total with its edges, the flag ranges and the regex memory bound on a hostile dotted run) and `scripts/test-review-checks-committed-data.sh` (12 checks, with vendor/ and node_modules/ files planted and left unflagged, and the repository-total row passing through the hub), registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/committed-personal-data.sh`.
- size-budget-raise: .claude/skills/deep-code-review/references/method-situational.md 43864→44018 the analyzer list names the new committed-data step and its rows

### Added
- `supply_chain_check.sh` scans a git DIR with OpenSSF Scorecard offline when `--scorecard owner/repo` is not given; before, that run printed `SKIPPED scorecard`. It exports the repo root's HEAD (`git archive HEAD`, tracked files only) and runs `scorecard --local` on the export, so an untracked `node_modules` cannot score Binary-Artifacts 0. The export is removed afterwards, also when the run is stopped by SIGTERM, SIGHUP or SIGINT. Only the checks that work offline run: Binary-Artifacts, Dangerous-Workflow, Dependency-Update-Tool, License, Packaging, Pinned-Dependencies, SAST, Security-Policy and Token-Permissions. Vulnerabilities is never included because it reported a false 10 ("0 existing vulnerabilities") while api.osv.dev was unreachable, and Fuzzing errors offline. Scores stay informational with no pass/fail threshold, as in the remote mode, and the `ok scorecard` line says the offline view is partial and not comparable with a public Scorecard score. A subdirectory DIR scores the whole repo root, and the same line names the root and says so. `git archive` runs with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, so a partial clone that is missing blobs is SKIPPED with a reason naming the partial clone instead of fetching over the network. A non-git DIR or a repo with no commit is also SKIPPED with the reason (exit 3 unless `--allow-skip`), and `--scorecard owner/repo` keeps the remote scan. The `supply-chain-check.md` table row and the script header say so. Test: `scripts/test-supply-chain-check.sh`, with a fake scorecard that records its arguments and the files it can see, and can hang so a test can signal the script.

### Fixed
- `comms_lint.py` `audit-pr`: the budget (1200 words and 160 lines, a failure above 1.5 times either) now counts everything outside `## Changes by area`, so a body written to the template with many areas no longer fails for its area text (eight areas came to 2024 words and failed). Inside that section each `### ` area fails above 200 words and the whole body fails above 3000 words, with no slack. The per-area cap covers `### ` areas only: bullet areas, text before the first `### ` heading and a `#### ` section that follows no `### ` heading are bound by the 3000-word cap alone. The `words` and `lines` the lint reports, and its score line, are the counted ones. `artifact-templates.md` states the scope and both caps. ## [1.623.0] — 2026-10-30

### Fixed
- `scripts/ci-gates.sh rules` now compares its sorted rows in the C locale, like the `sort -u` calls that feed them. Under a UTF-8 locale such as `en_US.UTF-8` its two `comm` calls saw unsorted input, so a baseline with a few rows could report a baselined rule as new, or a baseline that only shrank as grown and needing a `rule-baseline-raise:` line. The shipped baseline is empty, so nothing failed yet. Regression test: `scripts/test-rules-locale.sh` (registered from `scripts/ci-tests.d/rules-locale.sh`) runs the gate under C and `en_US.UTF-8`.

### Added
- `scripts/ci-gates.sh tests-wired --allowlist <file> <root>`: a standing check that every `scripts/test_*.py` and `scripts/test-*.sh` is run by CI. A test counts as run when `scripts/ci-tests.d/*.sh`, a `.github/workflows/*.yml` step, or a test those run (for example `test-ci-gates.sh`) names it on a non-comment line; otherwise it needs a `name<TAB>reason` row in `scripts/ci-test-allowlist.tsv`. A row without a reason, for a missing file, or for a test CI already runs also fails, so the list only shrinks. It runs from `scripts/ci-tests.d/tests-wired.sh`; its regression test is `scripts/test-tests-wired.sh` (a planted orphan fails, and it gives the same answers under `en_US.UTF-8` as under the C locale).
- The first run found 71 tests that no CI step ran: 59 are now registered (`secret-rule-waves.sh`, `security-gate-waves.bg.sh` as a background suite, `orphan-tests-misc.sh`, `orphan-tests.sh`) and the 12 corpus re-scores of 30 s or more are allowlisted with their measured runtimes.

### Fixed
- `scripts/test_auto_update_legacy_marker.py` took about 326 s because it copied `docs/bench` (about 90k files) into a scratch tree; it now skips that directory and runs in about 4 s. Its `install.sh` run, `scripts/test_install_canonical_global.py` and `scripts/test_peer_pains_5.py` now set `DCR_NO_PROBE=1`, so none of them calls github.com through the sandbox probe.

### Added
- `veche.py`: a decided record carries `kill_criteria_by_lens` (`{lens: text}`), each seat's own kill criterion as worded before near-duplicates collapse, so a reader can see which seat asked for which tripwire. It is additive: `kill_criteria` and `validate_verdict.py` are unchanged, a seat that gave none is left out of the map, and the evil twin's criterion stays in `minority_report.twin` (#2140).

### Changed
- `veche.py --help`: `--option` states the exact name rule (the `TOKEN` pattern, which the refusal for a bad name now quotes too), `--stakes` and `--reversibility` state the real gate (the council is skipped only when stakes are low or medium and reversibility is easy, and either flag alone convenes), and `--json-out` says how the file is written (#2136, #2139).
- `council.md` states the reply contract a custom `--cmd` must meet, as the parser really accepts it: a JSON object with a `verdict` and string-only `claims` items, prose and stray braces around it skipped, the first object with a valid `verdict` wins, and the `scores` map may sit in the verdict object or in any other object (#2137). It also lists `kill_criteria_by_lens` in the output row.

### Fixed
- `veche.py --json-out` writes through a temp file in the same directory and `os.replace`, at the early write and at the final one and on every outcome, so a reader or a crash never sees half a record. A symlinked path keeps pointing at its target, an existing file keeps its mode, a device or FIFO target is written in place, and an unwritable path still exits 2 with the `--json-out: cannot write` message (#2139).

### Fixed
- The wall-clock pins of `scripts/test_destructive_guard_w20.py`, `scripts/test_secret_extra_rules_w12.py`, `scripts/test_secret_extra_rules_w13.py` and `scripts/test_secret_extra_rules_w14.py` (0.2 s and 0.5 s on 100 KB lines) are now 2.0 s, so a loaded CI runner no longer fails them; a catastrophic-backtracking regression still takes far longer.
- `scripts/test-rules-locale.sh` and `scripts/test-tests-wired.sh` print `SKIP  en_US.UTF-8 ...` and run their C-locale cases when the runner has no `en_US.UTF-8`, instead of failing on a locale that is not installed.

### Changed
- `veche.py --help` states the `--json-out` directory rule: the record is written through a temp file beside the target, so a read-only file in a writable directory is replaced, while a read-only directory or a bind-mounted file exits 2. Test: `scripts/test_veche_doc_claims.py`.
- `council.md` says the `scores` map may sit under `scores` in the verdict object itself, or in any other object (bare or under `scores`), as `veche.py` reads it.

### Fixed
- `comms_lint.py` `audit-pr`: the attribution footer may sit in markup. A `<sub>🤖 Generated with ...</sub>` line (with or without a `---` rule before it), a `*Generated with ...*` or `_Generated by ..._` line after a rule or the robot line, and a `Co-Authored-By:` line in the same markup are footer-shaped, so a compliant body that ends with one no longer fails "Not fixed carries detail ('https://')". Markup alone does not make a footer: a wrapped line that is not a Generated or Co-Authored-By line, a Generated line with no rule or robot before it, and anything after a footer are still checked. The accepted markup is bounded (`<sub>`, `<sup>`, `<small>`, `*`, `_`, at most six), so a long run of `*` stays linear. `references/artifact-templates.md` states the rule. ## [1.622.0] — 2026-10-30

### Added
- Audit, security and hardening PR bodies (the PR title says audit, security or harden) must now explain the proposed changes before a reviewer opens the diff. `comms_lint.py` has a new kind `audit-pr` (budget 1200 words, 160 lines) with a `sections` rule that fails, at any length, when a required heading is missing (`Summary`, `What changes for reviewers and users`, `Changes by area`, `How to verify`, `Not fixed`; the names live in one constant, `AUDIT_SECTIONS`; `Dependency upgrades` is optional), when `What changes for reviewers and users` is empty (it needs items or `None`), or when `Not fixed` carries a file:line, line reference, HTTP route, URL or file path (counts only, tracked privately). Headings inside fenced code are not sections, sub-headings stay inside their section, and a template hint in an HTML comment is not content.
- Coverage: `comms_lint.py --kind audit-pr --file BODY --range BASE..HEAD` also fails when a file the PR changes is not named under `Changes by area`, by its full path or by a containing directory written with a trailing slash. Nothing is exempt, so `changelog.d` fragments and lockfiles must be named too. `changed_files()` reads the range with a read-only `git diff --name-only` and treats `A..B`, `A...B` and a bare `A` alike (B against the merge-base, the files the PR carries); an unreadable range (or one starting with `-`) exits 2 with the reason on stderr, so a bad range never passes as clean. Many uncovered files are listed as a count with the first five paths. The check stays linear on hostile input (a heading line of 50,000 spaces, a 200,000-character path-like token, 8,000 files against a 50 KB section): the heading and path patterns are bounded, and coverage uses `str.find` with explicit boundary checks. HTML comments are blanked with `str.find` as well, so a body of thousands of unterminated `<!--` stays linear (`scripts/test_comms_lint_comments.py`).
- The check runs by itself: `comms_guard.py` (the existing `PreToolUse` hook, registered by the operating layer) checks a `gh pr create|edit` as `audit-pr` when its `--title` says audit, security or harden. `create` without `--head` also gets the diff against `origin/<--base>` (default `origin/HEAD`; the `origin/` prefix means a stale local branch is never used and a `--base` value cannot act as a git option), so coverage is checked, read in the directory of a `cd` ahead of `gh` (a lane runs `cd <worktree> && gh pr create`, and the hook's own cwd is another checkout); `edit`, `--head` or a missing repo or base check the headings only. It stays advisory and fails open (it adds the exact fix per failing rule and never blocks); a `comms_lint.py` without the new kind keeps the old `pr` check. Other PR titles are unchanged.
- The body template is in `references/artifact-templates.md` (the reference that owns PR bodies, already routed from `communication-structure/SKILL.md`), with the new row in its budgets table. Test: `scripts/test_audit_pr_body.py` (against a throwaway git repo, registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/audit-pr-body.sh`); `scripts/test_comms_lint.py` lists the new kind and rule.

### Fixed
- `clock_lint.py`: the `timing bet under load` rule now covers JS/TS test files too (it flagged Python tests only, so the same bets passed in `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.mts` and `.cts`). It flags a fixed sleep (`sleep`, `delay`, `wait`, `waitForTimeout` with a literal, or a `setTimeout` inside `new Promise(...)` or around an assert) followed by an assertion in the same test block, a `{ timeout: N }` of 5000 ms or less in the options of a wait-style call, and an elapsed-time upper bound (`expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(N)`, chai `.below`, `assert(elapsed < N)`). `clock-lint: allow` on any line of the call, or on a comment line above it, is the escape; a fake timer or clock marker in the file exempts the file; any failure of the rule fails open as `COULD_NOT_CHECK`. Like the Python rule, `--block-added` blocks it only in newly added files (#2141).
- `scripts/test_clock_lint_reltext.py`: the elapsed-time fixture is a real timing bet, so the test now expects exactly that one finding and still no real-clock or advisory line.
- `verification-handback.md` and `testing-situational.md` name JS/TS beside Python for the timing-bet rule (byte-neutral edits).

### Added
- Pre-push commit identity check. `pre-push-verify.sh` now refuses a push when the author or committer email of any commit it adds is not a noreply form (`<local>@users.noreply.github.com` or `noreply@<domain>`), unless the address is listed in the gitignored `.identity-allow.local.txt` (one email or glob per line). The rules live in one script, `deep-code-review/scripts/identity_gate.py`, which the hook calls and `perun_doctor.py` imports. It checks the pushed commits that neither the remote sha (for an existing branch; ignored when it was never fetched) nor any remote-tracking ref has, so a branch rebased onto a newer main is not blamed for main's commits, masks every address in its output (`jane@example.com` shows as `j***@***.com`), and prints the fix (`git config user.email <id>+<username>@users.noreply.github.com`, `git commit --amend --reset-author`). It runs before the verdict cache and the unset-command handling, so neither a cached pass nor `DCR_PREPUSH_ALLOW_UNSET` skips it. `perun_doctor.py` gains a WARN-only "commit identity" row when the effective `user.email` is not a noreply form but the default branch's last 10 authors all are. Known ceiling: `Co-authored-by:` trailers are not checked, and with no python3 or no `identity_gate.py` the hook prints one notice and the push goes on. New test `scripts/test_identity_gate.py`.

### Added
- `scripts/council_bench.py`: an offline harness that scores the idea-critic council (`veche.py`) on the evil-twin corpus. Each case (default: the R2 cases) goes to `veche.py` as a packet under a throwaway root, and the hidden key never reaches a seat (the seats run in a directory that holds only the proposal). It prints, per case kind, how often the council blocks (HOLD or REVISE) or holds the proposal, with bootstrap intervals, and with `--judge` the R2 judge's recall and false-kill on the council deliverable. One `--records` directory holds a configuration's records and replays offline with identical numbers. A live run needs `--cap-calls`, checked before every council and judge call. No live run is committed, so the council and evil-twin rows of the scoreboard stay UNMEASURED. Test: `scripts/test_council_bench.py` (stub seats and judge, real `veche.py`).
- `council.md` points to the harness from its kill-criterion section.

### Fixed
- `agentic-delivery/scripts/heavy_gate.py`: a `grype` target whose name only starts with a subcommand (`grype db:latest`, `grype help.json`, `grype version:latest`) read as the light `grype db|version|help` form and was never held, because the lookahead used `\b` and `:` or `.` is a word boundary. The lookahead now needs the subcommand to be a whole word. A bare `grype` that reads an SBOM from stdin (`syft . -o json | grype`, `(cat sbom.json)|grype`, a pipe followed by a newline, `grype < sbom.json`) is now held, because it scans; a bare `grype` with no pipe or redirect into it stays light.
- `heavy_gate.py`: `npm ci --package-lock-only` was read as light through the lockfile-only exemption, yet `npm ci` removes `node_modules` first, so it is now held. `npm install --package-lock-only` stays light. A bare `npm install --package-lock-only` without `--ignore-scripts` can still run the project's own lifecycle scripts; that ceiling is recorded in a `ponytail:` comment beside `LIGHT_FLAGS`.
- `heavy_gate.py`: `uv tool run`, `yarn dlx`, `bun x` and `npm exec` are now unwrapped like `npx`, `uvx`, `bunx` and `pnpm exec`, so `uv tool run semgrep scan .` or `yarn dlx trivy fs .` is classified by the tool behind the launcher instead of passing light.
- `heavy_gate.py`: a backslash-newline continuation (`semgrep \` newline `scan .`) is joined before the command is classified. The tokenizer used to turn it into a separator, which split `semgrep` from `scan`, so the continued form passed light. The same join applies to `ceo_altitude_guard.py`, which reads commands through `heavy_gate.tokens` and `heavy_gate.segments`. A `#` comment line is left whole, because bash ends a comment at its newline even after a trailing backslash: `# note \` followed by `pytest -q` is still two lines, and `pytest -q` is held. A comment that follows a command on the same line (`echo hi # note`) still swallows the newline after it, so a heavy command on the next line reads light; that was already so before the join and is not changed here.
- `command -v pytest`, `command -v jest`, `command -v vitest` and `command -v playwright` are now pinned as light presence checks in `scripts/test_heavy_gate_scanners.py`; before, only the mutation test for `strip_wrappers` held that early return.

Tests: new tables and cases in `scripts/test_heavy_gate_scanners.py`. The rows that change behaviour fail on the previous `heavy_gate.py`; the stay-light rows (`command -v TOOL`, bare `grype` without stdin, `npm install --package-lock-only`) pin existing behaviour and pass on both.

### Added
- `agentic-delivery/scripts/heavy_gate.py` now holds whole-repo security scanners, JS dependency installs and Perun's own scan and CI entrypoints on a busy host, so audit runs and the scanner hub pass the same machine-wide admission check as test runners and builds. Held: `semgrep` (`scan`, `ci`, `--config`), `trivy` (`fs`, `repo`, `image`, `config`, `rootfs`, also behind a global flag such as `--cache-dir DIR`), `osv-scanner`, `grype`, `checkov`, `gitleaks` (`detect`, `git`, `dir`), `trufflehog` (`git`, `filesystem`, `github`), `npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun` `ci`, `i` and `install`, also behind `npx`, `uvx`, `bunx` or `pnpm dlx`, and `review_checks.sh`, `run-ci-tests.sh` and `app_pentest.sh` (as `bash PATH`, `./PATH` or a bare path, including a quoted `"$DIR/..."` path). Still light: `--version`, `--help`, `command -v TOOL` presence checks, db-only and lockfile-only runs (`--download-db-only`, `--download-java-db-only`, `--package-lock-only`), `osv-scanner`, `grype` or `checkov` with no argument, `grype db`, `grype version`, `grype help`, `zizmor`, `actionlint`, `shellcheck`, `hadolint`, single-file `bandit` and `ruff`, and the new `--list-affected` dry form of `run-ci-tests.sh`. Regression tests are in `scripts/test_heavy_gate_scanners.py` (pattern tables plus the hook on a busy and an idle machine).
- Known ceilings, also recorded in a `ponytail:` comment beside the patterns: the tool list is fixed and a launcher outside the unwrap list (`docker run`) or `bash -x PATH` still passes light; an unquoted `$VAR/script.sh` entrypoint is not matched because the tokenizer splits at `$`; `semgrep -f`/`-c`, bare `semgrep .`, `npm add`, bare `yarn`, `npm --prefix DIR ci` and the rarer `trivy`/`trufflehog` subcommands are not held.

### Changed
- `npm install` is no longer classed as light: it is a dependency install and is held like `npm ci`. `ceo_altitude_guard.py` counts build and test commands through the same pattern set, so the wider set also counts toward its per-turn threshold.
- The auto-wired `heavy_gate.py` line in `agentic-delivery/references/full-map.md` now says tests, builds, scans and JS installs.

### Fixed
- `gh_rest.py`: behind an HTTP proxy, `curl -i` prints the proxy's CONNECT reply before the real response, so the fallback returned the response headers glued to the body and callers failed to parse it as JSON (seen in the macOS sandbox). The fallback now skips every leading `HTTP/` header block. Tests: `scripts/test_gh_rest_proxy_headers.py`.

### Fixed
- `scripts/test-prepush-ci-parity.sh`: the fixture committed as `t@example.com`, which the pre-push commit identity check refuses, so "privacy ignores a deleted file" and "privacy skips a dangling symlink" failed (4/6). The fixture now commits as `t@users.noreply.github.com`, as the sibling pre-push tests do (6/6). `scripts/test-stage-run-lifecycle.sh` also commits as `t@example.com` but passes unchanged (16/16): its pre-push case pushes a HEAD already pinned as `origin/main`, so the identity check has no added commit to refuse.

### Added
- `provision_tools.sh`: new skill script that makes the scanners `review_checks.sh` wires actually run. The agent sandbox denies installs and the network, so scanners come out NOT RUN until the owner provisions them outside it. A plain run is a dry run that lists the missing scanner binaries and the cold caches (trivy DB, osv-scanner offline DB, a local semgrep `p/default` snapshot) and installs or writes nothing; `--print` emits the ONE line to paste yourself: `brew` and `pipx` installs (the pipx pins are the PyPI versions checked 2026-10-29; brew formulae cannot be pinned) plus the cache warm-ups (trivy with an empty `DOCKER_CONFIG`, because its DB download fails when `~/.docker/config.json` names a missing credential helper; `osv-scanner --offline-vulnerabilities --download-offline-databases`; a `curl` of the semgrep registry pack). A scanner found only in `~/.local/bin` (pipx, `uv tool`) counts as installed.
- `review_checks.sh` uses warm caches offline with no flag: the osv-scanner offline DB runs as `--offline-vulnerabilities` (`REVIEW_OSV=1` still selects the online API, an explicit `REVIEW_OSV_DB_DIR` still wins, a cold cache stays NOT RUN with the fix named) and the semgrep snapshot replaces the registry `p/default` pack as a local `--config` file (it counts as warm only when it has a top-level `rules:` key, so an empty file or an error page is cold and the registry pack is used; `scripts/test-provision-semgrep-warm.sh`); trivy runs offline against the cache `provision_tools.sh` warmed and is given it as `--cache-dir` (the cache moves under `DCR_CACHE_ROOT` when that is set, which trivy's own default dir ignores, so a provisioned host used to stay NOT RUN). It appends `~/.local/bin` to PATH (`DCR_USER_BIN` overrides, empty disables; `DCR_CACHE_ROOT` overrides the user cache dir).
- `review_checks.sh`: a closing stderr line `review_checks: ran X / wired Y scanners; not run: ...; partial: ...; fixable: ... (run: bash .../provision_tools.sh --print [DIR])` (wired = the scanners that had work in this run, shellcheck, ruff/pyflakes and `--history` gitleaks included, which a provision cannot install and so are never fixable), recorded in `review-checks-last.json` in the git common dir. A scanner that ran with a narrower scope (trivy secret-only, semgrep with errors) is listed under `partial` and in the record's `partial` key instead of counting as a full run. The osv-scanner fix names this repo as DIR: a bare `--print` treats one ecosystem's DB zip as a warm cache and can print nothing.
- `perun_doctor.py`: a `review scanners` row reads that record. WARN (exit 1) when scanners the last run wired did not run, or ran without their offline cache, for a cause `provision_tools.sh` fixes (the osv-scanner fix carries this repo as DIR); INFO with no readable record, no provisioning fix, or a partial scope; OK when everything wired ran in full.
- `scripts/test-provision-tools.sh` (hermetic: stub binaries, throwaway HOME and caches; it also runs the printed owner line against stubs and re-runs the review to prove a provision ends in ran = wired) and `scripts/test_doctor_review_scanners.py`.
- `docs/standards-index.md`: the osv-scanner, trivy, semgrep and PyPI sources behind the offline flags and pins, fetched 2026-10-29; the one observed osv-scanner v2.7.0 deviation from its docs (the DB directory is `osv-scalibr/`, not `osv-scanner/`) is recorded there.

### Changed
- `scrub_env.sh` pins `DCR_CACHE_ROOT` (a throwaway dir) and `DCR_USER_BIN` (empty) for every CI test child, so no test depends on which scanners or caches the host has provisioned. A test run by hand on a provisioned host that restricts PATH should set both itself.
- `tool-hub.md`: a Provisioning section (and the pre-seed bullet points at `provision_tools.sh --print`); osv-scanner is described as offline on a warm DB, online only with `REVIEW_OSV=1` (it used to say it stays behind that flag; `method-situational.md` and the `review_checks.sh` header agree), and the unsourced "exits 127" claim is gone (the osv-scanner docs list 127 as a general error only); `full-map.md` routes `provision_tools.sh` and tightens three pointer lines to pay for it, so the file stays 18996 bytes and the mustload floor keeps its pin.

A bundled rerun that also fails leaves semgrep NOT RUN and not fixable (a snapshot would not help). ### Fixed
- `review_checks.sh`: ten cases where a finding was dropped or mislabelled, or a run could read as clean. Each has its own block in `scripts/test-review-checks-scanner-gaps.sh` (stub tools on a hermetic PATH, offline), and each fails on the previous script.
  - zizmor findings were silently dropped: zizmor echoes the path it was given (`./.github/...`), which never matched the changed-file list. Paths are now normalized. A batch hub tool (zizmor, actionlint, bandit) that returns a row for a file outside the list it was given is now listed under `NOT RUN` with a `not-checked` row instead of reading as clean (gosec is exempt: it scans `./...`).
  - `--full` on a repo whose file list outgrew a pipe buffer dropped gitleaks, trivy and hub rows: `printf list | grep -q` under pipefail failed whenever grep matched early. Membership is now tested against a temp file.
  - osv-scanner: an exported `OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY` that already holds a seeded database now runs offline by default (as `REVIEW_OSV_DB_DIR` does; `provision_tools.sh --cache osv` reads it); `REVIEW_OSV=1` still asks the API. A cache with no database is never used: with none, osv-scanner prints empty results, not an error, which would read as clean.
  - actionlint is routed for workflow files (`actionlint -format '{{json .}}'`, exit 1 = findings), alongside zizmor.
  - An empty diff, or one with only excluded paths, exited 1 with no output (`grep -c` exits 1 at a count of 0 under `set -e`). It now exits 0 with `[]` and says `0 files in diff`.
  - semgrep: errors with zero findings on one 200-file chunk marked the whole tool `NOT RUN`, even when other chunks scanned fine. That chunk is now partial (stderr line plus a `not-checked` row, semgrep stays under `analyzers ran`); a scan is `NOT RUN` only when every scanned file errored. A single scan with errors on some files and no findings is likewise partial.
  - checkov and grype rows had shifted columns (rule held the check name or package, message empty, line 0) because `read` collapsed the empty leading file field. Rows now carry the rule id, line and message.
  - semgrep rule ids no longer carry the dotted local config-directory prefix that semgrep adds.
  - grype is routed to SBOM-like names only (`sbom`, `bom`, `cdx` or `spdx` as a whole name part): `app.cdx.json` is scanned, `bomb.json` and `kaboom.json` are not.
  - checkov: the flat "nothing to check" summary (no `results`, `parsing_errors` 0, for example variables-only Terraform) is a clean file instead of `NOT RUN`; compose files are no longer routed to it (not a checkov framework).
- Bundled semgrep rules (`templates/semgrep-taint/js.yml`): a `typeof req.body.password !== "string"` type check was reported as a hardcoded credential compare, because semgrep binds the whole operand and the name regex matched the tail of `typeof req.body.password`. `hardcoded-credential-compare` and `hardcoded-basic-auth` now skip an operand that starts with `typeof`; `scripts/test_semgrep_typeof_compare.py` applies the rule regexes to the bound text (offline, no semgrep) and fails on the previous rules.

A `---` rule or `🤖 Generated` line now starts the footer only when every line after it is footer-shaped (blank, `---`, `🤖 Generated ...`, `Generated with/by ...`, `Co-Authored-By: ...`); any other text after a rule is checked like the rest of its section. ### Fixed

The fallback carries over to the later chunks only while no registry run has succeeded; once one has, each later chunk tries the pack again. If the bundled rerun fails too, semgrep is `NOT RUN` as before. Test: `scripts/test-semgrep-registry-timeout.sh` (stub semgrep and trivy, so it stays offline).

### Added

Spend comes from ccusage (MIT, `ccusage claude daily --json --offline`, documented output shape only) when it is on PATH and the default log directory is read, with a parity line against `token_report.py`; otherwise, or when ccusage fails or prints another shape, from `token_report.py`'s own reader. A model with no rate row stays UNPRICED (never $0) and a transcript that cannot be read is counted: both are printed (`unpriced: <models>`, `unreadable: N sessions`) and make the `token_report.py` total a lower bound, so the parity line is skipped. Sessions are ranked by USD, unpriced ones last and flagged. Waste is `token_report.py`'s `lever_ranking` summed over the biggest sessions by USD in the window (cache pin, auto-compact, lane tool cap, Bash output cap), printed as upper bounds that overlap and are not additive, with the subagent share; the orchestrator tier is listed apart as an exposure (not a saving, not additive). Lever state comes from the user-level settings and the environment only (a project's own settings would mute a lever for every project): a lever whose key is set is skipped, and with unreadable user settings it is shown as state unknown. Transcripts whose main and lane files together exceed `--max-mb` (default 128) are counted as not measured and the spend coverage is printed. Reads usage, timestamps, model ids and tool-result sizes only; never message text; writes nothing. Hermetic tests in `scripts/test_spend_hub.py` use the frozen synthetic token-lever fixture, generated synthetic sessions and a ccusage shim. The tools read to choose ccusage are logged in `docs/standards-index.md`.

### Fixed

A run that owns the tag marker (or runs with `TRAIN_UNIQUE_RUN=off`) clears a leftover cancel file at start; it is kept while a live same-tag twin may own it, so an urgent stop is never swallowed. A cancel that arrives after the run has started is honored as before. The header says to touch the file only once the train runs (#2142).

### Fixed
- `veche.py`: a `COULD_NOT_DECIDE` record from a council that actually ran now keeps `dropped` (each failed seat with its own reason: `cmd exit N`, `cmd timeout`, `cap reached before call` or `malformed answer: ...`) and `cost` (calls and characters charged), as a decided record does. Before, the failure record kept one reason and lost the per-seat reasons, the `dropped` list and the call cost, so a council that lost its seats could not be told apart from one that never started (#2135).

### Fixed
- `veche.py`: `--alarm-s` now fires while the council is still running. Before, `COUNCIL_BLOCKING_WORK` was printed only after the run had finished, so a stuck council said nothing for as long as it ran. The line now reads `council still running after Ns (K calls started); default_action=...`, a decided run that already alarmed in flight does not repeat the line, and a run that then fails still prints its own `COULD_NOT_DECIDE` alarm line (#2138).
- `veche.py --progress-s N` (default 30, 0 = off) prints a `veche: running Ns, K calls started` heartbeat to stderr while the council runs, so a long council is no longer silent.

- `veche.py --json-out PATH` also writes the JSON record to PATH, for decided, `COULD_NOT_DECIDE` and `NOT_CONVENED` records alike. The file is opened before any seat is called, so a bad path exits 2 with a `--json-out: cannot write` message and costs nothing (#2139).

### Fixed
- `veche.py`: when the stakes gate skips the council, stderr now says so (`veche: NOT_CONVENED, no seat called (...)`) and adds `; --twin ignored` when `--twin` was given, so the skipped twin is no longer silent (#2139).
- `council.md` documents `--json-out`, `--progress-s`, the in-flight `--alarm-s`, the `--option` token rule, `verdict_basis` and the `dropped` and `cost` keys of a failure record.

### Fixed
- `veche.py`: `--option` names are checked before any call. Every seat has to echo an option name back as a JSON key, and a name that is not a short token made seats fail silently. A name must now be a short token (letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 32 characters); anything else is refused with a `COULD_NOT_DECIDE` record whose reason names the option and the rule, and no seat is called (#2136).
- `council.md` and `commands/council.md` state the rule, and the example run uses `--option ship --option wait` instead of option names that are whole sentences.

### Fixed
- `veche.py`: the decision record explains itself (#2140). `verdict_basis` says how the verdict was reached: the tally top and its votes, a tie and whether the cautious order or `--chair` broke it, an `owner-request` council whose `HOLD` became `REVISE`, or a `do-nothing` decision that turned `PASS_TO_USER` into `REVISE`.
- `veche.py`: a dissenting seat's answer now appears once. `dissent` keeps the verbatim answers (the validator requires the key) and `minority_report` carries the twin plus `dissenting_seats`, the names of those seats, instead of repeating the answers.

### Fixed
- `veche.py`: a seat reply is read by scanning for JSON objects, not by cutting from the first `{` to the last `}`. A brace in the prose around the answer (`{as asked}`, a trailing `:{`) no longer makes the whole reply unparseable, and scores sent as a second JSON object (`{"scores": ...}` or the bare options map) are used when the verdict object has none. The first object with a valid `verdict` is the answer; an object without one is still rejected as `bad verdict`. The evil twin's reply is read the same way (#2137).

## [1.621.0] — 2026-10-29

### Added
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh --affected` now records a receipt for every run, pass or fail, through lkg.py's internal `record_affected_cli` entry, which only the runner uses and which is no CLI subcommand (kind `affected`, `<hash>.<tree>.affected.json`, never the last-known-good pointer, pruned after 7 days). It holds HEAD, the working-tree tree hash taken before any suite runs (`lkg.py tree`: `git add -A` into a temp copy of the index, so tracked, staged and untracked-unignored files count and the real index is untouched), the base, the blob of `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` as it ran, each selected suite and its exit code (`-` for a suite the fail-fast runner never reached) and the overall code. The tree is re-hashed after the suites: a suite that changed it leaves no receipt. A lane's hand-back could claim a pass the runner never produced (a claim of 44/45 for a head where one suite failed); the receipt is what makes the claim checkable.
- Receipts work inside the agent sandbox, which denies `~/.cache`: they are written to and read from the first writable of `<git common dir>/perun`, `$TMPDIR/perun`, then the landing cache dir (reads take the newest across all three).
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh --list-affected [BASE]` is the dry form of `--affected`: it prints `selected: <suite>` per suite and runs no gate, suite or receipt. `lkg.py affected-check <tree> [BASE]` uses it to re-derive the selection for the tree and requires every selected suite at rc 0 and the receipt's runner blob to be the tree's, so a hand-written receipt that lists some suites (or another runner) is refused, and a receipt missing a key is skipped, never a `KeyError`. Exit 0 pass, 1 refused, 3 could not verify (no writable receipt location, an unreadable receipt file, or a failed re-derivation). The local receipt stops honest, stale and partial over-claims; a deliberate forgery needs CI proof, and CI is the authority.
- `handback.py --body-file` now flags a line that claims a full test pass (`run-ci-tests`, `--affected`, `Tests: N/N` or `Tests N/N`, "N tests passing", beside pass, passing, green, ok, any `X/X` or a tick, so "44/45 pass; rerun 45/45 pass" is a claim) unless `lkg.py affected-check` accepts a receipt for the head's tree (re-derived against the merge-base of `--base`) or the head is the last-known-good. It prints `unverified test claim (no receipt for this tree)` (or `receipt for this tree failed: <suite> rc=1`) per line and exits red (`handback RED: test claim`). Honest prose is not a claim: "not passed", "did not pass" and "2 of 3 passed" are ignored. "added 2 tests; lint ok" is not a claim. When no receipt location is writable, the tree or merge-base does not resolve (the receipt's own base is never used instead), or the receipt file cannot be read, the claim reads `test claim could not be verified` and the hand-back exits 3 (UNVERIFIED), never red. Error text shows the home directory as `~`. Test: `scripts/test_affected_receipt.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/affected-receipt.sh`).

### Fixed
- `scripts/test-review-checks-tool-hub.sh`: every case now runs `review_checks.sh` on a hermetic PATH (the shim dir, the inert scanner stubs and a dir of symlinks to only the system binaries it needs) instead of the host PATH. The "missing -> NOT CHECKED" and "not-checked row in JSON" cases failed on any host with a real zizmor, bandit, hadolint, gosec, grype or checkov installed; they now simulate absence, and no host tool runs un-stubbed in the other cases. Verified with the tools installed, with a stripped PATH, and with decoy tools first on PATH.

### Added
- Bundled semgrep rules (`templates/semgrep-taint/js.yml`, `py.yml`, run by `review_checks.sh` when the repo has no semgrep rules of its own): `perun.{js,py}.hardcoded-credential-compare` (WARNING) flags a variable, property, subscript or `.get("...")` named like pass, password, secret, token or API key that is compared with `==`, `===`, `!=` or `!==` to a non-empty string literal, and `perun.{js,py}.hardcoded-basic-auth` (ERROR) flags a base64-decoded value (`Buffer.from(..., "base64")`, `atob`, `base64.b64decode`) compared to a literal, including after `.split(":")` or destructuring. Also flagged: `.toLowerCase()`/`.trim()`/`.strip()`/`.lower()`-wrapped names and `compare_digest(x, "literal")`. Not flagged: empty or single-character literals, scheme and sentinel literals (bearer, basic, none, null, undefined, true, false), a bare `pwd`/`PWD` name, env reads (`process.env.X`, `os.environ`, `os.getenv`), JWT header fields (`alg`, `typ`, `kid`) in the decoded-Basic rule, and test, fixture, mock and e2e paths. Template literals are not matched.

### Fixed
- `surface_check.py checks`: when no check ran at all (no check-runs at the sha, with or without `--require`) and the head commit message holds a GitHub CI-skip token (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]` anywhere, a bare prose mention is enough; or a `skip-checks: true` trailer only as the last line after two empty lines; matching is case-sensitive because the docs do not say it ignores case), the verdict is a terminal FAIL naming the token as the likely cause instead of "wait and re-check". A required name with no run while an unrelated check ran stays COULD_NOT_CHECK. The FAIL text also names the other zero-run causes (no CI on the ref, path filters). The fix is one new commit with a clean message. Token list verified against the GitHub docs on 2026-10-29 (`docs/standards-index.md`). Test: `scripts/test_surface_check_skip_token.py`; eval `zero-checks-skip-token-head-message`; triage line in `red-gate-triage.md`.
- `review_checks.sh --history` scanned `BASE...HEAD` (symmetric), which also scanned every BASE-only commit when the branch was behind BASE, so main's history raised findings against the PR. It now scans `BASE..HEAD`, the commits the branch adds. `gate-epistemology.md` principle 2 states the scope (origin/main..HEAD plus `git diff origin/main...HEAD`, the ranges `review_checks.sh` uses, never old_tip..HEAD after merging main; scan and push as separate steps). Test: `scripts/test-review-checks-history-range.sh`; eval `banlist-scan-range-after-main-merge`.

## [1.620.0] — 2026-10-29

### Added
- `audit_skills.py`: new `control-char` rule flags NUL and other C0 control characters (all but tab, LF, CR, FF) in text files, one finding per character as `path:line: high control-char: control character U+XXXX at col N` (first 20 per file, then a count of the rest). A known binary extension is `unscanned` unconditionally and there is no path skip (the audit has ignore markers); a text-extension file with a NUL in its first 8 KB still gets `unscanned` plus the first control character, since git shows such a file as binary and hides its diff; UTF-16 files (BOM, or NULs on alternate bytes) are decoded and scanned. A NUL past 8 KB used to make the whole file `unscanned`; it is now scanned. Tests: `scripts/test_audit_skills_control_char.py`.
- `review_checks.sh`: new built-in `invisible-chars` step, always on and with no tool to install, flags NUL and other C0 control characters and bidi, zero-width and tag characters in the changed text files of the repo under review (every tracked text file under `--full`). One row per finding in the usual JSON shape (`tool` `invisible-chars`, rule `control-char`, `hidden-unicode` or `not-checked`, message `control character U+001B at col 6`), first 20 per rule and file then a count row, at most 200 rows then one `not-checked` row, and listed under `analyzers ran`. Locale files (`.po .arb .xlf .xliff .properties .strings`, or under `locales/ i18n/ l10n/`) report only bidi overrides and isolates; tag characters inside a flag emoji sequence and ESC in `.snap .golden .ansi .log` or `__snapshots__/` are skipped; a file with an early NUL is reported only under a known text extension (else skipped silently); UTF-16 is decoded, not reported as NULs; only the first 2 MB of a file is read (a `partially scanned` row beyond); file names are scanned too (line 0); `third_party/`, `Pods/`, `bower_components/` and `*.min.js` are skipped. Rows under fixture or test paths are tagged `[likely-fixture]` (the gitleaks FXD/FXB definition) instead of dropped, and a timeout keeps the rows found so far. The rules live in the new `invisible_chars.py` next to the script, which `scripts/audit_skills.py` now imports instead of keeping its own copy; a scan that fails or times out adds a `not-checked` row. Tests: `scripts/test_invisible_chars.py`, `scripts/test-review-checks-invisible-chars.sh`, `scripts/test_invisible_chars_hardening.py`, `scripts/test-review-checks-invisible-chars-hardening.sh`.
- `scripts/test_secret_anthropic_airtable.py`: pins that the privacy gate's secret scanner (vendored gitleaks v8.30.1 rules, identical to upstream master for these four) flags Anthropic API and admin keys and Airtable personal access tokens and legacy keys, and stays quiet on near-misses. No new regex was needed; fixtures are built at runtime.

### Changed

## [1.619.0] — 2026-10-29

### Added
- `perun_doctor.py`: new "stale local skills" row. WARNs when a repo-local `.claude/skills/<perun skill>/SKILL.md` has an older `version:` than the global copy (the local copy shadows the newer one, so the stale one silently wins), naming both versions and paths with the fix hint "remove or update repo-local copy"; plugin skills are namespaced and coexist with repo-local ones, so they are not compared; a missing side, unparsable version (`1.2` equals `1.2.0`), repo equal to home or a symlinked skills dir shows INFO n/a. New test `scripts/test_doctor_stale_local_skills.py`.

### Fixed
- Per-mode coverage can no longer read as zero findings. `validate_status_claims.py` has a fifth detector: a findings claim for a review mode (security, perf, a11y, privacy, reliability, correctness, ux) fails unless the file carries a `mode: ran (N files)` (N >= 1) or `mode: NOT RUN (reason)` entry for it. A claim is the mode word beside a count or negation word at the start of a line, bullet, table cell or clause ("security: no issues", "security findings: 0", "Security — all clear", "0 new security findings", "No security concerns", "perf: no regressions"); a claim beside a NOT RUN entry, a bare `ran`, `ran (0 files)`, a reasonless or placeholder (`reason`, `x`, `n/a`, `none`) NOT RUN is flagged too. Fenced code is skipped; `ran (12 files, 0 findings)`, `ran (1,200 files)` and a table row `| security | ran (3 files) |` are entries. Closes a dogfood miss where a lane that ran only perf handed back "security 0 new". `report-format.md` adds a required `Mode coverage:` line (repeated in the BLUF and every lane hand-back), `full-map-report.md`'s definition of done names it, and the example report carries one.
- `handback.py --body-file FILE` runs the same check on the hand-back body and stops red (`handback RED: mode coverage`) on an unbacked claim; without `--body-file`, or without deep-code-review installed, nothing is checked. Test: `scripts/test_handback_mode_coverage.py`.
- `review_checks.sh`: a tool that timed out, crashed or lost the lease was listed under "analyzers ran"; it now leaves that list (even when a later file passes) and appears once in a new `NOT RUN: <tool> (<why>), ...` part of the stderr summary (`none` when empty), and a skipped tool that is not a hub tool now also lands a `not-checked` row on stdout, so `[]` never hides it. A tool that is merely not installed stays under "skipped (not installed)". Tests: `scripts/test-mode-coverage.sh`, eval `report-mode-coverage-not-run`.

### Fixed
- `review_checks.sh`: when the heavy lease is still full after `REVIEW_LEASE_WAIT`, the heavy scanners (gitleaks, osv-scanner, semgrep, trivy, grype, checkov, gosec) now run degraded instead of being skipped, which left a security coverage hole on a busy host. They run under `nice -n 19` without taking the lease, with `--jobs 1` for semgrep and `--parallel 1` for trivy (the other tools have no single-worker flag and run as-is). The "analyzers ran" summary names them, for example `semgrep (degraded: lease full, nice 19, 1 worker)`. `REVIEW_LEASE_FULL=skip` restores the old skip. `supply_chain_check.sh` does not use the lease and is unchanged. New test `scripts/test-review-checks-lease-degraded.sh`.
- `review_checks.sh` degraded mode hardening: the perl timebox used on stock macOS (no `timeout`) now exits 127 when the scanner cannot be exec'd instead of exiting 0 with empty output, which read as a clean scan for every caller (such a tool is now reported not run). Degraded mode probes `nice -n 19 true` once and runs without nice, and without the `nice 19` label, when nice is missing or warns (sandbox `setpriority` EPERM). A degraded semgrep `--jobs 1` or trivy `--parallel 1` that exits non-zero is retried once without the flag; a good retry drops the `1 worker` label. The test now runs on a restricted PATH of stubs plus the system binaries it needs.

### Added
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh --affected [BASE]` runs the privacy gate and the trigger lint, then only the `scripts/ci-tests.d` tests a changed file can reach. Changed files are BASE (the argument, else `RUN_CI_BASE`, else the pre-push hook's `BASE_SHA`, else merge-base with `origin/main`) versus the working tree plus untracked files, read NUL-delimited with unquoted names (renames count as a delete plus an add; a changed path that is not a file, symlink or deletion fails closed). With no resolvable base it prints `affected: NOT RUN (no base)` and exits 0, so it never blocks a push. A test is picked when its own text, or a `scripts/test-*.sh` / `test_*.py` it invokes (one level), names a changed file as a whole name (`SKILL.md`, `ci.yml`, `README.md`, `INDEX.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` need the repo-relative path). A changed `.sh`/`.py` no test names gets one reverse-dependency hop (scripts that source or import it, then the tests naming those); if still none it prints `UNCOVERED: <file> (no test names it; CI only)`. `scripts/test-ci-gates.sh` is left to CI (it runs sharded there; `test-ci-gates: left to CI`) unless it or `scripts/ci-gates.sh` changed. Privacy scans only the changed files, or the whole tree when a `.banlist*.txt`, `scripts/ci-gates.sh` or `scripts/secret_scan.py` changed (the tree holds ~90k fixture files and CI scans all of it). It prints `affected: N of M tests (selected by: file→test)`, runs nothing when no file changed, exits non-zero on any failure, and never records the last-known-good pointer (a partial run proves nothing about HEAD). The repo `.githooks/pre-push` now defaults `DCR_PREPUSH_CMD` to this command (the env override is kept), so a sibling test broken by a change is caught before CI. Test: `scripts/test-run-ci-tests-affected.sh` (temp-repo fixture).

### Fixed
- `review_checks.sh` keeps every temp file (raw rows, scanner output, gitleaks config/report, semgrep HOME, audit dirs) in one private `mktemp -d` dir per run, removed on exit, so concurrent runs sharing `$TMPDIR` cannot touch each other's files.
- `review_checks.sh` no longer reports semgrep as "not run (partial scan)" while emitting its findings: a partial scan prints `partial: semgrep ran but reported errors` and keeps the findings.
- `review_checks.sh` finds `tsc` in `node_modules/.bin/tsc` (cwd or git toplevel only; run only when REVIEW_TEST_CMD is set, since it executes project code) when it is not on PATH, instead of reporting it not installed.
- `supply_chain_check.sh` reports zizmor/actionlint as `n/a` when the repo has no workflow files; INCOMPLETE only when workflows exist and the tool is missing.
New test `scripts/test-scanner-reporting-fixes.sh`; `test-supply-chain-check.sh` and `test-review-checks-security-folds.sh` updated to the new wording.

### Added
- `surface_check.py deps`: when a lane diff (tracked or untracked) touches `package.json` or a lockfile (npm, yarn, pnpm, bun), a local green is refused unless a `node_modules` exists inside the worktree at or above each touched file and every changed dependency, peer, override or resolution entry resolves inside the worktree (Node otherwise walks up to a parent checkout's stale deps, as in a zod 3 to 4 bump that passed locally and failed CI). Versions are compared only for exact, `^`, `~` and x-range specs (a prerelease never satisfies a plain `^4.0.0`); every other spec is reported as "N unjudged (range/tag), version not compared" and is not a version proof. Detection only; it prints the install command to run and never installs. Yarn Plug'n'Play has no `node_modules` and always fails here.

### Added
- `scripts/tenant_scope_check.py DIR` (stdlib, report-only): parses `*.prisma` models, treats a model with a `workspaceId`/`orgId`/`tenantId`/`teamId` field as tenant-scoped, and flags `findUnique`/`findFirst`/`update`/`updateMany`/`upsert`/`delete`/`deleteMany` (and `OrThrow`) calls in server code (`app/**/actions.ts`, `app/api/**`, `server/**`, `*.server.ts`) whose `where` has `id` but not the scope field (HIGH, "unscoped tenant access"), plus tenant-linked models with no scope field that server code uses (MED, "model missing tenant key"). False-positive guards: scope field as a top-level `where` key (bare, quoted or computed; also compound keys and a top-level `AND`; not text such as `id: x.workspaceId`, not `OR`), relation key, variable or spread `where`, comments, strings, test files, a `tenant-scope-ok` comment. It is a heuristic lead-finder, not coverage: silence is not proof of tenant isolation (aliased/awaited clients, variable `where`, findMany/count/raw SQL are not seen), and it prints `heuristic; scanned N server files` on stderr. Output is one `path:line: SEV: message` per finding plus a JSON summary; exit 0. `review_checks.sh --full` runs it as an optional step (SKIPPED when no `*.prisma` is tracked). Routed from `references/full-map.md` (domain T row), which stays within its frozen byte budget and the Phase 0-2 must-load floor pin. New test `scripts/test-tenant-scope-check.sh`, eval `audit-tenant-scope-id-only-where`.

## [1.616.0] — 2026-10-29

### Fixed
- `review_checks.sh`: when osv-scanner and trivy give no dependency result (DB unreachable in a sandbox or offline, not installed, lease full), the ecosystem's own audit now runs per lockfile (`npm audit --package-lock-only` for `package-lock.json`, `pnpm audit` for `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pip-audit -r` for `requirements*.txt`) and a `review_checks: dependency scan: <tool> ran for <lockfile>` line names which one ran; its findings land in the JSON under that tool. Coverage is tracked per lockfile (osv-scanner success, or a trivy `Target` for that lockfile), so one covered lockfile never hides another that was not scanned. Like osv-scanner it is opt-in (`REVIEW_OSV=1` or `REVIEW_OSV_DB_DIR`) because it queries the registry. The audit runs on a copy of the lockfile in an empty temp dir with the public registry and no user or global npmrc (a repo `.npmrc` registry or credentials are never read), and `pip-audit` gets `--no-deps --disable-pip` (no resolver, no venv, no target code). The tool counts as ran only after its output parsed. A changed lockfile with no dependency scan at all (opt-in unset, fallback tool missing or unreachable, unparseable output, or no fallback for the ecosystem such as `yarn.lock` or `Cargo.lock`) now yields a `dep-scan` `not-checked` row instead of a silent clean. A trivy secret-only run no longer counts as a dependency scan.

The policy failure is reported once on stderr and no longer adds a bogus not-checked row to the scanner that happened to hit it first. ## [1.614.0] — 2026-10-29

### Fixed
- `perun_auto_update.py`: hook mode now also updates a user-global install. When `~/.claude/.perun-install.json` exists, the home directory is not already the project target and the project's `auto_update` policy is on (a project opt-out covers `~` too), the SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hook spawns a second background worker for `~`, with its own 6h throttle stamp. Before, only `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` (or the cwd) was targeted, so a global install never updated. An unresolvable home falls back to the project target only. The worker's git lock and status checks still run on `~` and fail soft when it is not a git repo; the PR step never runs for `~`, so a dotfiles repo there gets no `perun/update-v*` branch. ## [1.613.0] — 2026-10-29

### Added
- `stage_run.py`: every `train-*` stage (`VERIFY_CMD`, `BROWSER_CMD`, each `RERUN_CMD` run) now gets `TRAIN_PORT`, a free loopback port picked per stage by binding port 0, and `PORT` set to the same number when it is unset. Serve on `$TRAIN_PORT` instead of a fixed port so parallel trains and re-runs no longer collide with EADDRINUSE and land nothing. A `TRAIN_PORT` the caller already set is kept; if the OS refuses the bind the stage still runs without one. A caller-set `PORT` that differs from `TRAIN_PORT` is left alone with one stderr warning. An EADDRINUSE the stage prints is not mapped to DEFER (75): `stage_run` does not read stage output.
- `train_land.sh` and `train_yield.py`: the yield ledger now records the head SHA each PR rode with. A train that ends with no culprit (every PR passed the failing ids alone on the base, or no REAL id existed) is ledgered with outcome `unpinned` (or `flaky`); a culprit, a base red and the "may be an intermittent regression" CANT are never ledgered as either. A PR that rode `TRAIN_SOLO_AFTER` (default 3, 0 = off) such trains at its current head is named by `train_yield.py solo PR:SHA...`. `train_land.sh` lands at most one such PR per train (the first eligible), alone and without a union, only when every check on that exact head passed, with the merge pinned to that SHA (`land_train.sh` accepts `LAND_PRS="<n>:<sha>"`); the other PRs stay in the train and are re-tested on the new base by the next one. A PR whose checks are not all green stays in the train. The exclusive heavy lease is released for the solo landing, and a single PR left over is reported as left (not landed).

### Added
- agentic-delivery: five gate-hardening mechanisms. (1) `pre-push-verify.sh` probes `nice` first and, when it is denied or broken, runs the gate at normal priority with one notice instead of failing. (2) The `heavy_gate.py` busy message names the lease holders (pid, kind, age, train gate) read from the lease files, with no ps or top. (3) With `DCR_PREPUSH_CMD` unset, the pre-push hook reuses the project's own lint (package.json `lint` script, Makefile `lint:` target, or pyproject `[tool.ruff]`), and an unreadable config fails closed. (4) `perun_doctor.py` reports dev-DB servers (postgres, mysqld, mongod, redis-server) whose data dir is gone and prints a `kill -TERM` line for the owner; it never kills. (5) `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` also runs the privacy gate and the trigger lint before the tests. ### Added

The LLM verify step was not run (no spend). Re-score with `python3 docs/bench/sast-sca-1027/run.py`.

### Added
- agentic-delivery: four mechanisms from peer delivery reports. `host_installer.py` announces a fixed named host installer (command built by the script, quoted with shlex), prints the one-line owner `! <command>`, is called by `perun_auto_update.py` after an update and cleared by `install.sh --global-rules`; policy `installer_unapplied_h` (hours, default 0 = off) makes the landing watchdog warn while it stays unapplied, and a corrupt state file alarms and is quarantined. `peer_ack.py` implements a read receipt on the board: a directive posted with `board_post.py --token` is undelivered until the `to:` agent posts an `ACK --token` (the one non-chatter ACK); an unreadable board counts as undelivered. The watchdog's WIP count exempts at most one PR labelled `p0-recurrence` with a numeric `Fixes: #N` trailer, and only when `gh` shows the issue reopened within 24 h (fail closed). `pregate_parity.py` allows a faster checker to run fail-fast before the authoritative gate only after 5 failing commits show it failed too and no counterexample exists; `record` writes the gate-time ledger. Test: `scripts/test_delivery_peer_mechanisms.py`.

### Added
- review_checks.sh gitleaks pass: optional repo-root `.gitleaks-allow` (`rule path-glob sha256-of-secret` per line) drops known false positives by content hash, read from the base ref only (a change cannot approve its own secret), so it survives history rewrites that break baseline fingerprints. The default allowlist template now also skips lockfiles. Test: `scripts/test-review-checks-gitleaks-allow.sh`.

Every `Tests:` line needs each `X/Y` with X==Y and a total above 0; a missing line, `0/0` or `5/6` is unverified, unless a non-empty `No-Tests-Reason:` trailer is present (a BLOCKED/WIP head subject is exempt). `HANDBACK_TESTS_COUNT=enforce` fails closed with `handback tests-count UNVERIFIED: no passing test count` and exit 4; the default `shadow` only warns, `off` skips. ### Fixed

New policy key `hold_labels` (non-empty list, default `["do-not-merge"]`, case-insensitive; an unreadable policy also skips). Test: `scripts/test_hold_reread.py`.

### Added
- agentic-delivery: the landing watchdog now alarms per lane. Opt-in policy `lane_idle_h` (hours) plus `lane_globs` (`{lane: [fnmatch globs]}`) emit "Lane stalled: ..." when a lane has green PRs waiting and its last merge (last 100 merged PRs) is older than the limit, so a busy lane can no longer hide an idle one behind the total-merges alarm. No map or limit keeps today's behavior. Test: `scripts/test_lane_stall.py`.

### Added
- agentic-delivery: last-known-good (LKG) pointer. The new local full-suite runner `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` runs every `scripts/ci-tests.d` test and, only when all pass, records the sha and UTC time with `lkg.py record` (state beside the landing watchdog's cache, keyed on the git common dir so worktrees share it, written atomically). `land-release.sh` requires `origin/main` to be the LKG and otherwise reports the untested gap: policy `lkg_gate` `shadow` (default, warns), `enforce` (refuses with exit 1; a crashed `lkg.py` refuses with exit 2) or `off`. The landing watchdog warns "Last-known-good is N h old" when policy `lkg_stale_h` (hours, default 0 = off) is exceeded and fails open on any error. Test: `scripts/test_lkg_pointer.py`.

### Fixed
- supply_chain_check.sh osv API fallback walked every `package-lock.json` and `requirements*.txt` under the target, including gitignored stale copies (build output, old worktrees), so a lockfile already patched to a fixed version still reported a critical from an old copy's version. It now skips gitignored files, matching `osv-scanner -r`. Test: `scripts/test-supply-chain-osv-fallback.sh`.

### Added
- deep-code-review: bundled generic semgrep taint-mode rules (`templates/semgrep-taint/py.yml`, `js.yml`) for SQL injection, command injection, path traversal, SSRF, unsafe deserialization/eval, XSS and open redirect, with generic sources (request data, function parameters) and sinks and allowlist-guard exclusions. `review_checks.sh` now runs them plus `p/default` when semgrep is installed and the repo has no semgrep config (`REVIEW_SEMGREP_REGISTRY=0` drops `p/default`; an unreachable registry reruns with the bundled rules alone). `security_verify.py` accepts a semgrep `--json` report directly and maps `extra.dataflow_trace` `taint_source`/`taint_sink` to `source`/`sink`.
- In-sample score on the 2026-10-27 SAST fixture (the rules were tuned against it, so this is not a generalization claim): raw `p/default` TP 8, FP 3, FN 5; bundled rules alone TP 13, FP 0, FN 0; bundled plus `p/default` TP 13, FP 3, FN 0. Caveat: semgrep OSS 1.182 emits no `dataflow_trace` (only the Pro engines do), so on OSS reports every row still reaches `security_verify.py` as `unverified` with a note to trace the source by hand. A blind held-out fixture will judge generalization. Tests: `scripts/test_semgrep_taint.py`, `scripts/test-review-checks-semgrep-default.sh`.

Stage weights, a gh retry shim, a red-main owner alarm and a serial-test detector

- stage_run.py reads PERUN_STAGE_WEIGHTS (stage=weight) and records the weight on its heavy lease; the slot cap, and so heavy_gate.py, count it. A heavier stage waits until it fits, runs alone if it exceeds the cap, and frees its weight to waiting stages when it ends.
- scripts/gh-shim/gh is a PATH shim that retries idempotent gh reads with backoff on transient errors only; writes run exactly once.
- red_main.py reports the count of reds with no owner or fix past 1h and the oldest red age; policy keys red_uncovered_max and red_oldest_h (default 0 = off) make it exit nonzero.
- flake_ledger.py serial lists tests that fail only in the full parallel run and pass solo; the triage reference states the rule: move them to the serial project the same day.

Train, pregate and pre-push stages now run through `stage_run.py`: each takes the machine-wide heavy lease that `heavy_gate.py` counts (bounded wait, then DEFER exit 75) and is killed, process group included, after the policy key `stage_timeout_min` (default 120 minutes; the train uses `TRAIN_STAGE_TIMEOUT_MIN`, default 180), with the stage name logged. A deferred (75) or timed-out (124) stage is infrastructure, not RED: `train_land.sh` ends exit 3 "stage did not complete" without a ratchet culprit hunt, `train_flake.sh` returns 125, and a command that itself exits 75 or 124 is reported as 1. The lease records pid and start times, so a SIGKILLed `stage_run` has its orphaned child reaped by the next one and a reused pid never holds a slot. New `file_finding.py` searches each title word and refuses to file an issue that matches an open issue, a closed issue or a PR merged in the last 14 days (at least two shared title keywords, or any explicit keyword; `--force REASON` overrides and logs). The `heavy_gate.py` PreToolUse hook now waits inside the hook for a transient load or lease HOLD (backoff, `PERUN_HEAVY_HOOK_WAIT_SECS`, default 60, cap 120, 0 = old immediate deny) before it denies the turn, clamped to the hook's own timeout minus 2s; the operating-layer template raises that timeout from 5s to 70s and `install.sh --apply-operating-layer` replaces an older 5s entry instead of adding a second one. The repo `pre-commit` hook now runs under `stage_run.py --hook` with a 60s wall-clock cap (`PERUN_COMMIT_HOOK_MIN`): a hung hook exits nonzero with `COULD-NOT-CHECK: hook exceeded 60s; index.lock holder: <pid cmd or unknown>`, only reports that holder and never signals it, and never passes; the lane preamble says commit hooks run fast checks only and full suites run on the train host. `stage_run.py` also skips, with a warning, a process group it may not signal (PermissionError) and keeps that lease instead of running unleased; leases record the host and another host's lease is ignored; a malformed `PERUN_HEAVY_WAIT_SECS` exits 2; the stage timeout is stretched by max(1, load1/cores), capped at 3x, measured at stage start (never for the commit hook). `file_finding.py` ignores empty and under-3-character keywords, matches keywords as whole words and, for a title with fewer than 2 qualifying words, matches only an equal normalized title. The `pre-commit` hook warns on stderr when it cannot apply the cap. `stage_run.py` now exits 2 on a nan, inf or negative timeout or wait, handles SIGHUP and the death of its parent process (the stage's group is killed and the lease released) and installs its signal handlers before the slot wait; `--probe` waits for a slot and gives it back. `train_land.sh` renews the exclusive heavy lease in the background (`PERUN_LEASE_HEARTBEAT_SECS`, default 600) so a stage longer than the 2h lease TTL keeps it, drops it while waiting for a full slot (`TRAIN_SLOT_WAIT_SECS`) and retakes it, and runs ratchet attribution under `stage_run.py` (`TRAIN_RATCHET_TIMEOUT_MIN`, default 30; a timed-out ratchet names no culprit). `file_finding.py` never matches on an empty normalized title and also searches open PRs. `pre-push-verify.sh` prints `deferred: heavy slot busy` or a timed-out message for stage rc 75 / 124 and still rejects the push. Three generic lessons: fanout sizing is re-read between shards and never fixed from the load at stage start, a heavy slot guards only the contended stage and not the whole train, and a lane checks the state of issue #N before applying a workaround tied to it.

### Fixed
- `cost_statusline.py` recompiled the 2800-line `token_report.py` on every status-line refresh because it disabled bytecode writing; it now caches bytecode in `~/.cache/perun-pyc`. On a loaded host (load average ~80), 25 interleaved runs per arm on one fixed transcript: median 193 ms to 133 ms, minimum unchanged (52 vs 53 ms), so the gain is real only for the recompile cost and disappears on an idle machine's best case. The cache is skipped when `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` is set.
- `destructive_guard.py` (the Bash PreToolUse hook) is now a small stub that runs the unchanged guard logic from `destructive_guard_core.py` out of the `__pycache__` bytecode cache. Python never caches the script it is started on, so the 2079-line file was recompiled on every tool call. The hook command, exit codes, `import destructive_guard` and `--selftest` are unchanged, and the stub blocks (exit 2) if the core cannot be loaded. A crash inside the core's `main()` also exits 2, with its own "guard crashed" message. 25 interleaved runs per arm on a loaded host (load average ~50), same payload, warm cache: minimum 64 ms to 42 ms, median 77 ms to 50 ms; reproduce with `python3 scripts/bench_hook_latency.py BEFORE.py AFTER.py` (the before copy comes from `git show <base>:<path>`). Where the skills directory is read-only or `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` is set, no cache is written and the cost is as before. Tests: `scripts/test_destructive_guard_stub.py`, `scripts/test_destructive_guard_stub_crash.py`.

### Changed
- CI now runs the `gates` workflow as parallel jobs (gate helper self-tests in three shards, documented gates, per-PR tests, live eval and scorer tests, and one job for the cheap steps) behind an aggregate job still named `gates`, cutting wall time from the sum of the steps to the slowest job. Every original step is kept with unchanged commands, and `scripts/test-ci-shards.sh` fails if an original step name is dropped; it checks step names only, not per-job membership or step bodies.

- `handback_cap.py` no longer counts blank lines or markdown link URLs toward the cap and keeps the three-block release valve. Test: `scripts/test_hook_friction.py`.
- `lane_resume_nudge.py` and `operating-discipline.md` now say a resumed lane's tool-call cap does not reset and a fresh lane is better for a large remainder.
- `tier_gate.py` fail-closed on a missing tiers file is pinned by test (clear message, exit 2, no FAIL line).

### Added
- Policy `lockfile_skip_review` (default `off`): with `on`, `review_gate.py check --audit-clean` skips the review lane for a lockfile-only PR.
- `testing-situational.md`: reproduce a flake under CPU throttling before calling it a flake.

### Added
- `install.sh --dry-run` installs into a throwaway empty directory and lists the files it would write, without touching the target. Every install now ends with a summary of the files written, split into vendored (skills, gate templates) and generated (AGENTS.md, commands, settings, the uninstall record).
- A bash 3.2 portability gate (`scripts/test-bash3-portability.sh`, with a planted-RED fixture) fails on bash-4-only constructs (`declare -A`, `mapfile`, `readarray`, `${var,,}`, `${var^^}`, `&>>`, `|&`, `coproc`) in shipped shell scripts. Lines may opt out with a `bash4-ok` comment. The scan found no real hits; two quoted-text false positives carry the marker.

### Changed
- install.sh adds the settings backups (`.claude/settings.local.json.bak.*`), the uninstall record (`.claude/.perun-install.json`) and `.perun/` to the target's `.git/info/exclude` (idempotent, never a tracked `.gitignore`), so they no longer show up as untracked files.

### Added
- Three owner rules are now default-on hooks in the operating layer. `reply_cap.py` (Stop and UserPromptSubmit) tells the agent every turn to reply in at most 3 lines and 500 characters, blocks an over-cap reply once per turn and appends a dated line to a counter log (`~/.cache/perun/reply-cap.log`). `decision_gate.py` (PreToolUse on `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode`) fails closed unless a decision record with `evil_twin:` and `council:` verdict lines (HOLD, REVISE or PASS_TO_USER) is under 30 minutes old in `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.perun/decisions/` (project-local and git-ignored so the Write tool can create it under sandbox or plan mode; the block message names the exact path; the gate writes a self-ignoring `.perun/.gitignore`; for `ExitPlanMode` the two lines may sit in the plan text itself); on Stop (argument `stop`, fails open on unparseable input) it also blocks a final sentence that asks the owner to decide in plain chat, once per turn, until a record exists; it checks the record exists, not its quality, and never gates Bash, Edit or merges. `handback_cap.py` now logs `narr_rate` per lane and sends a `systemMessage` when a lane wrote at least 100 estimated tokens of prose between tool calls (detect and measure, not prevention).
- `./install.sh --global-rules` copies those scripts to `~/.claude/perun-rules/` and idempotently merges their hooks into `~/.claude/settings.json` (backup first, existing hooks kept, needs `jq`; a 0-byte file counts as `{}`, a symlinked file is written through; `lane_liveness.py` is copied too so `handback_cap.py` runs from the global copy). See `docs/owner-rules.md`.

### Added
- `operating_selfcheck.py` now FAILs when the memory index (`MEMORY.md`) is over 150 lines or 20KB (the harness truncates it and the lessons at the tail are lost) and WARNs when the newest owner-facing status stamp (`.perun/last-status-update`, skipped if absent) or the handoff `handoff_inject.py` re-injects is older than 24h. `handoff_inject.py` prefixes a `STALE:` line to a handoff older than 24h. `operating-discipline.md` gains short memory and handoff hygiene doctrine (delete superseded handoffs, rotate long sessions daily, put regression guards at merge or train time).
