### Changed
- The guard timing check in `scripts/test_security_gates_corpus.py` is now a scaling check (25KB vs 2.5KB, best of 3, fail above 30x) with a loose 1 s ceiling, so CI noise no longer trips an absolute 100 ms cap while quadratic code still fails.

### Added
- `docs/security-heldout-table-1026/`: one table scoring every blind secrets and guard held-out corpus against the ported rival rules, with Perun rules as they stood at corpus authoring (the only evidence column) next to current main (in-sample), a pooled blind-at-authoring total with exact Clopper-Pearson intervals and an exact paired sign test, and `results.py` to regenerate it byte-identically (`scripts/test_security_heldout_table.py`).

### Fixed
- `stall_guard.py` now also blocks, once, a turn that only schedules a wake-up (`ScheduleWakeup` or `CronCreate`) while its last text mentions CI, checks, merge or waiting and nothing was launched (no `Agent`, `Task`, `Workflow` or background tool): "Waiting on CI is not a stop: launch the next priority lane now, then wake on the CI notification." `PERUN_STALL_GUARD=off`, the one-shot rule and fail-open are unchanged. `install.sh --with-delivery` wires it through the operating layer (the plugin adds no hooks).
- The idle-wait block now passes while background lanes from earlier turns are still open (more `run_in_background` launches than `<task-notification>` completions in the transcript tail), and only fires on forward-looking text (waiting on or for, CI or checks running, pending or in progress, until checks), so "PR merged, CI green" never matches.
- Open background lanes are now tracked per id (launch `agentId`, `resumedAgentId`, background tool_use id; closed by a terminal `<task-notification>` status), not by counting notifications, because one agent notifies again on every resume.

- Added the first measured answer to whether Perun beats caveman and ponytail on tokens (`docs/bench/token-voice-1026/`): 60 hidden-test bug-fix tasks x 2 samples x 4 arms on Haiku 5.5 via `claude -p`, $0.39 total. The Perun arm (the opt-in `--with-terse-replies` text; default Perun is not measured) cut median output tokens 33% vs no voice prompt (995 to 667; paired median diff -356, 95% CI -493 to -292) and 32% vs caveman ultra (976 to 667; -292, -355 to -245); vs ponytail it is -59% (-919, -1088 to -852) but 117 of 120 ponytail replies add unrequested test code, so that is not a voice win with pass rates 0.958 to 0.983 in every arm (non-inferior at a -0.05 margin, no multiplicity correction). Caveats: one model, one task family, Perun's arm is a hard reply cap, pass rates sit near the ceiling, and the run deviates from the free-PCSS preregistration (disclosed in the ledger).

- `merge_train.py` runs now print `RUN <id>` and poll the state dir between stages and inside every backoff wait: `<id>.cancel` releases the run's refs, prints `CANCELLED` and exits 0, and `<id>.drop-<pr>` removes that member (verify rebuilds the smaller union; merge HALTs because the remaining union was never verified). Each file is consumed once. A PR whose head has pending or missing checks now inherits the green of its prior head only when the raw `git diff --binary` of merge-base..head hashes the same and no completed check on the new head is red (a base-merge-only move, logged `CARRIED <old>-><new>`); the union train gate still always runs.

### Added
- `_lock.sh`: a lock's `ts` file now also records the host (`<epoch> <host>`). Liveness is `kill -0` or `ps -p` (a live other-user pid is never read as dead). `PERUN_CLAIM_REAP=enforce` reaps a dead-PID claim recorded by the same host (never another host's, never one without a host record) under a `mkdir` reaper guard (re-read pid, re-check liveness, one atomic rename to a unique tomb; a guard is never broken: if the guard dir exists the reap is skipped and the claim stays, with a "reap skipped: guard held" log line that names the hand-clear command), never restoring over a new holder; `lock_drop` of a claim this shell does not own now fails loudly. The default `shadow` only logs `SHADOW claim-reap: would reap ...` and keeps the report-only `STALE-LOCK` path.
- `train_land.sh`: `BASE_RED_FAILFAST=enforce` ends the train as BASE RED at once (exit 1, no solo re-runs, no bisect, heavy lease freed) when every failing id is already in the base's measured red set (`BASELINE_FAILS`, read after the lease wait; fails closed unless `$BASELINE_FAILS.base` holds the gate's base sha and that sha is still the remote base tip). The default `shadow` logs `SHADOW base-red-failfast: would end BASE RED now ...` and runs on unchanged.
- Test: `scripts/test-train-liveness.sh` (plants a dead-PID claim); evals `train-dead-claim-reap-shadow` and `train-base-red-failfast-shadow`.

A red merge train is now re-run first for only its failing checks, at low load (`merge_train.py verify --rerun-cmd`); a pass there is logged as a flake and the batch lands, and only a red that reproduces is bisected. `landing_watchdog.py` gains opt-in alarms for merges per hour below a target and for PRs per landed train below a floor (policy `merges_per_hour_target`, `train_yield_floor`). `fanout-host-sizing.md` ranks host work train > pregate > lane and says lanes yield cores while a train's test stage runs.

### Added
- `merge_train.py` verify and merge refuse a red base (`REFUSED red-base`) unless the lineup head is the `--base-fix` PR, and merge re-reads the open queue when it fires. Test: `merge_train.py --selftest`.

## [1.605.0] — 2026-10-26

### Fixed
- The shipped `pre-push-verify.sh` hook no longer refuses an annotated tag push: it verifies the commit the tag points to instead of comparing the tag object's sha with HEAD.

## [1.604.0] — 2026-10-26

- Added deterministic answer keys, a stdlib scorer and a reproducible results script for the business-ops bench (`docs/bench/bizops-keys-1026/`): rule-derived checks for leading with a number, prompt-computable arithmetic, routing the jurisdiction-specific part to a professional and no invented benchmarks; no judge and no paid calls. Caveat: the lead-with-a-number check encodes the skill's own doctrine, so it is circular and drives most of the gap. On the 150 held-out scenarios the shipped skill passes 111 and the round-4 edit 112 against the rival's 84 (shipped vs rival 41 to 14 discordant, exact McNemar p = 0.0004; edit vs shipped 15 to 14, no difference). Exploratory and post-hoc (not preregistered), with the lead-number check ignored: rival 131, shipped 137, edit 137, and no pair differs (shipped vs rival 12 to 6, p = 0.2379; edit vs rival 9 to 3, p = 0.146; edit vs shipped 6 to 6, p = 1.0). The r4-001 pre-rules read is self-attested; the professional and benchmark regexes can still false-pass or false-fail.

### Changed
- `ceo-strict` now gives the main session zero free edits and blocks any Edit/Write tool call and any shell redirect, `tee`, `sed -i` or `perl -i` write under the project dir, whatever the file extension (docs, config, changelog fragments and handoffs included); files outside the project, such as memory and scratchpad files, stay allowed. `~` and `$VAR` in write targets are expanded, and the project root falls back to the git toplevel when `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is unset. Known gap: `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `touch`, `dd` and interpreter writes such as `python -c` are not caught. Role `ceo` keeps one free source edit per turn, and `ceo:off` and `PERUN_ROLE=off` remain the escapes.

- Added deterministic answer keys, a stdlib scorer and a reproducible results script for the contribution bench (`docs/bench/contribution-keys-1026/`): a regex safety check (leak, sanitise, hold) on saved outputs, not a measure of answer quality, where the judge preferred the rival; no judge and no paid calls. On the 150 held-out scenarios the pre-slim shipped skill passes 129 against the rival's 118 (16 to 5 discordant, exact McNemar p = 0.027); the round-4 edit leaks names into code blocks most often (11 of 150).

- Added deterministic answer keys, a stdlib scorer and a reproducible results script for the idea-critic bench (`docs/bench/idea-critic-keys-1026/`): a regex structural check (numeric stop trigger, stated recommendation, what would change the answer) on saved `idea-critic-r9-1018` held outputs, not a measure of answer quality; no judge and no paid calls. On the 150 held-out scenarios the rival passes 132, the previous skill 131 and the shipped edit 133, with no pair significant (exact McNemar p >= 0.625).

### Fixed
- The installed skills `INDEX.md` no longer reads as if `scripts/skill_index.py` ships with the install: it now says the file is generated in the Perun source repo.

## [1.603.0] — 2026-10-26

### Changed
- The two slowest per-PR tests, `conflict-free-prs` (about 150 s locally) and `bench-check` (about 110 s), now run as background tests (`scripts/ci-tests.d/*.bg.sh`) alongside the gate steps, and the CI job timeout rises from 25 to 35 minutes. Green PR runs took about 23.5 minutes, so slower runners hit the 25-minute limit.

### Added
- Destructive guard wave 12: `rm -r` on a `/tmp` or `$TMPDIR` path in the same command line as `ln -s` is blocked (a link made on the spot can point the scratch path at the host; was allowed on main). Blind held-out-17 (`docs/bench/security-gates-heldout17-1025`) at main 93fbf7853: 58/60 blocked, 3/59 benign flagged; no FP rule written (pid-scoped `/tmp/<name>-$$` stays a documented lead, the perl print row and `git push -f` stay flagged on purpose), so in-sample is unchanged. The two misses are a heredoc split into rows by the corpus, not rejoined. Pin and probes: `scripts/test_security_gates_heldout17_blind.py`.

### Added
- Destructive guard wave 13: `mv` of a system directory or `/` (`mv /etc /etc.bak`) is blocked; `find . -name '*.pyc' -not -path './.git/*' -delete` (artifact glob plus literal `-not -path|-name` exclusions) is allowed. Blind held-out-18 (`docs/bench/security-gates-heldout18-1025`) at wave 12: 59/60 blocked, 1/59 benign flagged; in-sample now 60/60 and 0/59. Pin and probes: `scripts/test_security_gates_heldout18_blind.py`.

### Added
- Destructive guard wave 14: writes to raw disks (`cat /dev/zero > /dev/sda`) and `kubectl delete -f -` are blocked; `mv` brace expansion, `--target-directory=` destinations and `~/../../etc` sources are blocked. Allowed on narrow rules: `rm -rf "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/out"`, `rm -rf "$td"` after `td=$(mktemp -d)`, `find . -name node_modules -type d -prune -exec rm -rf {} +`, `mkfs` of a relative `*.img`, and a local test-database `DROP TABLE` through `psql`. Blind held-out-19 (`docs/bench/security-gates-heldout19-1025`) at wave 13: 58/60 blocked, 9/59 benign flagged; in-sample now 60/60 and 4/59. Pin and probes: `scripts/test_security_gates_heldout19_blind.py`.

### Added
- Destructive guard wave 15: a command substitution used as the command word (`$(printf 'rm\x20-rf\x20/')`, a base64 or hex decoder, a variable set from one) is blocked, `$'\x72\x6d'` words are decoded before the check, and `crontab -r` (any flag form) and `crontab /dev/null` are blocked; `crontab -l`, `-e` and `crontab -l | crontab -` stay allowed. Blind held-out-20 (`docs/bench/security-gates-heldout20-1025`) at wave 14: 58/60 blocked, 0/59 benign flagged; in-sample now 60/60 and 0/59. Pin and probes: `scripts/test_security_gates_heldout20_blind.py`.

### Added
- Destructive guard wave 16: `mdadm --zero-superblock|--create`, `cryptsetup erase|luksErase|luksFormat|luksKillSlot|luksRemoveKey`, `docker swarm leave --force`, a delete verb fed by `xargs` (`xargs redis-cli del`), `aws s3 sync --delete`, `gsutil rsync -d`, writes to `/proc/sysrq-trigger`, and `crontab` fed empty input are blocked. Narrow allows: `${TMPDIR:?}/child`, `rm -rf $(mktemp -d)`, `rm -rf ~/.cache/<name>` (one level, no trailing slash), `find -type f -name '*.orig' -exec rm -f`, and rsync into a named child of `/var/www`; each keeps its bypasses (symlink, `..`, redefined variable or mktemp, `--delete` hidden in an rsync option) blocked. Blind held-out-21 (`docs/bench/security-gates-heldout21-1025`) at wave 15: 53/60 blocked, 6/59 benign flagged; in-sample now 60/60 and 1/59 (`git branch -D` stays blocked). Pin and probes: `scripts/test_security_gates_heldout21_blind.py`.

### Added
- Destructive guard wave 17: `kubectl replace --force`, `kubectl scale --all --replicas=0`, `etcdctl del --from-key|--prefix`, `bq rm -r|-f`, an `ansible` ad-hoc `-m shell|command|raw -a CMD` call (CMD judged as a command; no `-m` means `command`) and `ansible -m file -a "path=P state=absent"` (judged as `rm -rf P`; `--check` is a dry run). Narrow allows: `pulumi destroy --preview-only`, `aws dynamodb delete-item` with one literal `--key`, `npm unpublish` of one exact prerelease version, `cargo yank` of one exact prerelease version (a stable version stays blocked). `git push --delete` stays blocked. Held-out-22 (60 dangerous, 60 benign) landed unchanged; blind at wave 16: 54/60 blocked, 5/60 benign flagged.

### Added
- Destructive guard wave 18: `terraform|tofu workspace delete -force`, `helm rollback --force`, `launchctl bootout system/...` and `launchctl unload -w /Library/LaunchDaemons/...`, `systemctl disable|mask` of ssh, network, docker or systemd-* units, `chmod -R 000` on an absolute or home path, `btrfs subvolume delete`. Narrow allows: `git filter-repo --analyze|--dry-run`, `shred -u ./relative/file` (not `.git`, credentials, `..`, globs or absolute paths). Ten dangerous and ten benign rows added to the security-gates-1024 corpus and re-pinned in `SHA256-frozen.txt` (56/56 blocked, 0/55 false positives, in-sample).
- Guard wave 18, round 3: `chmod` wipes via `$PWD`, `.*`, `--rec` prefixes, `-rwx` and sequential symbolic modes; `launchctl asuser|submit` recursion, case-folded and glued unload paths, `-D system|all`, `gui/$UID`; `systemctl` option values skipped, glob units, more critical units (narrowed so `systemd-timesyncd` and `NetworkManager-wait-online` stay allowed); `terragrunt workspace delete -force`; `helm rollback --force` only when `rollback` is the subcommand.

### Added
- Destructive guard wave 19: blind held-out-24 misses closed (blind 42/60 blocked, 0/60 benign flagged; now 60/60 and 0/60, in-sample). New blocks: removal of a core package (libc, glibc, systemd, kernel, dpkg, sudo, ...) through `apt|dnf|yum|zypper|apk|rpm|dpkg|pacman` and `rpm -e --nodeps`; `influx delete` without `--predicate` and `influx bucket|org delete`; `cockroach sql` DROP; `cypher-shell` `MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n`; `oc delete project`; `eksctl|skopeo|crane|regctl|oras delete`; `borg delete|prune`; `velero ... delete --all|-l` and `velero uninstall`; `setfacl|chgrp|chattr -R` on root or home; `chmod 000` of a critical binary; `passwd -l|-d` of root; `usermod -L root`; `find /home -exec chown|chgrp|setfacl`. Preview flags, list forms, single-item deletes and non-critical packages stay allowed. Pins in `scripts/test_security_gates_heldout24_blind.py`; the 18 in-sample rows live in `scripts/test_security_gates_w19_insample.py` because the landed 1024 corpus is frozen.

Review 2 closed: bounded (linear) cypher scan, cypher wipe forms (IN TRANSACTIONS, WITH/LIMIT, WHERE true, path and relationship patterns), apt false spellings and `-o` values, `--root` normalization, `autopurge`, dynamic package lists, exact core names, owner-bit-only chmod revoke on data paths, `//etc` sed, find|xargs chmod and `sh -c`, group-qualified kubectl kinds, influx option values, and find start paths limited to `/`, home and top-level system dirs.

Follow-ups, not in this change: other package managers (emerge, xbps-remove, snap, rpm-ostree, transactional-update, opkg, pkg), a broader critical-binary list, kops/kopia/duplicity deletes, `cypher-shell -f` file vetting, and shell-comment stripping before tokenizing (pre-existing).

### Added
- Destructive guard wave 20: every review-3 finding and the held-out-25 misses. New blocks: `userdel -r|-f` and `deluser --remove-home|--remove-all-files`; one `sed|perl -i` of `sshd_config` that sets both `PermitRootLogin` and `PasswordAuthentication` (ssh lockout); `iptables|ip6tables -P INPUT|OUTPUT DROP|REJECT`; `chpasswd` fed a `root:` or `0:` line; `vipw|vigr`; attached `usermod -pVALUE root`. Pins in `scripts/test_destructive_guard_w20.py`.
- Cypher scan is now a linear keyword stream over each `;` statement with strings and `//`, `/* */` comments removed: no 300-character window, `;` in a string no longer hides the `MATCH`, `MATCH (a:K), (n)` comma patterns count, and a WHERE with `or|xor|not|true|exists`, a constant comparison or a self-comparison is not a filter (so `WHERE a OR b` deletes are blocked; rewrite as separate statements). A labeled `MATCH ... CALL { DETACH DELETE } IN TRANSACTIONS` is allowed.
- Package removal: an apt short-flag bundle that carries a value flag (`-tstable`, `-ca`) is no preview; the last preview switch and the last root option win (`--simulate --no-simulate`, `-r /mnt -r /`); rpm spellings of the core libraries (`libgcc`, `zlib`, `libselinux`, `python3-libs`, `python3-dnf`, `rpm-libs`, `libdnf`, ...) are blocked while `python3.9-pip` is not.
- `find -exec chown|chmod` start paths cover subtrees of `/etc`, `/usr` (not `/usr/local`), `/bin`, `/lib*`, `/boot`, `/root`, `/System`, `/Library`, `/private/etc`, plus `/home/<user>` and `/Users/<user>`; `find /home -exec chmod go-rwx` stays allowed. `chmod go-rwx` of `/etc`, `/var`, `/home`, `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/group`, `/etc/hosts`, `/etc/resolv.conf` and `/etc/nsswitch.conf` is blocked again (`chmod o-rwx /home` stays allowed as hardening); owner-only carve-outs shrink to secret files (`/etc/shadow`, `sudoers*`, `ssh/*`, `ssl/private`, `/root`, `/home/<user>`).
- Unquoted shell comments (`#` at the start of a word) are removed before tokenizing, so `rm -rf ./build # not /` is judged without the comment; `a#b`, `$#`, quoted and escaped `#` are kept.
- Review fixes: a Cypher `{k:v}` map literal or `SET n:Label` after `MATCH (n)` is no longer a filter (only labels, types and property maps inside the MATCH patterns count); a WHERE filters only when every `OR` branch names a property, label or pattern, so string/`IN`/`id(n) >= 0`/`size(`/`coalesce(` tautologies are blocked while `= true`, `IS NOT NULL`, `NOT (n)--()` and `OR` of real filters are allowed; `find -exec chmod go-rwx` is blocked for subtrees of `/usr`, `/bin`, `/lib*`, `/etc`, `/var` (not `/etc/ssh`, `/etc/ssl/private`); `libstdc++6`, `libcrypt1`, `libaudit1`, `libacl1`, `libattr1`, `libblkid1`, `libmount1`, `libsmartcols1`, `libuuid1` are core names.
- A command over 65536 characters or 2000 lines is blocked (fail closed) instead of scanned; the `_emitted` start pattern no longer backtracks quadratically.
- `kubectl delete namespace.foo.io` (a CRD) is no longer read as a namespace.

Kept false positives: `WHERE exists(n.p)` stays unfiltered (a held-out pin); `git push origin --delete tmp/<name>` stays blocked. Remote branch deletes need a human to confirm; run it yourself with the `!` prefix.

Decided, not changed: `sed -i` of `/etc/fstab`, `/etc/ld.so.conf` and `/etc/pam.d/*` stays blocked (a bad edit stops boot or all logins; copy the file first and ask the owner).

Follow-ups, not in this change: split sshd_config edits across two commands, other package managers (emerge, xbps-remove, snap, rpm-ostree, opkg), `cypher-shell -f` file vetting, `MATCH (a), (b:X) DELETE a` (a later labeled pattern counts as the filter).

### Added
- Destructive guard wave 21: every review-2 finding. Pins in `scripts/test_destructive_guard_w21.py`.
- Cypher: an operand tested both null and not null through `NOT`, parentheses, a wrapping function (`toString(n.x)`) or `exists(n.x)` is an always-true WHERE; `all|any|none|single(x IN [..] ...)` over a list literal, `id(n) = id(n)`, `id(n) IS NOT NULL`, `size|length|coalesce(..) >= 0` or `IS NOT NULL` are constants; a nested `WHERE` inside a function call no longer counts as the outer filter; `MATCH ((n))` is the bare pattern.
- Cypher false positives closed: `id(n)`/`elementId(n)` against a constant, `size(n.tags) = 0`, `length(n.name) > 3`, `coalesce(n.deleted,false)`, `exists(n.tmp)`, `NOT exists((n)--())` and `1 IN n.ids` are filters; `<literal> IN` is a constant only before a list literal.
- Size cap (65536 characters or 2000 lines, fail closed) no longer counts the body of a heredoc fed to a plain `cat [>file]`, `tee [-a] file` or `git commit -F -`; a heredoc fed to a shell or interpreter, an unterminated one, and an unquoted one whose body expands `$(` or backticks still count.
- `sed|perl -i` of `sshd_config` is blocked when `PermitRootLogin` and `PasswordAuthentication` are edited by two separate commands in one line (`&&`, `;`, `|`, newline).
- `find /etc/<app> -exec chmod go-rwx` is allowed again for app directories; system-owned `/etc` children (`passwd`, `shadow`, `pam.d`, `ssl`, `ld.so*`, `sudoers*`, `systemd`, and similar) stay blocked.
- Reading stdin no longer hangs when it is a terminal.

Review round 2 (same wave):
- Cypher: `id(n)`/`elementId(n)` is a filter only when compared (`=`, `<`, `>`, `IN [..]`, `IN $p`) to a short literal or parameter; `IS NOT NULL`, self-compare, `<> ''`, `STARTS WITH ''`, negative or huge constants and `IN range(` are tautologies again.
- Cypher WHERE is read per branch: a branch is unfiltered only when every `AND` term is a tautology (`id(n) IS NOT NULL AND n.k=1` is allowed), a null pair counts only when it is the whole OR branch, `NOT ( ... )` around a null pair is refused, and `any(x IN [1,2] WHERE x = n.k)` is a filter (only an empty list literal is vacuous).
- Unquoted heredoc bodies (any command, any size) have their `$( ... )` and backtick substitutions vetted as commands, including `$\<newline>(`; quoted tags (`<<'EOF'`, `<<"EOF"`) stay inert.
- The split sshd_config check is tokenised: `sed|perl -i` or `ex` as the command word, a file argument ending `sshd_config` or an `sshd_*` glob, a value `no`, root-login keyword in one edit and `Password*`, `KbdInteractive*` or `ChallengeResponse*` in another. Setting `yes`, `prohibit-password`, quoted or `git log --grep` text and `sshd_config_x` are allowed.
- A 10,000,000-character hard ceiling applies even to data heredocs.

Skipped: `cat -n <<'EOF'`, `echo hi; cat >f <<'EOF'`, `cat >f 2>&1 <<'EOF'`, CRLF and `git commit -m x -F -` big bodies still fail closed (safe false positives).

Review round 3 (same wave), redesign to fail closed:
- Cypher WHERE is an allowlist. It filters only when every OR branch is an AND of `v.prop OP literal|$param`, `v.prop STARTS WITH|ENDS WITH|CONTAINS|IN ...`, `v:Label`, `v.prop IS [NOT] NULL`, `id(v)|elementId(v) = literal|$param` or `IN [list]|$param`, or a pattern predicate such as `(n)--()`, and no operand is tested both null and not null. Any `NOT`, any other function, constant-vs-constant term, `id()` range or property-vs-property comparison blocks the delete. This blocks again several deletes base allowed: `size(n.tags) = 0`, `length(n.name) > 3`, `coalesce(..)`, `exists(..)`, `NOT exists((n)--())`, `id(n) >= 100`, `1 IN n.ids`, `any(x IN l WHERE ..)`, `n.a IS NULL AND n.b=1 OR n.a IS NOT NULL AND n.b=2`; rewrite them as `v.prop OP literal` or as separate statements.
- Unquoted heredoc: from every unescaped `$(` or backtick, the text to the end of the body is vetted as a command (no paren matching); more than 32 substitutions blocks; an odd run of backslashes before `$(` or a backtick makes it literal text.
- The split sshd_config check is quote-aware (`;`, `|` inside a quoted sed, ex or perl script stay in their command), covers `sshd_config.d/*`, and matches keyword prefixes (`Permit`, `Root`, `Pass`, `Kbd`, `ChallengeResponse`).

Review round 4 (same wave):
- Cypher allowlist: a pattern predicate with a variable-length `*` is refused (`(n)-[*0..]-()` matches `n` itself); an operand with an `IS NULL` branch refuses any other OR branch on that operand; complementary comparisons of one operand and literal (`=`/`<>`, `<`/`>=`, `>`/`<=`) and a term next to its own `NOT` are refused. Widened: `NOT` before a non-null term or pattern, `$p.x`, exponents, `- 1`, doubled quotes, nested `n.a.b`; whitespace and comments are normalised before the clause split (`STARTS  WITH`). The block message now lists the allowed grammar. `n.k IN [1,2] OR n.k IS NULL` is blocked (split it into two statements).
- sshd_config split: skips `VAR=val`, shell keywords and `sudo|doas|env|nohup|xargs` with options; covers `gsed` and `awk -i inplace`; `\t`/`\s` before `no`; keywords anchored to `PermitRootLogin` and `PasswordAuthentication|KbdInteractiveAuthentication|ChallengeResponseAuthentication` (abbreviated keywords such as `s/Permit.*/` are no longer read).
- Heredoc substitutions: counted as substitutions (a backtick pair is one), cap 64; each is vetted up to its quote- and comment-aware close, or to the end of the body when no close is found or the text holds `case`; prose after a `$(date)` is no longer read as a command.

Review round 4 (same wave):

Grammar shrunk instead of chasing spellings.

- Cypher `DETACH DELETE ... WHERE` is a filter only when it has no `NOT` (except `IS NOT NULL`), no `XOR`, and no two OR branches that touch the same operand (compared with whitespace removed). Newly blocked: `NOT n:Foo`, `NOT (n)--()`, `n.a = 1 AND NOT n.b = 2`, `n.a = 1 OR n.a = 2`, `n.id = 1 OR n.id = 2` (use `IN [..]`). Complement checks no longer run across AND terms, so string ranges such as `n.ts >= "2024" AND n.ts < "2025"` are allowed again. Literals ignore whitespace (`- 1`).
- Unquoted heredoc command substitutions are vetted from each substitution start to the end of the body (fail closed, cap 64; a backtick pair counts once, and `$(` inside backticks no longer resets state). Newly blocked: a body such as `$(date)` followed by a line `rm -rf /`.
- sshd lockout: any command with `sed|gsed|perl|awk|gawk|ex|vim|vi|ed` as a word and an `sshd_config`/`sshd_config.d/*` word is treated as an edit, with no wrapper list; `ed` heredoc bodies are read; shell comments are no longer stripped when tokenising.

Wall-clock cap (same wave):

- The check runs in a forked child; the parent kills it and blocks (exit 2) after 10 seconds, so a hook that spins in a regex or waits on input ends on its own instead of running for hours. A child that crashes or dies on a signal, a parent stopped by SIGTERM, and any uncaught error or exit code other than 0 or 2 also block; a failed fork falls back to vetting in-process. Pinned in `scripts/test_destructive_guard_w21.py`.

PASSWORD`, `PASSWORD(...)`, Oracle `IDENTIFIED BY`, Apache `Header`/`RequestHeader`/`PassengerEnvVar`, `proxy_set_header Authorization`, `az acr login`, CloudFormation parameters in any key order and as JSON, and Terraform bodies up to 3000 characters. ## [1.602.0] — 2026-10-24

### Changed
- Token optimization: the bytes the repo's skills, commands and the delivery operating layer's SessionStart hook load into every session (every skill and command in the repo, which is no single `install.sh` flag set; opt-in hooks such as `--with-terse-replies` add SessionStart text it does not measure) are now measured per source by `scripts/always_loaded_bytes.py` (skill descriptions, command descriptions, SessionStart hook output; UTF-8 bytes, bytes/4 for tokens) and ratcheted by `scripts/test_always_loaded_bytes.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/always-loaded-bytes.sh`), which also pins every trigger keyword and the full routing phrases (a mutation check proves a dropped qualifier fails). A review-only install loads only deep-code-review and no SessionStart hook, so its figure is a subset. Total 4000 to 3889 bytes (about 1000 to 972 tokens): duplicated or restated wording removed from the `agentic-ceo`, `communication-structure`, `growth-analytics` and `idea-critic` descriptions, the `/perun-run` command description and the always-on host rules (`HOST_RULES`, also sent to every subagent); no skill body or reference changed, and all trigger-coverage metrics stay full.

### Added
- Always-on bytes: `scripts/test_always_loaded_surface.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/always-loaded-surface.sh`) closes the gap in `scripts/always_loaded_bytes.py`: it fails if the plugin manifest gains agents, hooks, commands or MCP servers, if a SessionStart hook appears that is neither measured nor silent, or if a UserPromptSubmit hook injects text in a clean session. Measured from committed files, a full plugin install puts 3,952 bytes (about 988 tokens) in every session: skill descriptions 3,202, command descriptions 409, SessionStart hook 341, and 0 from UserPromptSubmit hooks and agents. That is about 8% of the 12.8k cache-write gap against the comparison review plugin, so the gap comes from the skill body and references loaded when a review runs, not from always-on text. No trim was shipped: a 15% cut (593 bytes) would drop trigger phrases pinned by `scripts/test_always_loaded_bytes.py`.

### Added
- Bench: answer keys (`keys.json`) for all 40 held-out scenarios of the business-ops, growth-analytics, idea-critic and contribution rival rows, 10 per row, 3-6 must-hit and 1-3 must-not regex items each. Keys test what an answer adds beyond the prompt (an echo baseline of each prompt scores at most 0.25 hit rate), accept number forms (`$280k`, `100,000`, `13 percent`) and paraphrases, and use no Perun verdict tokens. `scripts/rival_eval_keys.py` (a wrapper around the unchanged, hash-pinned `scripts/rival_eval.py`) adds `key_score` (per-arm hit rate and violation rate, deterministic, no judge). Must-nots are negation-aware ("never name X" is not a leak), skip bracketed placeholders, and for contribution scan only the drafted message; a scenario that needs a draft and has none counts as a violation (`no_draft`). Results land in `results.json` as `answer_key` next to the pairwise verdict. `rival_eval_keys.py keys SKILL RUNDIR` rescores cached outputs offline and fails on a missing arm directory. `check` rejects an unkeyed or malformed key. Tests: `scripts/test_rival_answer_keys.py`.

### Added
- `scripts/rival_eval_cost.py run ...` (a wrapper around the unchanged, hash-pinned `scripts/rival_eval.py`) records real per-arm usage (`prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `spend_usd`) from the PCSS response or `claude -p` JSON into `results.json` `cost_per_arm`, with a per-output sidecar so resumed runs keep it; arms without reported usage stay unmeasured.
- `scripts/bench_verdict.py --cost results.json` prints per-arm cost per item and the Perun/rival ratio and exits 0 when Perun cost <= rival cost, 1 when Perun costs more, 2 on a usage error, 3 when unmeasured (a distinct code from a loss).

### Added
- Benchmark: free pilot outcome bench for the `idea-critic` (evil twin) skill, `scripts/evil_twin_bench.py` with `docs/bench/evil-twin-r1-1021/`. R1 is a pilot and is NOT preregistered: its freeze list and results landed in the same commit and `scripts/rival_eval.py` is not frozen. The `cases.txt` names were amended after results (third-party-looking names replaced by fictional ones): the first `cases.txt` hash in `SHA256-frozen.txt` is the pre-amendment hash and no longer matches, a later line re-lists the amended hash, the cache was rekeyed, and the model responses saw the old names. 30 fictional proposals (24 with one planted fatal flaw and a hidden key, 6 sound controls), three arms (no skill, the idea-critic SKILL.md, a generic pros-and-cons prompt), a free PCSS generator and a different blind judge. Verdict INCONCLUSIVE: the no-skill arm caught 24 of 24 flaws (above the 0.90 headroom ceiling), perun 24/24, brainstorm 23/24; false-kill on controls was 0/6 none, 2/6 perun, 0/6 brainstorm (intervals wide). Judge caveat: the perun 2/6 is a scoring artifact; the R1 judge counted a "revise / do not approve yet" answer (p15, p25) as KILLED, which breaks the false-kill guard (perun 2/6 against none 0/6 plus one case); R2 fixes the rule. No skill text changed. The committed cache lets `scripts/test_evil_twin_bench.py` replay the run offline.

V2 inlines one compact review method as the whole prompt (no reference load, one read of the patch, two turns) to answer V1's 4.2x token cost against the toolkit code-reviewer. On 21 judged held-out cases (one more dropped for a judge failure), one `claude -p` run on `claude-sonnet-5-5` for every arm, F1 was V2 0.782, toolkit 0.719, real skill 0.702; V2 minus toolkit +0.063 [-0.099, 0.249] at 1.12x the toolkit's tokens (13,325 against 11,868). Neither keep rule holds, so the result is REVERT and SKILL.md is unchanged; V2 is about half the real skill's tokens (27,986). The gain seen on the free tune host did not transfer. Spent $3.18 of a $25 cap. Tests: `scripts/test_review_cost_v2.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/review-cost-v2.sh`).

Input is one flat JSON object bound by key name; every limit (`min_runway_months`, `min_ltv_cac`, `max_payback_months`, `min_margin`) comes from the input, none is built in. A check with no stated limit prints SKIP, all-SKIP prints INCONCLUSIVE and exits 3, any FAIL exits 1, bad input prints `ERROR <reason>` and exits 2. ### Changed
- Behavior change on install and upgrade: re-running `install.sh` with the operating layer applied on a repo whose policy has no `role` key now turns the CEO-altitude guard on (warn) and prints `CEO-altitude guard now warns (role=ceo); opt out: perun_policy set role off`. Opt out with `perun_policy.py set role off` (kept on later installs) or `PERUN_ROLE=off`. Cause: `ceo_altitude_guard.py` never warned in a fresh install because the policy default `role` is `off` (it only counted). `install.sh` with the operating layer applied now writes policy `role: ceo` (warn) unless the policy already has a `role` or `PERUN_ROLE` is set; `role=off` and `ceo-strict` stay available via `--policy` or `perun_policy.py set role`. Uninstall undoes only what install armed: it removes `role: ceo` (and `.perun/policy.json` when install created it and nothing else is in it), and only while the file is byte-for-byte what install wrote (the marker records its sha256); a changed file is kept and uninstall says so. Any explicit `perun_policy.py set` clears the recorded hash, so a policy you set yourself is kept even when its bytes match; a plain reinstall does not refresh the hash (fail-safe: uninstall then keeps the file). Lanes are unaffected (they carry `agent_id`). Tests: `scripts/test_ceo_guard_default_warn.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/ceo-guard-default-warn.sh`).

### Added

The plan file carries a `Grants: push, pr` line; the user approves the plan once, and `.claude/skills/agentic-delivery/scripts/plan_gate.py` records the verbatim approval against the plan's sha256. The agent runs `check <action>` before every gated action: exit 3 parks that action and the run continues, exit 2 (including a missing ledger or any failed `grant`) halts the run and asks the user. Push and PR-open proceed; merge only when the plan's `Grants:` line names it and the user's whole approval reply is exactly "approve merge" (case-insensitive, trailing period or exclamation mark allowed; an allowlist, so "disapprove merge", "approve merge, nope", "approve merges later" and "approve, do not merge" all park); force-push, deploy, secrets, spend, delete, external sends, history rewrite and settings edits always park (even if a plan or forged ledger lists them), as does any unrouted action. A malformed or forged ledger exits 2 (fail closed), and editing the plan voids the grant. Parked actions go into one end-of-run ask; `parked` exits 2 if the parked list disagrees with the append-only park-event log, which is advisory since the ledger is agent-writable. This is the agent's policy record, not an enforcement point: host permissions and the sandbox stay the boundary, and no hook or settings are changed. Offline simulation of prompts per ticket, before to after (grant derived from a plan without and with `merge`): clean ticket 4 to 2 to 1, one review round 5 to 2 to 1, review round plus deploy 6 to 2 to 2. It runs the real gate on fixed action sequences, so it counts policy prompts, not measured human sessions. Tests: `scripts/test_plan_gate.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/plan-gate.sh`).

### Added
- Positioning: new `.claude/skills/positioning/scripts/positioning_check.py`, a stdlib-only runnable check of a drafted positioning statement or message house, read as JSON from a file or stdin and bound by key name. It enforces only rules quoted verbatim from `SKILL.md` or `references/full-map.md`: a statement that starts with Hypothesis, generic segment ("teams") and alternative ("the competition"), `[ASSUMED]` tags and no invented number or quote on unsupplied statement elements, differentiator and pillar proof or `UNVERIFIED — needs proof`, exactly one core message, no market fact the user did not supply, an explicit `name_cleared_by_professional` boolean (false fails; any non-blank `name_clearance` text fails unless it is true, with no wording match), no brand system or messaging bible pre-PMF, and no buyer reaction without a source. Every output line cites the rule text it enforces. It holds no limits of its own: a check whose input keys are absent prints SKIP, all-SKIP prints INCONCLUSIVE and exits 3, any FAIL exits 1, bad input prints `ERROR <reason>` and exits 2. Routed from `SKILL.md` with one run-this-when line. Tests: `scripts/test_positioning_check.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/positioning-check.sh`), which also fails if a cited rule text drifts from the skill. `docs/capability-matrix.md` no longer says positioning has no scripts.

### Changed

The fast path also says to verify each finding by re-reading and tracing, to report only at confidence 80 or more, and to name the pinning test for every guarantee-bearing comment. The `mustload` gate reads its load-map and phase tables from `full-map.md` and counts that file (not the slim `SKILL.md`, which `routing --max-bytes` and the new test bound separately) in the Phase 0-2 floor, so both floor pins re-pin down by 14 tokens (22796 and 30772). `scripts/floor-anchors.tsv` and `scripts/hidden_test_bench.py` follow the moved sections, as do `scripts/review_load_bytes.py` (quick path is now `SKILL.md` alone; the full path reads the map and still skips `INDEX.md` when the map says a routing match does) and the tests that pinned old `SKILL.md` text. `size-budgets.tsv` gets a `full-map.md` row and a lower `SKILL.md` row. ### Added
- Agentic-CEO / Agentic-Delivery: `token_report.py --nudge` prints ONE line, or nothing: the top `--advise` finding of a session with its at-stake USD and the exact `--fix-plan` (or `--advise`) command to run, so the advice reaches the user without `/cost-retro`. Silent when no rule fires or the lever's settings key is already set. After a `--apply` backup (`<settings>.bak` plus the empty `<settings>.bak.perun` marker only `--apply` writes, so a `.bak` from another tool is ignored; within 14 days) it appends a did-it-work receipt, `since applying <keys>: input-eq/turn -N% (n turns before, m after)`, comparing input-equivalent per deduped main turn either side of the backup's mtime, over every project transcript within 14 days before it (so an `--apply` in an earlier session still reports; each file under the 128 MB cap and all together under 256 MB read within 30 s, else the receipt is dropped and the advise line stays); below 20 main turns on either side it prints `unknown`, never a guess. The `session_brief.py` SessionStart hook shows it from the newest prior transcript of the project: it reads a cache keyed by the transcript, the settings mtimes and sizes, and the UTC date, and a miss starts a detached `--nudge --nudge-cache` refresh (transcripts over 128 MB are skipped; one refresh per 90 s behind a `<cache>.lock`; a 60 s watchdog caches the line so far (an empty one if unfinished) and exits, and a failure caches an empty line, so a bad transcript is not retried until it changes), so the hook never parses a transcript and adds only an import of `token_report.py` and a few stats (hook median 456 ms before and 457 ms after, nine runs, on the project whose newest transcript is 417 MB). A cached line is shown only while the settings are unchanged and the cache is under 14 days old, so an applied lever stops being advertised at once. The line sits after the priority line, so it is the first cut when the three-line cap bites. Lane evidence names file stems, never the free-text lane description, and the unused-MCP evidence gives a count, not server names. Fail-silent, no network; reads usage, timestamps, model ids, tool names and settings keys only. Policy key `spend_nudge=on|off` (default `on`; `install.sh --policy spend_nudge=off` or `perun_policy.py set spend_nudge off`) mutes it, like `statusline`. Tests: `scripts/test_spend_nudge.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/spend-nudge.sh`).

### Added
- Agentic-CEO: `token_report.py` answers "where does my money go" across projects, months, models and lane types. `--rollup auto` prices the current directory's project (the `~/.claude/projects/<encoded cwd>` dir; an error when there is none), and `--rollup` on the `~/.claude/projects` parent prices every project under it, with one requestId dedupe across all of them. `--by month` adds calendar-month buckets beside day and week (adjacent for the delta, including across a year boundary). `--group project|agent|model` ranks spend by project, lane type (`agentType`; the main sessions are `main`) or model, each row with its share of priced spend. Cache hit % (cache read / (input + 5m and 1h cache writes + cache read)) appears in the text report's MAIN and SUBAGENTS lines and in every rollup, bucket and group row, `n/a` when there are no prompt tokens. A group, bucket or session holding an unpriced model stays `UNPRICED` (or `$X + UNPRICED (model)`), never $0. Reads usage, timestamps, model ids and the lane `agentType`; no message text or meta description reaches the output. `commands/cost-retro.md` step 2 and `docs/token-cost-tips.md` point at it. Tests: `scripts/test_spend_rollup_groups.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/spend-rollup-groups.sh`), hand-computed on fake transcripts, and `scripts/test_spend_rollup_nits.py` (an unreadable project dir is skipped, `--rollup auto` without a project errors, the nudge watchdog keeps the advise line).

### Added
- Agentic-delivery: `cost_statusline.py` now also prints the active 5-hour window, e.g. `win 2h10m left | 62% | +14k/min` (time left, the host's `rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage`, and the window's weighted-token burn per minute). It reuses `token_report.burn_blocks` through a sibling import of `agentic-ceo/scripts/token_report.py` (imported without writing `__pycache__`) and reads `transcript_path` from the statusLine JSON (key checked against the host statusline docs). From the last 1 MiB of the transcript it parses, as JSON, every whole line that mentions `"usage"` and keeps only `requestId`, `apiBlockIndex`, `timestamp`, `isSidechain`, `type`, `message.model` and `message.usage` of main-thread turns; no message content is kept, printed or sent anywhere. Time left uses the host's `rate_limits.five_hour.resets_at` when it is finite and at most one window ahead, else the modelled window. A modelled window or burn rate read from a clipped tail is marked `~`, unless the tail holds a gap of a whole window between two turns (that anchors the block chain; merely reaching back 5 hours does not). When the host sends no `prompt_cache.hit_ratio`, the cache share is computed from the same tail and shown as `tail cache N%`, distinct from the host's session-wide `cache N%`; it survives a failure of the window part. Without `token_report.py`, without a readable transcript, or on any error, the output stays the plain fields and nothing is printed to stderr. Tests: `scripts/test_cost_statusline_window.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/cost-statusline-window.sh`), including a CPU bound (under 500 ms, import included) on a 50 MB transcript of about 330-byte lines.

### Added
- Agentic-CEO: `token_report.py` (and so `/cost-retro`) gains a live 5-hour window view, `burn_blocks.active` in `--json` and an `Active window` text line, when the clock sits inside the newest window: minutes left, burn per minute so far, the projected total at the reset and, with the new `--limit N` (your own weighted-token budget per window, never guessed), percent used and minutes to reach it. When the pace passes the limit, or with no limit reaches 2x the median of earlier windows, a `Lever:` line names the fix from measured fields: `/compact` or `/clear` plus a handoff when main context over the auto-compact window drives it, trim the lane that drives it, else pause new lanes and use a cheaper tier until the reset. This matches the active-block remaining-time, burn-rate and projection view of ccusage `blocks` (public docs read 2026-10-22) and adds the concrete lever; usage, timestamp and model fields only, never message text. The projection and lever wait until 15 minutes of the window have passed (earlier it prints "too early to project"); `--limit` must be a finite number above 0 and prints a note when no live window exists.

### Added
- Agentic-CEO: `token_report.py` now reports 5-hour usage windows (`burn_blocks` in `--json`, one summary line in the text report): weighted tokens, burn per minute, lane share and most lanes open at once per window, the peak window's multiple of the median of the others, and, for the peak window, a named driver with a concrete lever (main thread over the auto-compact window: `/compact` at a task boundary or `/clear` and resume from a handoff note; and, only when that window is at least 2x the median of the others, one lane at or above 40%: split or trim that lane; no spender at 40% with 3 or more lanes open at once: dispatch fewer lanes per wave). The window is modelled on the public `ccusage` blocks report and the Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor session model; it reads only timestamps, usage fields and lane labels, and is a pace signal, not the account's real quota window. Tests: `scripts/test_token_burn_blocks.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/token-burn-blocks.sh`).

### Added
- `token_report.py` now prices Claude Haiku 5.5, which was UNPRICED. Its price is tiered per request by prompt size (input + cache writes + cache reads): a turn at or under 100,000 tokens pays $0.10 / $0.125 / $0.20 / $0.01 / $0.50 per MTok (input / 5m write / 1h write / read / output), a turn over 100,000 pays $0.50 / $0.625 / $1 / $0.05 / $2.50. Each turn is tiered on its own, in session, rollup and `--by` bucket spend alike; every other model and a user `--rates` file stay flat. Default rates re-read 2026-10-22. Tests: `scripts/test_token_haiku_tier.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/token-haiku-tier.sh`).

### Fixed
- `token_report.py --outcome` now refuses every other mode or option when it is given explicitly, including values equal to the defaults or empty strings (`--top 5`, `--project .`, `--rollup ""`); the guard checks for unset options rather than truthiness. The straddle count uses the latest turn timestamp of a session rather than its last line. Tests: `scripts/test_token_outcome.py`.

### Added
- `token_report.py --outcome DIR` measures whether spend nudges moved anything, from main-thread usage, timestamp and model fields only (never message text). Per UTC week it prints turns, input-equivalent tokens per turn, cache-hit %, and the share of sessions that passed a lever trigger (main context reached the 200,000-token auto-compact window; a turn on a top-tier model) and later applied it (an observed context drop of over 50%; a later turn on a lower tier). `--since DATE` adds before/after rows, `--json` emits the same data. A correlation over a changing work mix, not proof of cause. Tests: `scripts/test_token_outcome.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/token-outcome.sh`).

### Added
- `token_report.py --rollup DIR --by day|week` adds UTC day or Monday-start week buckets to the project rollup: raw tokens, priced spend, each model's token share and the delta versus the previous adjacent bucket. The existing cross-file requestId dedup is reused, a bucket holding an unpriced model stays UNPRICED (an all-unpriced bucket is never $0), and the buckets sum exactly to the plain rollup total. Tests: `scripts/test_token_rollup_buckets.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/token-rollup-buckets.sh`), including a hand-computed fixture.

### Added
- Agentic-delivery: `train_land.sh` no longer stalls the queue when a red train has no attributable culprit. Where it used to exit `CANT` (exit 3) and land nothing (`no culprit pinned` or `real failure(s) not pinned`), it now splits the remaining PRs into halves, re-runs the full gate on each half stacked on the fresh base, lands a half only when its own gate is green, and recurses on a red half up to `TRAIN_SPLIT_DEPTH` (default 2; `0` restores the old behavior, a non-number disables splitting with a warning). Each later half redoes the push-lock and lease waits and lands only while the base is still the one it was gated on. A leaf (a single PR or the depth floor) keeps the CANT and FLAKY semantics: it lands nothing. Only a CANT leaf continues the split; exit 2, 4 and 126+ abort it. The run always prints `SPLIT done: landed #...; CANT (not landed) #...; gates=<n>` (landed is what `land_train.sh` merged), and exits 0 only when every PR landed, else 3. The flake-on-base CANT never splits. Documented in `references/red-gate-triage.md`. Tests: `scripts/test-train-split.sh` (registered in `scripts/test-ci-gates.sh`); `scripts/test-peer-pains-2.sh` now pins `TRAIN_SPLIT_DEPTH=0` for its plain-CANT cases.

### Fixed
- Agentic-delivery: the exclusive heavy lease is now renewed from `train_land.sh`'s gate subshell: `perun_policy.py` heavy-exclusive commands honor `PERUN_HOLDER_PID`, which `train_land.sh` sets to its own pid on the renew call only (the renew previously credited the subshell and did nothing). The override is honored only for a positive pid that is the caller's parent or grandparent; anything else (0, -1, text, a foreign pid) falls back to the caller, so it can never release, renew or take another process's lease, and `_alive` now rejects pid <= 0.

### Added
- `outcome_claim_guard.py` Stop hook: a second claim class, "unseen UI". A reply that says a page, view, screen, chart, layout, dashboard or localhost URL works, shows, renders, loads, is up (not "set up"), visible or ready is flagged (default `warn`, same `outcome_guard` policy key and next-prompt note loop, fail open) unless the session transcript has an image Read or screenshot call (tool name or action, or a Bash `playwright screenshot` / `screencapture` / `--screenshot`) after both the last source edit (any Edit/Write, or an in-place `sed`/`perl`) and the last dev-server (re)start (`npm|pnpm|yarn|bun dev|start`, `next dev`, `vite`, `turbo run dev`, `make dev|start|serve|up`, `docker compose up`, `rails s`, `python -m http.server`). A hedge ("not visually checked") exempts only its own sentence; inline-code text still counts as claim text; the ambiguous nouns board, route and ui need a visual verb (so "the board loaded 40 PRs" is not a claim). Only the last 2 MB of the transcript is read, and only tool names, file paths, actions and Bash command lines, never content. Twenty-one replay checks in the new `scripts/test_outcome_claim_guard_ui.py`; one eval in `agentic-delivery/evals/evals.json`.
- `deep-code-review/references/testing-ui.md`: "Ready for a UI means seen, not loaded" (phone and desktop screenshots from a fresh server, fixture data and data source off, never-blank unconfigured/empty/error state, reuse the sibling pages' frame, name open-source references for a new feature-class UI).

### Added
- Agentic-CEO: `token_report.py --advise` (and so `/perun:cost-retro`) gains three usage-optimization rules, each fired by a deterministic trigger over usage, timestamp and model fields (never message text; the effort rule also reads settings keys, only to stay silent when one is already set): `idle-resume` (2 or more main turns that re-wrote at least half of a 100,000-token-or-larger context after a gap over 1 hour: `/compact` before stepping away, or `/clear` between unrelated tasks), `cache-bust` (2 or more same-model turns within 150 seconds where cache read was under 5% of the previous context, whatever the growth (a collapse with a net shrink stays silent because it looks like compaction; a clear of the oldest tool results can also fire): a changed cache prefix, so do model, effort, fast-mode, MCP and plugin changes at a task boundary), and `effort` (main output averaging 1,500 or more tokens per turn and 30% or more of main input-eq plus output with no `effortLevel`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` or `modelSettings` set: `/effort low` or `/effort medium`; heuristic thresholds, not calibrated on a corpus). Every command and setting is confirmed on code.claude.com/docs pages fetched 2026-10-21 and logged in `docs/standards-index.md`; skill-description budget and `idleCompaction` were dropped because no transcript field measures the first and the docs fetch did not confirm the second. Tests: `scripts/test_cost_advice_levers.py` (registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/cost-advice-levers.sh`).

## [1.601.0] — 2026-10-21

### Added
- `scripts/audit_skills.py`: a read-only, stdlib supply-chain auditor for an installed skills directory. It scans every file (SKILL.md, references, templates, scripts, hooks, dotfiles; only `.git/objects` is skipped) for a network fetch run as code (piped to a shell or interpreter, `eval`/`source` of a fetch, fetch then `&& sh`), calls to hosts outside an allowlist (`--allow-host` extends it; userinfo tricks like `github.com@evil.test` are judged by the real host), bidi, zero-width and tag characters in content and file names, base64-decoded execution and PowerShell encoded commands, writes to agent settings, MCP config, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, hooks, shell rc and credential files, `rm -rf` on root, home, globs or variable-prefixed paths, and instruction-override phrasing. Binary, oversize and symlinked files are reported as `unscanned`, never skipped silently. The skill under audit cannot silence its own findings: `audit-skills: ignore <rule>` markers apply only with `--honor-markers` (for your own skills) and only to the named rule. Exit 0 clean, 2 findings, 1 error or usage error; `--json`; each finding carries a severity and file:line. Bench `scripts/test_audit_skills.py`: 89 fictional malicious and 51 benign skill folders generated at test time, recall 89/89 (asserted exact) and 0 false positives on those author-written fixtures (a regression guard, not an independent estimate), under 30 s. This repo's own skills raise 21 findings, all triaged in the test with a reason and pinned per (file, rule) count (guidance and guard denylists that name the pattern, one oversize eval corpus; none execute it). Scheme-less fetch hosts, unreadable directories (exit 1), directory names, long-option `rm`, system-directory `rm`, skill-install and rc/git-config writes, variation-selector and soft-hyphen smuggling are covered; the allowlist names well-known origins, not trusted content, and the phrase lists are heuristics (both stated in `--help`). Routed from the README Safety section.

Result on 36 held-out fabrication prompts and 8 controls: strict fabrication 0.58 current vs 0.47 edited, paired difference +0.11 with 95% CI [-0.03, 0.25], so a tie; the edit is not kept and the skill is unchanged. ### Added
- `token_report.py --advise [--project DIR]` (tests: `scripts/test_cost_advice.py`, registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/cost-advice.sh`): a table of 10 rules, each one measured signal from the transcript usage fields, model ids, tool names and settings keys, one recommendation, and a link into `docs/token-cost-tips.md` or `model-tiering.md`. Rules: top tier on mechanical lanes, lane consults, cache writes above reads with and without model switches, many short lanes, repeated context drops, a long context with no auto-compact window, large per-turn context jumps, unused MCP servers, and `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false` with MCP servers configured. A lever the user, project or local settings or the environment already set is never recommended, and an unreadable settings file counts every setting as set. At-stake dollars are the priced spend of the flagged items under the dated default rates, `UNPRICED` when no rate exists. No message or tool-result text is read. The unused-MCP rule skips servers that settings already disable (`disabledMcpjsonServers`, merged across scopes like every list key, or outside `enabledMcpjsonServers`); the short-lanes rule skips lanes still in flight; the cache rules need at least 10 turns. `/perun:cost-retro` now runs `--advise`.

The receipt is valid only for its exact head, names exactly the unchecked checks and records the kill criterion `revert-pr-if-an-unchecked-check-fails-post-merge`. A named check is skipped only while it is missing or unfinished on the head; one that ran and failed still blocks. A train carries at most one PARTIAL-PASS PR and only one may be outstanding: a second is skipped (`second PARTIAL-PASS (one per train; #M holds the slot)`, or `merged and undecided` until `partial-kill` decides the landed one), and `merge` HALTs if the recorded plan breaks that rule. `merge --apply` records the landed PR in the train state. The new `partial-kill` subcommand checks its unchecked checks on the merge commit: a failure opens a revert PR (`--apply`; dry run by default; exit 1); a running check, or one absent while CI is still running within `--wait` seconds (default 3600), prints PENDING; a check that never ran, or only skipped or neutral, prints UNVERIFIED (exit 1, record kept, never KEPT); KEPT only when every named check succeeded. The revert is opened through GraphQL `revertPullRequest`, so it still needs the normal merge path and was not exercised against the live forge. A partial pass is never counted as a pass. Tests: `scripts/test_partial_pass.py` (12), `partial_pass.py --selftest`.

Known limit: a single unquoted variable that word-splits into an option (`S="-9 1"; kill -0 $S`) is not detected.

- `destructive_guard.py` no longer lets a shell comment hide later lines: `shlex` treated `#` as a comment that swallowed the newline, so `echo hi #x` followed by `rm -rf /` on the next line passed unchecked. ### Fixed
- `train_land.sh` (#1777): a busy gate no longer refuses or fails after doing work. A gate that finds the exclusive heavy lease held now waits up to `LEASE_WAIT_SECS` (default `LOCK_TIMEOUT_MIN` x 60) and then `DEFER`s with exit 4 and nothing built, instead of exit 1. A held `train-push.lock` is waited out (`PUSH_WAIT_SECS`, default raised from 600 s to `LOCK_TIMEOUT_MIN` x 60) before the fetch and compose, so a held or stale push lock fails before any gate work and the union is built on the base the landing leaves. The lease is released as soon as the push lock is held, so heavy commands are allowed while a train lands. Composing during another train's landing is deliberately not done: that union would be stale at its own land. Replay model (`scripts/test_train_lease_replay.py`, seeded, 4 drivers x 30 trains, a model not a production measurement): refused attempts 1138 to 0, idle gate time 5.2 to 0.0 min, merges/day 134.4 to 134.6. ### Fixed
- `heavy_gate.py` unwraps `timeout [opts] DURATION`, `nohup`, `env [-u NAME]`, `nice [-n N]`, `stdbuf`, `xargs [opts]` and `bash|sh|zsh -c 'STRING'` (any option cluster holding `c`, such as `-lc`) before the heavy check, so `timeout 600 pytest`, `nohup npm test &`, `xargs pytest` and `bash -c "pytest"` are held like a bare run. Path-qualified wrappers (`/usr/bin/env`), `sudo -u USER`, `exec -a`, `time -f`, `uv run --with`, `setsid`, `ionice`, `doas`, `caffeinate -t`, `arch -arch`, `xargs -I{}` and BSD `xargs -J %`, a `--` after the wrapper and value-taking shell options (`bash -o pipefail -c`) are unwrapped too. ### Added
- `job_lease.py run [--name N] [--timeout S] -- CMD` (tests: `scripts/test_job_lease.py`, registered in `scripts/ci-tests.d/job-lease.sh`): a per-repo lease for long jobs (ship scripts, QA runs, merge trains). It is a kernel flock (`serial_gate.py run`) on `<git-common-dir>/perun-job-lease/N/lock`, shared by every worktree, so the owner and every agent queue instead of colliding; the kernel frees it when the holder dies. The child gets `PERUN_RUN_SUFFIX`, and `job_lease.py suffix` prints a fresh `<pid>_<6 hex>` suffix, safe in database, container and directory names. The child also gets `PERUN_JOB_LEASE` (the held lease names), so a nested `job_lease.py run` of the same name runs under the holder's lease instead of deadlocking on it. The lease belongs to the wrapper process: it frees when the wrapper dies, even if the child lives on. Fails closed (exit 2, command never runs) outside a git repo. Field cause (#1574): two long QA runs, one owner and one agent, collided on one database name. `multi-session-coordination.md` names it in its script list.
- A waiter on a lock now prints a queue line at least every 2 minutes (`PERUN_QUEUE_NOTE_SECS`, default 120; a non-integer or non-positive value falls back to 120; `serial_gate.py` accepts a positive float and shows the holder for slot waits too): `train_land.sh` while it waits for the exclusive heavy lease (`queued Ns: another gate holds the exclusive heavy lease; Ns of wait left`), `_lock.sh` `lock_take` (`waiting on lock held by pid ...` repeats instead of printing once), and `serial_gate.py run` (`queued Ns on <lock dir>; holder <owner record>`). Field cause (#1574): hooks and trains sat 17+ minutes on a lock with no progress line; the lease wait in `train_land.sh` was silent for up to `LEASE_WAIT_SECS` (30 minutes by default).

One `gh api repos/<slug>/issues/N` read per number prints `#N PR MERGED|CLOSED|OPEN` or `#N ISSUE OPEN|CLOSED`; an open issue also lists the backticked file paths and `name()` / `fn(x)` / snake_case / CamelCase / UPPER_CONST symbols its body cites that the checkout's HEAD does not contain (symbols are searched outside `*.md` and `changelog.d`; paths may be any `dir/name.ext` or an extensionless name such as `Makefile`) (`absent at HEAD: ...`). Dollar figures price the merged per-model totals once under the dated default rates; a model with no rate is named `UNPRICED` and never estimated, and an all-unpriced project reads `UNPRICED`, not `$0`; an empty project or window reads `$0.00`, and unreadable lane transcripts are counted in the line and the JSON (`unreadable_lanes`); a session file that is not valid UTF-8, or has no parsable turn, is counted in `unreadable_sessions` and the line instead of crashing or vanishing. ### Added
- `agentic-delivery/scripts/stall_guard.py`: Stop hook, wired in the operating-layer template and checked by `perun_doctor.py`. When a turn ends on "stopped / holding / waiting on you" and launched no Agent and no background tool, it blocks once with a nudge to launch the next lane, review or build, or to name the one owner-only blocker. The next stop passes (`stop_hook_active`); `PERUN_STALL_GUARD=off` disables it; any parse error fails open.

### Added
- `token_report.py --fix-plan` prints a minimal JSON settings patch for the fired levers that map to a key: `promptCacheTtl` `1h`, `autoCompactWindow` (the computed window), `bashOutputMaxChars` (the documented 10000 starting value), and env `LANE_TOOL_CAP` set to the lane p90 when that lowers the cap. Keys already set are skipped, and the subagent-model rule is never patched because it names no value. `--apply PATH` merges the patch into the symlink-resolved PATH: it refuses unreadable or invalid JSON and I/O errors (exit 2), writes `PATH.bak` only if absent with PATH's mode, replaces the file atomically, adds only absent keys, creates a missing PATH in an existing directory (mode 0600), and a second run prints `nothing to apply`. Under `--advise`, a lever whose key is already set no longer shows in the `Lever:` lines or `Top levers`, and unreadable settings print a note. Tests: `scripts/test_token_apply.py`.

### Added
- `token_report.py` now measures idle-gap cache rewrites and spend by model tier. Main-thread 5m cache-write tokens that follow a gap over 5 minutes are split into 5m-1h and over-1h gaps, with an upper-bound input-eq saving if a 1h cache pin held the cache (the report's formula: gap writes x (1.25 - 0.1) minus 0.75 x every other 5m write) as a share of main input-eq. The report also gives input-eq share by model for main and lanes (`UNPRICED` for a model with no rate, never zero). Text and `--json` (`idle_rewrites`, `tier_split`) carry them; all figures are upper bounds, not a bill. Two `Lever:` lines print only when material: pin the main cache to 1h when at least 30% of 5m writes follow an idle gap and the bound is at least 5% of main input-eq and less than half of cache writes are already 1h (names the `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` override and the v2.1.242+ pin requirement; `host-enforcement.md` says which accounts get 1h); a negative bound prints "a 1h pin would not save". Sidechain lines are no longer counted as main turns, and orchestrator tier when a top-tier main carries over 40% of all input-eq. `/perun:cost-retro` leads with them. Tests: `scripts/test_token_cache_gap.py`.

### Added
- `token_report.py` now estimates what auto-compact would save on the main thread: `auto_compact` in `--json` and a `Lever: auto-compact ...` line replay each main turn's context (input plus cache writes plus cache read), compact at 200000 (the `autoCompactWindow` `install.sh` writes) to an assumed 30000 tokens, then grow by the observed per-turn deltas; saving is 0.1 times the context removed, minus 1.25 times the restart size per simulated compaction. An upper bound, not a bill: quality lost to compaction and the summarizer call are not modelled, and a session that already compacts or never passes the window is skipped. The saving ranks in `Top levers` as `auto-compact at 200000`. `/perun:cost-retro` merges its two "lead with" instructions into one (lead with the top-ranked lever; its `Lever:` line gives the how). Tests: `scripts/test_token_compact_saving.py`.

### Added
- `token_report.py` now ranks the levers it already prints by estimated saving: a "Top levers (est. upper-bound saving, not a bill)" block, and `lever_ranking` in `--json`, list each firing lever whose saving the report already computes (the 1h cache pin bound and the lane tail beyond the shipped `LANE_TOOL_CAP`; no new estimate) sorted by input-eq saved with its share of main plus lane input-eq. The orchestrator-tier lever has no computed saving, so it lists after the ranked ones as `UNPRICED`, never zero. `lane_tail` gains `tail_ie_over_shipped_cap`. `/perun:cost-retro` now says to lead with the top-ranked lever. Tests: `scripts/test_token_lever_rank.py`.

### Changed
- `docs/bench/token-levers/` now also shows the tool-result and startup levers. `overlay.py` (not frozen; the frozen files are untouched) builds a `fire` and a `quiet` variant of the synthetic session in a temp dir, and `run.sh` asserts both: a Bash result past `bashOutputMaxChars` and a 112 KB `CLAUDE.md` fire (5.6% and 5.2% of fixture input-eq), results at or below the 10000-char floor and a 2 KB `CLAUDE.md` stay quiet, and the startup-remainder lever fires only with the small file. The README states these as fixture numbers and compares truthfully with RTK and context-mode, which compress output while Perun measures whether the lever applies. `token_report.py` no longer prints "(estimate)" twice on the startup-trim row of "Top levers", and the `lever_ranking` docstring names the startup-trim arithmetic it does compute.

### Added
- `token_report.py` now prints, and `--json` carries as `lane_tail`, the share of lane input-equivalent spent beyond two tool-call caps and the p90 lane tool calls: `tail_share_over_cap` against the reference cap (default 150; `build_report(cap=)` accepts an override, but `--budget` is gate-only so CLI output uses 150) and `tail_share_over_shipped_cap` against the `LANE_TOOL_CAP` the operating-layer template ships (250, read from the template at runtime; omitted if unreadable). When the tail beyond the shipped cap is 10% or more of lane input-eq it adds a lever line: lower `LANE_TOOL_CAP` toward the p90, enforced by `lane_cap.py`. Both figures are upper bounds: the redo cost of the tail in a narrower lane is ignored.

### Added
- `token_report.py --project DIR` now prices each auto-loaded instruction file lanes re-read: project `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, the user-level `CLAUDE.md` (from `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.claude`) and the project memory `MEMORY.md`. Size is file bytes / 4 (an estimate; contents are never read) and the upper-bound input-eq a file contributes is tokens x (1.25 per lane start + 0.1 per later lane turn) summed over lanes. `AGENTS.md` and memory are labelled "if loaded". `--json` gains `startup_files`; the text report prints the top 3 and, when half of the largest file's cost (an assumed trim fraction) is 5% or more of main plus lane input-eq, a "trim or split <file>" lever that also enters `lever_ranking` as an estimate-labelled "trim <file>" row (`estimate: true`). It also reports `startup_remainder`: measured lane startup minus the file estimate (system prompt, tool/MCP definitions, skill listing, brief; not split further) as tokens, input-eq, and shares of lane startup and lane input-eq; when it is over half of lane startup and at least 15% of lane input-eq a Lever line points to the MCP-unused / tool-search advice, batching short lanes and a smaller toolset per lane type. Both are skipped (`startup_files` empty, `startup_remainder` null, a note printed) under `--since`, where a windowed lane's first turn is not its start. Lane records gain `turns`. Tests: `scripts/test_token_startup_files.py`.

### Added
- `token_report.py` now measures tool-result size, the lever peer tools target: `tool_results` in `--json` counts main and lane tool results over 10000 chars (length only, never the text), split by tool (`by_tool`: Bash/PowerShell, Read, other such as MCP), and estimates their carry as chars/4 tokens times the turns resent until the next observed compaction (or the end) times the 0.1 cache-read weight. It is an estimate, clamped to the scope's input-eq (`clamped` says when). At 5% of session input-eq or more from Bash/PowerShell output past the 10000-char cap, it ranks a `cap Bash output with bashOutputMaxChars` row marked `estimate: true` and prints a `Lever:` line pointing at `docs/token-cost-tips.md`; a set `bashOutputMaxChars` or `BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` mutes it. Large Read and MCP results get info lines (read with offset/limit, check MCP output size), never a ranked row. Tests: `scripts/test_token_tool_results.py`.

## [1.599.0] — 2026-10-19

### Added
- Operating layer: `landing_watchdog.py`, a `UserPromptSubmit` hook (and a `check` CLI) that tells the model when the merge pipeline has landed nothing while green PRs wait. It fires when the default branch got zero first-parent commits in the last `landing_stall_min` minutes (policy key, default 60) and at least one open non-draft PR has every check green, adding one line: "Landing stalled: 0 merged to <branch> in N min, K green PRs waiting. Fix landing before starting new work." This closes a failure where a coordinator kept spawning work for 40 minutes to several hours while green PRs waited unnoticed. It asks the remote (one `git fetch`, one `gh pr list`) at most once per 15 minutes per repo and replays the cached verdict between, with the cache under `<cache>/perun/landing-watchdog` beside the other hook state. Mode is `warn` (default) or `off` via env `PERUN_LANDING_WATCHDOG` or policy `landing_watchdog`; it never blocks, and no gh, no origin, a failed fetch or any error prints nothing. Wired into the operating-layer settings template, `install.sh`, `perun_doctor.py`, `perun_policy.py`, an agentic-delivery eval and `scripts/test_landing_watchdog.py`.

## [1.597.0] — 2026-10-19

### Added
- Operating layer: `outcome_claim_guard.py` (Stop, plus PreToolUse on Bash) checks that delivery claims are measured. On Stop it reads the final reply and flags an outcome claim ("fixed", "faster", "improved", "done", "ends the risk", "no longer") about the pipeline, gates, trains, queues or merges, and output counts reported as progress ("9 PRs merged and 4 lanes spawned"). A reply passes if it gives a before and after on an outcome metric (lead time, gate or CI minutes, landed per hour, failure rate) tied to a merged sha or PR, or if it says honestly that the work is unmeasured. On `gh pr create` and `gh pr merge` whose diff touches pipeline paths (workflows, git hooks, train, gate and CI scripts; policy `outcome_guard_paths` overrides the globs) it requires a `pipeline_profile.py compare` verdict line in the PR body or a commit message: KEEP passes, while REVERT, UNVERIFIED or no verdict is denied in block mode and advised otherwise. Policy `outcome_guard` (`off|warn|block`, default `warn`; env `PERUN_OUTCOME_GUARD` overrides it). The default is `warn` because a replay over real coordinator replies put well over 10% of flags on honest replies. Block mode stops a reply once and never loops (`stop_hook_active`). It fails open. Tests: `scripts/test_outcome_claim_guard.py` (run in CI).

### Added
- `docs/bench/judge-calib-1018/`: calibration of the growth round-5 judge slot-1 skew (GLM-5.1, GLM-5.2, gpt-oss_120b; frozen judge, both orders, 60 spent round-4 and round-5 held-out outputs, PCSS only, $0). Identical pairs end in "tie" (359 of 360 verdicts), and a pair with a real gap gives slot-1 0.45 to 0.52 with 0.97 to 1.00 correct picks, so the judges do not carry a general position bias; the round-5 skew (0.62 to 0.67) comes from close contests, where 41 to 42 percent of skill-versus-rival pairs are decided by slot alone and the judge takes slot 1 in 80 to 93 percent of them. No skill, rival row or past verdict changes; a protocol fix (capability and resolution gates in place of the pooled slot-1 gate) is proposed in the README for the owner to preregister, not applied.

### Added
- `docs/bench/judge-gate-sim-1018/`: preregistered offline replay and simulation of a judge with a slot-1 bonus (item 4 of the Proposal in `docs/bench/judge-calib-1018/`; spent growth round-4 and round-5 verdicts plus 2000-repetition synthetic runs at true win rates 0.45 to 0.60, n = 150, both orders, splits 0.5; no model calls, $0). Verdict FAIL against the preregistered bar (|bias| at most 0.01, coverage at least 0.93): the bonus shrinks win rates and paired differences toward 0.5 rather than leaving them unbiased, with a worst-cell |bias| of 0.0018 at delta 0, 0.027 at delta 0.2 and 0.055 at delta 0.4, and the resolved share falls as delta grows. Every cell passes only up to delta 0.05. No skill, rival row or past verdict changes.

Bench-integrity gate: scripts/bench_check.py fails new bench dirs with tune/held scenario id collisions, byte-identical outputs reused from another bench, a missing or late preregistration ledger event, a PREREGISTERED doc naming a missing hash file, or heavy 10-word shingle overlap with earlier benches

Each skill has a fixture under `scripts/eval-fixtures/rival/<skill>/` with a frozen held-out set (n of at least 10, its sha256 pinned in `rival.json`) and a tune set; a held-out run fails closed if the set (or a patch file it references) changed, overlaps the tune set or is too small, and a tune run never prints a verdict. Rivals reuse the texts already committed under `docs/bench/`; the five rivals that were never committed (positioning, contribution, business-ops, agentic-ceo, agentic-delivery) are fetched once from their public URL at run time and cached outside the repo. A rubric-free blind pairwise judge (DeepSeek-V4-Flash on the PCSS endpoint) sees every pair in both orders; a scenario is a win or loss only when both orders agree and is otherwise a tie (0.5). Each judge's slot-1 rate (share of decisive picks that chose Response 1) is reported as a health metric, and a judge outside 0.4-0.6 is dropped for that skill in favor of GLM-5.2; when both are biased the skill gets no verdict. The generator (default Qwen3.5-397B-A17B on PCSS, $0) is never a judge. `--gen claude` is opt-in: it makes one probe call, stops when plan-quota utilization reaches 0.8, and is capped at $0.50 per skill run and a total cap, counts in-flight reserves against the cap, and fails closed when no utilization reading comes back. A judge with no decisive verdicts counts as unhealthy, verdict caches are keyed on the scenario, the rubric and the judge, and `write heldout` refuses to overwrite a frozen set without `--force`. `PCSS_KEY` comes from the environment or a repo-root `.env` and is never printed.
- `--changed [BASE]` scores only the skills a diff touches; `scripts/rival-eval-premerge.sh` is the local pre-merge hook point (for example `DCR_PREPUSH_CMD="bash scripts/rival-eval-premerge.sh"`). It needs a local key, so CI never runs it.

## [1.587.0] — 2026-10-17

### Added
- `deep-code-review/scripts/derived_numbers.py`: a doc number can be bound to a counter with an inline marker, `<!-- derived: COUNTER ARGS -->N`. The check fails when `N` differs from the counter's result (a stale "N tests" or "N skills"), and `--fix` rewrites the claim. Counters are a fixed allowlist computed in Python: `files GLOB` (tracked files; a run of `*` is one wildcard, a glob is capped at 200 characters and 4 wildcards, and matching tracks live positions with no backtracking, so a hostile glob is a finding rather than a hang), `lines PATH`, `grep-count PATTERN PATH` (lines containing a literal substring) and `json-len PATH KEY`. Doc text is never run as a shell command, so a pull request's markdown cannot execute code in CI; an unknown counter is a finding that runs nothing. Paths must stay inside the repo and never pass through a symlink. Files are read as bytes (non-UTF-8 and CRLF round-trip under `--fix`, which writes a temp file and replaces atomically and skips symlinks), vendored directories and files without `<!--` are skipped, fenced code (by fence character and length), indented code and multi-backtick code spans are ignored, and the number never absorbs a trailing comma, period or decimal part. A repo with no markers passes.
- `scripts/dcr-gates.sh` (the runner `install.sh --with-gates` installs) runs it by default, plus its selftest; `DCR_DERIVED_NUMBERS=0` turns it off and any other value except 1 fails closed. This repo's CI runs it on its own docs: the skill count in `docs/perun-vs-rivals.md` (two places) is bound to `files .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`. Tests: `scripts/test_derived_numbers.py` (wired into CI). One `deep-code-review` eval: `docs-count-bound-to-source-command`.
