### Added
- Operating layer: `ceo_altitude_guard.py` (PreToolUse on Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit and Bash, plus UserPromptSubmit) keeps the main session at CEO altitude. It counts the main session's direct source edits per session. Once policy `role` is `ceo` it warns on the 2nd direct source edit and the 4th build/test run in a turn with `delegate: spawn a lane with the brief ...`; `role: ceo-strict` blocks them instead (a JSON deny, never exit 2). Subagents and in-process teammates are never counted, warned or blocked: the host sends `agent_id` only inside them (Claude Code hooks reference, fetched 2026-10-16, logged in `docs/standards-index.md`), and `agent_type` is not used because a `--agent` main session carries it too. The docs do not say outright that the main session omits `agent_id`, so a wrong assumption makes the guard silent, never blocking a lane; a separate top-level lane process sets `PERUN_ROLE=off`. Docs, config, memory, handoff, changelog and temp-dir files are never flagged; a Bash write to a source file (`> f.py`, `tee`, `sed -i`, `perl -i`) counts like an Edit. `ceo:off` in an owner prompt lifts it for that turn. It fails open. Tests: `scripts/test_ceo_altitude_guard.py` (59 tests, run in CI).
- Policy key `role` (`off|ceo|ceo-strict`, default `off`; `ceo strict` is read as `ceo-strict`) in `.perun/policy.json`. Env `PERUN_ROLE` overrides it for one process, and `install.sh --policy role=ceo` writes it. The agentic-ceo skill and `/perun-run` now tell the conductor to arm it.
- `operating_selfcheck.py` prints the drift counter: a `ceo-altitude:` line (role in effect, sessions recorded, direct source edits in all) and one `ceo-altitude-session <id>:` line per recent session of the project, counted even while `role` is `off`. It also reports a `ceo-altitude-guard` wiring item, PRESENT only when both events are wired. `perun_doctor.py` flags an installed guard that no hook calls.

### Added
- `ci_cost_advisor.py` (deep-code-review scripts) prices a repo's GitHub Actions. It reads `.github/workflows`, the repository's visibility and its git history, and estimates runs, minutes and dollars per push/PR and per month from each workflow's triggers, matrix and jobs, at the per-minute rates and included minutes that docs.github.com publishes (fetched 2026-10-16, logged in `docs/standards-index.md`). A public repo on standard runners is reported as free and gets no plan. For a private repo it prints before and after numbers for a local-first plan (run the full gate locally before the push, keep only a cheap required check in Actions, trim the rest) and a unified diff to review and `git apply`. It never edits a workflow. Every assumption is printed (job minutes default to 5, three pushes per PR) and `--job-minutes`, `--prs` and `--pushes-per-pr` take measured numbers.
- The patch only makes edits that cannot strand a required check: per-PR `concurrency` with cancel-in-progress (push and schedule runs never share a group), `push` limited to the default branch or dropped under strict protection, and, once `--required` names the required workflows and a local pre-push gate exists, gate workflows moved to `workflow_dispatch` and a docs `paths-ignore` that would have skipped 50% or fewer of the last 30 days of PRs. A required workflow never gets a path filter or `[skip ci]`: GitHub leaves a skipped required check Pending and blocks the merge.
- Policy key `ci` (`local-first|cloud|auto`, default `auto`) in `.perun/policy.json`. `perun_policy.py ci` prints the effective mode; `auto` is local-first when `github_actions` is off, otherwise the verdict of `ci_cost_advisor.py --decide` (a public repo, or a private one inside its free minutes, stays cloud; a private one using half its included minutes goes local-first; a missing or failing advisor means cloud). On local-first, lanes run every gate locally before the push and push each PR once (lane preamble, `operating-discipline.md`, `docs/for-fleets.md`), and `pre-push-verify.sh` prints a warning when a push re-pushes a branch that already exists on the remote.
- `scripts/test_ci_cost_advisor.py` covers pricing, trigger run counts, matrices, doc-only path filters, public versus private, a patch that applies with `git apply` and loads in a real YAML parser, the policy key, the lint route and the pre-push notice; it runs in `ci.yml`. Two evals (deep-code-review, agentic-delivery).

### Added
- New `agentic-delivery/scripts/flake_ledger.py` (stdlib only): a per-test pass/fail ledger keyed by tree SHA. A test with at least one fail and one pass on the same tree is a flake; after N distinct flake trees (default 3) `quarantine` lists it with an owner-reviewed expiry date (default 14 days). A quarantined test is reported and non-blocking until its expiry, after which it blocks again until `renew`; `quarantine` never extends an entry. A test that fails consistently on a tree (two or more fails, no pass) is never quarantined, and a quarantined test that fails consistently on the checked tree is blocking again (`check`). With `FLAKE_LEDGER_DIR` set, `train_flake.sh` records each `FLAKE`/`REAL` verdict in the ledger (best-effort) and prints `quarantined-flake <id>` instead of `FLAKE` for an id on its active quarantine list that re-ran alone as a flake and is not already failing consistently on that tree. `train_land.sh` counts such an id toward the new failures like a `FLAKE`, reports it, lands past it, and skips the flake-on-base check for it (so a known flake no longer ends in `CANT`). The label needs a solo failure (0 < failed solo runs < runs): a suite failure that passes every solo re-run keeps the plain `FLAKE` and its base check (a quarantined id runs all its solo re-runs, no early stop on the first pass). The ledger records each run separately (`SUITE`, then every solo `FAIL`/`PASS`; verdict labels are not evidence) and counts a flake tree only with a solo fail and a pass. Against a PR forging its own quarantine entry, `FLAKE_LEDGER_DIR` under the worktree or git toplevel is refused (exit 2), the quarantine list is read once into an unexported shell variable before any PR code runs (never a file; `train_land.sh` hands it to `train_flake.sh` on stdin and `check --quarantine -` reads it from stdin), and the variable is unset for `VERIFY_CMD`, `BROWSER_CMD`, `RERUN_CMD` and `FLAKE_SETUP_CMD`. Known ceiling, recorded as a decision in the `flake_ledger.py` header: same-uid code that learns the ledger directory by other means can still write it, and the files are not signed (no HMAC, the key would sit where the same user can read it), so the OS sandbox is the boundary: run the train sandboxed with the ledger directory outside its write set. `train_land.sh` prints `N quarantined (base not checked)` separately from the `each also flaky on the base` line. Ledger writers hold an `flock`, `quarantine.json` is replaced via a unique temp file, and a torn last ledger line is tolerated and dropped on the next append. Unlisted ids, expired entries, consistent failures (`REAL`) and a listed id already failing consistently on the union tree behave exactly as before. Routed from the "Fix a red gate or union" row of `agentic-delivery/SKILL.md`. Tests: `scripts/test_flake_ledger.py` (17 cases, incl. concurrent writers and torn lines) and `scripts/test-train-flake-ledger.sh` (11 end-to-end `train_land.sh` cases), both registered via `scripts/ci-tests.d/flake-ledger.sh`.

### Added
- Pipeline optimizer for slow delivery pipelines (commit and push hooks, CI, queue, merge wait): the procedure `agentic-delivery/references/pipeline-optimizer.md` and the stdlib script `agentic-delivery/scripts/pipeline_profile.py`. The conductor owns it as the COO function (flow, timebox, one batched escalation) with the Architect hat as the CTO function (the fix); `agentic-ceo` routes "the pipeline is slow" to it.
- `pipeline_profile.py map` is step 1 and mandatory: it reads hooks, workflows and the documented pre-PR commands into a suite x stage table (commit, push, precheck, ci, train) and flags every suite that runs at more than one stage, with the latest server-enforced gate to keep. `profile` measures per-stage wall time on the critical path, CI queue wait, push-to-merge lead time, reruns, flake suspects, duplicates in seconds and the cache hit rate (counted from job logs only; otherwise `n/a`) from the GitHub REST API plus local timings (`time`, `hooks --run`, `suites --run`), and prints a ranked bottleneck table. When one step dominates it says so and prices sharding from section timings (`--sections`). `fixes` prices a ten-fix catalogue from the profile with duplicate removal first, `compare` keeps a change only if the measured time dropped (exit 0 KEEP, 1 REVERT, 2 UNVERIFIED). A rate-limited API run keeps what it fetched and resumes from its `--data` bundle.
- Anti-stall rules in the procedure: no fix without a profile, one timebox per hypothesis, the measured delta reported at every step, one batched escalation with exact commands.
- Dogfood on this repository's own pipeline, record in `docs/bench/pipeline-1016/`: the profile put 82% of CI execution (10m27s of 12m46s) in `scripts/test-ci-gates.sh`; section timings showed each call of the shipped gate runner re-proving the same seven idempotent selftests (about 45 s per call). `dcr-gates.sh` now stamps a passing selftest once per run (`DCR_SELFTEST_STAMPS`; the key is the script's content hash; a failure is never stamped; an unusable stamp directory means run). Measured locally: full suite 2092 s to 1421 s wall (-32%), 971 s to 564 s CPU (-42%). The CI step is not re-measured yet; the record lists the commands and the kill criteria.
- Evals `pipeline-dedup-before-stage-tuning` (the same four suites at four stages: the answer is dedup, 1300s to 325s, not a faster runner), `pipeline-map-first`, `pipeline-moving-a-gate-is-not-weakening`, `pipeline-timebox-and-batched-escalation`, `pipeline-keep-only-if-time-drops`, `pipeline-local-precheck-breakeven`, `pipeline-dominant-step-drill-down` and `ceo-routes-slow-pipeline-to-pipeline-optimizer`. Tests: `scripts/test_pipeline_profile.py` and `scripts/test-selftest-stamps.sh`, both wired into CI.
- `docs/standards-index.md`: the sources for the catalogue and the measured fields, fetched 2026-10-16 with each quote checked verbatim.

### Added
- New `agentic-delivery/scripts/sandbox_preflight.py`, a read-only autonomy advisor (stdlib only, never writes settings). It scans a repo's package scripts, Makefile, git hooks and local scripts for what the Claude Code sandbox breaks (tsx Unix-socket IPC, local port binds, Chromium/Playwright, database clients, `gh` TLS, docker, git over SSH on macOS, writes outside the repo) and prints "To run autonomously, add:": a settings JSON snippet with only what the existing settings lack, led by sandbox config (`sandbox.enabled`, `sandbox.excludedCommands` written as the command the agent types, allowed domains, `allowLocalBinding`, `allowWrite`), then `permissions.deny` for destructive git, `rm -rf` and `sudo`, `permissions.ask` for publish, deploy and release, what stays blocked on purpose, and the per-host mechanism the docs confirm (Claude Code, Codex). The OS sandbox is the safety boundary: `permissions.allow` rules for the repo's test, lint and build commands (by name) and `git push <remote> HEAD` print only when the sandbox is enabled, with a disclosure that they run repo-controlled code (no static check can make that safe), and are checked against `destructive_guard.py`; with the sandbox off no allow rule is printed. A publish, deploy, release or push word in a unit's name or body means an ask rule, never an allow rule, and a prefix rule is used only when every file under the prefix was vetted. `perun_doctor.py` and `install.sh` print the section; sources and dates are in `docs/standards-index.md` (2026-10-16).
- `lane_guard.py` now copies the gitignored `.banlist.local.txt` from the main checkout into a new lane worktree when it is missing (plain copy, never a symlink, never an overwrite, only when git ignores the path, only after an OK result).

### Changed
- `terse_reply_check.py` now prevents instead of forcing a rewrite: on `SessionStart` it injects the reply budget (3 lines / 500 chars by default; code blocks and `! ` lines excluded), a violation on `Stop` no longer blocks but is recorded, and the next `UserPromptSubmit` gets a one-line reminder, so the user never sees a reply and its shortened copy. `TERSE_MODE=block` keeps the old rewrite. The opt-in template `terse-replies.settings.json` registers all three events.
- `handback_cap.py` no longer counts fenced code blocks or lines starting with `! ` toward its 800-char / 10-line cap, so copy-paste commands never force a rewrite; the whole message may still not pass 5 times the char cap, so a deliverable cannot hide in a fence.

### Fixed
- PRs that touch different skills no longer conflict once one of them merges. Lanes stop committing the derived files that every merge changed: `SHA256SUMS`, the `scripts/size-budgets.tsv` rows and the `INDEX.md` files. `scripts/regen-unlanded.sh` rebuilds them in CI for an unlanded PR (VERSION equal to main's), so every gate still reads current files and the size ratchet still compares the rebuilt rows to main. On a land commit (VERSION moved) nothing is rebuilt, so the committed files are checked byte-for-byte there; an unresolvable base counts as landed.
- `ci.yml` routes every skill through one glob loop and `write-checksums.sh` pins every skill dir by glob, so adding a skill edits neither list (the enumeration gate accepts both forms). New CI tests register as one file, `scripts/ci-tests.d/<slug>.sh`, instead of a line appended to a shared step.
- The size ratchet now also reads `size-budget-raise:` markers from `changelog.d/` fragments, as CONTRIBUTING already said.
- The pre-push hook skips the INDEX.md and SHA256SUMS stale checks on an unlanded tree and keeps them strict on a land commit.
- New test `scripts/test-conflict-free-prs.sh`: two lanes on different skills merge cleanly, the old flow (lanes committing derived files) conflicts as a control, and the strict land-commit check still bites.

### Changed
- Maximum pace no longer reads as a licence to spend. It lifts the lane and heavy-slot caps, the `HOLD`/`FULL` retry waits and approval pauses inside the granted budget, and spends more only where that buys speed or quality: parallel lanes up to the load gate, a stronger model or deeper verification on hard steps. A waste filter holds in both modes: no duplicate run of the same gate on the same tree, no idle polling, no courtesy messages, no restating, and the cheapest model that keeps quality for mechanical work. Spend is still reported. The old wording that max pace "outranks the model-tier economy" is gone.
- One source of truth: the rule, its triggers and the `perun_policy.py set tokens maximize` / `set local_cpu maximize` knobs now live once in `templates/lane-preamble.md` **Drive to the goal**; `references/operating-discipline.md`, `templates/loops/coordinator.md`, `commands/perun-run.md` and `docs/for-fleets.md` point to it. The preamble also names the way back (`set tokens efficient`, `set local_cpu efficient`), and the trigger list reads "push at max" instead of a bare "push" so a git push grant does not switch the spend mode.
- New eval `max-pace-mechanical-rename-stays-cheap` (a max-pace rename lane stays on the cheapest tier while a security re-review gets the stronger one) and new test `scripts/test_max_pace_no_waste.py`, which pins the wording, the single source, and that the documented knobs match `perun_policy.py`.

### Fixed
- The size ratchet (`ci-gates.sh size-ratchet`) now measures a raise from the larger of the file's real size at the base ref and its `size-budgets.tsv` row there. Lanes no longer commit rows, so after any landed PR grew a budgeted file the base rows were stale and every later PR failed with a raise it did not make. On a landed tree the row equals the size (or is a hand-kept budget above it), so nothing changes there. A `size-budget-raise:` marker names that larger base value as its old value. Five new cases in `scripts/test-ci-gates.sh` cover an untouched file with a stale row, real growth, a marker on the real size, a marker built on the stale row, and a hand-kept row above the size.

### Added
- `deep-code-review/scripts/gate_cache.py`: one PASS cache shared by every gate stage (pre-commit, pre-push, a precheck script, the merge-train gate), keyed by (git tree SHA, gate-set version, config hash) under `<git-common-dir>/perun-gate-cache/`. A tree that already passed the same suite prints one line, `cached PASS <tree>`, and skips it, so whichever stage reaches a tree first runs the suite and the others skip. Only an exit 0 is ever recorded: a FAIL, a dirty or untracked tree, an unmerged index, or a run that edited tracked files is never cached and simply runs. Entries are ignored after 7 days and deleted on the next write. Editing any hook file, the cache script, a path in `$PERUN_GATE_FILES` or `$PERUN_GATE_SET_VERSION` is a new gate set that misses every older entry; `$PERUN_GATE_CACHE_KEY` folds in a toolchain fingerprint. `PERUN_GATE_CACHE=0` opts out, `PERUN_GATE_CACHE=refresh` reruns and re-records. Wire any stage with `gate_cache.py run --stage NAME -c '<suite>'`.
- `deep-code-review/scripts/gate_map.py`: a read-only report of which suites each stage runs (pre-commit, pre-push, precheck, the train gate from `$VERIFY_CMD`/`$BASE_AUDIT_CMD`/`$BROWSER_CMD`/`$RATCHET_CMD`, or any `--stage NAME=PATH`), tagged cached or uncached. It flags a command that runs in two or more stages and says what to change: wrap the uncached stages, or set `DCR_PREPUSH_TREE_PURE=1` when the scopes differ. It writes nothing and runs no suite.
- `perun_policy.py heavy-acquire --kind light` and `perun_policy.py heavy-load`: a lease can declare a light kind (a read-only or doc lane), and `heavy-load` prints the weighted live-lease count.
- Tests: `scripts/test_gate_cache.py`, `scripts/test_prepush_gate_cache.py`, `scripts/test_train_gate_cache.py`, `scripts/test_gate_map.py`, `scripts/test_lane_weight.py`.

### Changed
- `pre-push-verify.sh` asks `gate_cache.py` before running `DCR_PREPUSH_CMD`, replacing the per-commit stamp under `dcr-prepush-stamps/` (that directory is now unused and can be deleted). The tier stays range-aware by default, so its key still includes the pushed range: `dcr-gates.sh` reads commit messages through `BASE_SHA`/`HEAD_SHA`, so a reworded commit or a different base must not share its verdict (the #1153 rule). Set `DCR_PREPUSH_TREE_PURE=1` when the tier is a pure function of the tree (lint, unit tests): the verdict is then shared across amends and with every other stage that runs the same command text through `gate_cache.py`. `DCR_PREPUSH_SKIP_CACHE=1` still forces a rerun and refreshes the entry; `DCR_PREPUSH_CACHE_KEY` is still folded into the key; without python3 or the script the tier runs uncached.
- `train_land.sh` (`BASE_AUDIT_CMD`) and `merge_train.py` (the `--verify-cmd` union gate) consult the same cache, so a base or union tree that already passed the same command is not re-tested; a failed union is never persisted.
- The heavy-lease count that `heavy_gate.py` compares with the slot cap is now weighted: a lane that declares `light` (or, with no declaration, one whose process tree measures under 15% of a core once its lease is 60 seconds old) counts a quarter of a heavy lane, so three light lanes plus one heavy lane no longer fill a four-slot host. A lane that cannot be classified (no `ps`, a young lease, an unknown kind) counts as heavy. `host_probe.py --live-lanes` accepts the weighted fraction.

### Added
- `agentic-ceo` now owns a product improvement loop for any project: "what are the next most impactful items?" Read `references/improvement-loop.md` (routed from `SKILL.md`). It starts with a strategy context (stage from the existing `deep-code-review` STAGE model, vision, north star, direction, constraints; a missing field is marked `assumed` and costs the owner one batched question), gathers evidence (issues and PRs, changelog, feedback files, support threads, analytics if present, session logs and token reports, rival changelogs fetched live), right-sizes between direct analysis and read-only C-suite role lanes (CPO, CTO, CFO, CMO, CISO, COO, each with a short brief and one fixed return schema, cheap models for gathering), scores with a printed formula, attacks the top 3 open items with `idea-critic`, has the CTO role write short ADRs, and renders strategy context, rejected items, ranked roadmap, ADRs and tracker-ready issues in that order.
- `agentic-ceo/scripts/roadmap_rank.py`: stdlib scorer for the loop. Score is reach x impact x confidence / effort x stage weight x vision factor. Confidence is computed, never typed: 1.0 when reach and impact both cite a real locator (URL, existing repo path, issue or PR), else 0.5, so "estimate:" or "~assumed" cannot bypass it. Effort includes +2 lane-days per owner or external-send gate and +0.25 per calendar-wait day. Items already in flight are scored and flagged, not dropped. Equal scores rank fewer assumed inputs first. A vision-misaligned item is rejected with its reason, `--strict` requires an `idea-critic` verdict on the top 3 open items, `--update` rewrites a marked block in a doc. Reads JSON, or a CSV plus `--context`. Tests: `scripts/test_roadmap_rank.py` (41 checks, wired into CI).
- `docs/roadmap.md` now opens with the Perun product roadmap built through this loop from `docs/roadmap-input.json` (the 2026-10-16 peer survey and field measurements committed as `docs/peer-survey-2026-10-16.md`, `docs/perun-vs-rivals.md`, open issues, the changelog and live rival changelogs): 22 scored items (15 open, 7 in flight), 6 rejected with reasons, 4 ADRs and tracker-ready issues for the open items. Field-proven items are included with sourced inputs (delivery dedup, the autonomy advisor); inputs without a source are listed as assumed. A test fails if the page and its input drift. The 2026-09-11 suite design record follows unchanged.
- Two `agentic-ceo` evals: `improvement-loop-strategy-first-scored-roadmap` and `improvement-loop-right-sized-roles`.

Any other remote is still not accepted as canonical. Tests: `scripts/test_auto_update_move.py`.

### Added
- `.claude/skills/INDEX.md` is now the single low-context entry point, still generated by `scripts/skill_index.py`: one line per skill (the first sentence of its description), one per slash command (`/name: purpose — argument hint`) and one per shipped script (`name: purpose — arguments`, with arguments only where the script's own header documents them; scripts with no documented CLI, such as hooks and sourced helpers, are listed by name). It also says where to read next: a skill's `SKILL.md` when its line matches, its `INDEX.md` for references and scripts. It points and never restates a checklist. It covers 11 skills, 5 commands and 90 scripts (60 with a documented CLI, 30 by name) in 10,053 bytes.
- `python3 scripts/skill_index.py --check` now also fails with `NOT IN INDEX: <skill>/<script>` (or `/<command>`) when a shipped `scripts/*.py|*.sh` or `commands/*.md` is not listed in the entry index. Coverage is read back from the file on disk, not from the generator, so a filter added to the generator cannot hide a script; `scripts/test_skill_index_entry.py` proves it with a generator that drops one.
- `scripts/size-budgets.tsv` freezes the entry index at its measured size (its own row in that file; the size changes with every script added), enforced by the existing `ci-gates.sh size` and `size-ratchet`. Adding a script now costs a visible `size-budget-raise: .claude/skills/INDEX.md <old>→<new> <reason>` marker, so the entry point cannot grow silently.
- `python3 scripts/skill_index.py --tokens` prints the always-loaded surface (skill descriptions, SessionStart host rules, the entry index) in bytes and estimated tokens (`bytes // 4`, this repo's chars/4 convention, not a tokenizer count). On the base commit: 1609 tok in total, of which 904 are injected by the host every session (descriptions 829, SessionStart host rules 75) and 705 are the entry index. After this change: 3417 tok, the whole increase in the entry index (2,823 → 10,053 bytes, 705 → 2513 tok); the 904 tok the host injects are unchanged. Nothing in this repo injects the entry index (no hook, install block, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` line points at it), so an agent reads it on demand instead of opening a skill's `INDEX.md` (agentic-delivery 3,388 tok, deep-code-review 4,924 tok, all eleven 9,893 tok) or its `SKILL.md` (up to 5,993 tok) to find what to run and how.

### Added
- Six lens references close the gaps found by checking the review against ISO/IEC 25010:2023, OWASP ASVS 5.0 and the LLM Top 10, WCAG 2.2, and the lens lists of seven review tools (CodeRabbit, Greptile, Qodo, Sourcery, SonarQube, GitHub Copilot code review, Anthropic's code-review plugin). Every source was fetched on 2026-10-16 and is logged in `docs/standards-index.md`. The other lenses considered (accessibility, i18n, observability, reliability, concurrency, data integrity, API compatibility, privacy, FinOps, supply chain and licensing, testability, DX, LLM risks, design-system consistency, runtime speed) were already covered and are not duplicated.
  - `safety-critical.md` (domain F): the ISO/IEC 25010:2023 Safety characteristic as five probes, and the rule that fail-safe is not fail-closed: a conflict goes to the owner, never a silent choice. A review never certifies a system as safe.
  - `energy-efficiency.md` (domain E): the Software Carbon Intensity frame, `UNMEASURED` instead of an invented kWh or gCO2eq, and battery, idle-power and carbon-aware-placement probes.
  - `delivery-speed.md` (domain K): measure time-to-green and the pull-request cycle from run history, then CI wall-clock, build-time and review-friction probes (caches, serial `needs` chains, retries that mask flakes, PR size, review latency, bot severity floors).
  - `code-structure.md` (domain H): read-only import-cycle, fan-in and co-change probes, and the structure-to-speed links (import-time work, bundle shape, hot and cold paths).
  - `product-impact.md` (domain M): a claimed outcome needs a metric with a baseline, an emitter, a guardrail and a decision rule, plus event-correctness probes (exactly once, after confirmation, survives page exit).
  - `compatibility-portability.md` (domain I): declared versus tested support matrix, portability probes, co-existence, installability and lock-in.

### Added
- Zero-chat lanes. `subagent_start_inject.py` now always injects `LANE_RULES` (189 characters, about 48 estimated tokens) into every subagent except the built-in types whose chat is the deliverable (`HANDBACK_EXEMPT_TYPES`): tool calls only with no prose between them, then a final message of `key=value` fields only (`status`, `sha`, `result`, `tests`, `blockers`, `report`) under 400 characters. `LANE_RULES=0` turns it off and `LANE_RULES_SKIP_TYPES` (comma-separated) skips more types, for a read-only review type that keeps a raised cap. It needs no house file, so an existing install gets it when the script updates.
- `handback_cap.py` is now also a lane audit. Whenever a stop is allowed it appends one JSON line per lane to `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/perun/lane-audit.jsonl` (`HANDBACK_AUDIT_LEDGER` moves or disables it): estimated assistant text tokens (narration between tool calls, and the handback) against tool-call tokens, plus the tool-call count, whether the handback is fields-only, its target violations (`viol`: `long`, `prose`) and `cut_tok`, the tokens a truncation to the field lines within the target would drop. Counts only, never transcript content. A hook cannot rewrite what the caller receives, so the truncation is measured, not applied. It reads the subagent's own `agent_transcript_path`; the hooks reference says `transcript_path` is the parent session's file and that the transcript is written asynchronously, so the final message is taken from `last_assistant_message` (or a `SubagentHandback` call) and counted once. The same reference gives no entry format and the sessions page calls it internal and version-dependent, so the parser reads only the `text` and `tool_use` blocks of assistant entries (the shape observed on local transcripts on 2026-10-16) and reports `COULD_NOT_CHECK` instead of zeros when it finds none. Token figures are estimates (characters / 4): the `usage.output_tokens` logged in those transcripts is far below the content size, so it is not used.
- `handback_cap.py --report [LEDGER]` and `--scan PATH... [--since-days N]` print medians, p90, totals, the text share, the fields-only rate and the off-target rate as aggregates, never content; `--scan` audits transcripts already on disk without writing the ledger.
- `scripts/test_zero_chat_lanes.py` (50 tests, run in CI) covers the never-a-second-handback rule, the unchanged 800/10 cap, the audit counts against a synthetic transcript in the observed shape, the ledger (one row per lane, no content, disabled, unwritable, XDG path), the report and scan modes, the injected rule, its size and its agreement with the logged target, and the docs. CI also now runs `subagent_start_inject.py --selftest`.

### Changed
- A handback that is off the fields-only 400-character, 8-line target (`HANDBACK_TARGET_CHARS`, `HANDBACK_TARGET_LINES`, `HANDBACK_FIELDS_ONLY=0` to skip the prose check) is logged, never sent back: a rewrite re-reads the lane's whole context, which costs more than a shorter handback saves. The blocking cap is unchanged (800 characters / 10 lines, `HANDBACK_MAX_CHARS`, `HANDBACK_MAX_LINES`, release after 3 blocks).
- The lane preamble now says zero chat between tool calls and a final message of `key=value` fields only. The default `.claude/house-defaults.md` that `install.sh` writes no longer carries its own copy of the handback rule (the injected lane rules own it); an existing file keeps its old hand-back line, so delete that line there.
- `host-enforcement.md`: the review-lane setup now says the default `SubagentStop` entry must exclude that type. Matching hooks run in parallel and any block wins, so the raised cap in a second entry had no effect while the default entry also matched. Matcher and parallel-execution rules are logged from the hooks reference in `docs/standards-index.md` (fetched 2026-10-16, with the sessions and session-storage pages).

### Measured
Reproduce with `python3 .claude/skills/agentic-delivery/scripts/handback_cap.py --scan ~/.claude/projects --since-days 14` (read-only; prints aggregates, never content).
- On 1,863 lane transcripts from the last 14 days on one developer machine (15 more, of the exempt built-in types, excluded), with token figures estimated at characters / 4: median text tokens per lane 222 (p90 996; narration between tool calls median 36, p90 765; handback median 126) against 7,479 tool-call tokens per lane, so text is 3.6% of lane assistant output. Of today's handbacks 59.6% already have the field shape, but the median handback is about 500 characters on one line and 73.5% are off the target.
- Projection (estimate; assumes every lane complies, meaning no narration and a handback within the target): median text tokens per lane at most 100, total 159,102 against 813,965 now. Net per lane, saved minus injected, in raw tokens: 351 saved on average (122 on the median lane) minus 48 for the rule = about +303 on average (+74 at the median). Saved tokens are output and the rule is cached input, so the net is larger in cost than in tokens; it is an upper bound that depends on the lanes following the rule, which only the ledger can show.
- The rule is 189 characters against 161 for a plain caveman-ultra subagent activation line and 3,780 for the full caveman skill file.

## [1.586.0] — 2026-10-16

### Added
- `install.sh --apply-operating-layer` now sets `autoCompactWindow: 200000` in `.claude/settings.local.json`, but only when no user, project or local settings file already sets it; policy `auto_compact: off` (`--policy auto_compact=off`) opts out, and uninstall removes only the value install added.
- New SessionStart hook `handoff_inject.py` (matchers `compact|startup|clear`) re-injects the newest `.claude/handoff*.md` after a compaction, at most 2KB (only the first 2KB is read), framed as data not instructions, nothing when absent; on `startup` a handoff older than 24h is skipped. Stdlib only, fails open. If any settings file is invalid JSON or JSONC the installer cannot tell whether the user set `autoCompactWindow`, so it writes nothing and prints a note. Tests: `scripts/test-auto-context-reset.sh`. Measured: 2048 bytes injected at most and about 32 ms per run (python3 start-up included); no token saving was measured, so none is claimed.

### Changed
- `context_nudge.py` no longer suggests the owner start a fresh session: it tells the agent to write `.claude/handoff.md` and not to ask for a restart. `references/operating-discipline.md` documents that auto-compact plus re-inject replaces "restart the session" (a session cannot `/clear` itself).

### Fixed
- Auto-update no longer skips with "no readable install marker" on older installs that have `.claude/.dcr-install-flags` but no `.claude/.perun-install.json`. `perun_auto_update.py` now treats such a repo as an install: the version comes from the installed `deep-code-review` `SKILL.md` frontmatter and the remote is the canonical public repo. Merge/rebase/train locks and an uncommitted `.claude/settings.local.json` still skip; hash-drift cannot be checked because an old install recorded no hashes, so uncommitted skill edits are preserved by install.sh's backup of the skill dirs it replaces, not by a skip. The update writes the real marker, so this is one-time.
- `install.sh` now records the canonical public repo as the marker `remote` when `PERUN_REMOTE` is unset and the install source has no git origin (tarball or plugin copy), so the marker always carries a remote for auto-update.

### Fixed
- Auto-update legacy installs (no `.perun-install.json`) read `version:` only inside a properly closed `---` frontmatter block of the installed `SKILL.md`; with no closing `---` the version is unreadable and the run is a logged skip instead of scanning the whole file.
- A legacy install always updates from the canonical remote: if the cache clone (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/perun/src`) was cloned from a different origin, the run logs a skip rather than inheriting that origin into the new marker.
- Docs for the legacy path no longer claim uncommitted-change skips apply to it: only git locks and an uncommitted `.claude/settings.local.json` skip; uncommitted skill edits are preserved by install.sh's backup, not by a skip.

### Changed
- `docs/perun-vs-rivals.md`: H1 now says the other H1 rubrics were not preserved, that rubric bias is shown for product-output-safety only and is a possible risk for the other rows (not re-run), and that the product-output-safety rival is a red-team tool skill run without its tools. New H1b: on a rubric-free blind judge product-output-safety lost to its rival, 0.150 [0.000, 0.400] on set A and 0.250 [0.100, 0.400] on fresh set B. - `perun_doctor.py` now checks drift in every root `install.sh` can write, not only four.
- New `scripts/test_extra_hosts_install.py` (run in CI): fixture repo and HOME under `$TMPDIR`, install, doctor, then uninstall with 0 leftovers; a user-edited copy is kept and a pre-existing copy is restored.

### Changed
- `docs/perun-vs-rivals.md` H10 now counts 11 native hosts and marks each as smoke-tested (Codex only) or docs-validated. No new host was run on a real install.

### Fixed
- agentic-delivery: `train_flake.sh` no longer false-blames a flaky test. An id is `REAL` only when it fails every one of the `FLAKE_RUNS` (default 3) isolated re-runs; any single pass makes it a `FLAKE`. `FLAKE_REAL_AT` now defaults to `FLAKE_RUNS` and is no longer clamped to 2. Measured on a 1-in-3 flake (200 trials, same seeds): 64/200 = 32.0% blamed before, 9/200 = 4.5% after (analytic 3.7%); `scripts/test-train-flake-rate.sh` proves it on the real script with a seeded 1000-trial simulation (31/1000 after, 248/1000 under the old rule). A flake that passes once now costs one re-run, not two.
- agentic-delivery: `scripts/test-train-flake-rate.sh` also pins that the keystone `contains` helper in `merge_train.py` works when a template-less `mktemp -d` is unusable (the TMPDIR fix itself landed separately), and runs the selftests without the `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` variables that `scripts/test-ci-gates.sh` exports, which override the selftest's own `git -c user.email` identity and failed `keystone-git-helpers-on-a-real-repo`.

- agentic-delivery: `train_land.sh` now lands a flakes-only red only when each flaked test also fails at least once in `FLAKE_RUNS` (3) solo runs on the base; a test that passes 3 of 3 on the base may be an intermittent regression and the train exits `CANT` (3) with nothing landed and no PR blamed. The all-N `REAL` rule alone let a regression that fails 2 of 3 runs (p=2/3) land 70% of the time, against 26% under the old 2-of-3 rule. Seeded simulation on the real scripts (`scripts/test-train-flake-rate.sh`, 300 trials per rate): a regression clean on the base lands 0/300 at p=0.5, 2/3 and 0.9, against 161, 73 and 6 of 300 under the old 2-of-3 rule on the same draws; a genuine flake that is also flaky on the base still lands about 70% of the time. End-to-end cases in `scripts/test-train-flake-base.sh`.

### Added
- `merge_train.py` caches the verify verdict per git tree SHA for the run, so an identical tree (for example a rebuilt union that equals a prefix the bisect already proved green) is never tested twice; the log prints `CACHED <label> tree <sha7> verdict=...`.
- `merge_train.py --gate-backoff` (default 5 s, doubling, cap 300 s) sets the delay before re-running a failing `--verify-cmd`; `--backoff` (default 30) keeps governing gh retries and throttles. On the 6-PR bench fixture the default sleeps for two deterministic failures drop from 180 s to 30 s (computed from the attempt log); test-run count is unchanged at 10 there because no tree repeats.

## [1.583.0] — 2026-10-16

### Added
- Host-native install manifests: `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` plus `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` for Codex, and a root `gemini-extension.json` for Gemini CLI (context-only: it loads `AGENTS.md`, because Perun's skills live under `.claude/skills`, not the `skills/` Gemini reads). Copilot CLI documents that it reads the existing `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, so it gets no new file. The README lists one install command per host.
- Codex was smoke-tested for real with an isolated `CODEX_HOME`: `codex plugin marketplace add` then `codex plugin add deep-code-review@perun` installed the plugin and the model prompt lists all 11 skills. Gemini was validated against the documented fields only.
- `land-release.sh` stamps the new manifests' versions with `plugin.json`, and the `version` gate in `ci-gates.sh` fails if any of them drifts. `scripts/test-host-manifests.sh` checks the manifests' shape and paths.

Tests: test-host-manifests.sh ok; ci-gates version ok; bash -n land-release.sh ci-gates.sh ok.

### Fixed
- `perun_doctor.py` no longer exits 1 on a fresh default install. The janitor/scheduler and policy-file rows
  are optional add-ons that install does not ship, so they are now `INFO` rows and never fail the exit
  code; every real problem (version, hooks, drift, sandbox) still warns or fails.
- `install.sh` no longer adds a backup on every unchanged re-run or update: a backup byte-identical to the fresh copy (no symlinks anywhere in it or its path) is dropped. Install never deletes any other backup, and it refuses to back up through a symlinked `skill-backups` path.
- `perun_uninstall.py` now removes everything install wrote, from the install marker: the skill backups
  it created (shipped copies only; your pre-install copy is moved back), `house-defaults.md`, the
  `settings.local.json.bak.<timestamp>` files, the sandbox and permissions values the operating layer added,
  `settings.local.json` itself and `AGENTS.md` when install created them, the `AGENTS.md` blocks, and any
  directory left empty. On default and `--full` installs the tree is back to its pre-install state
  (0 leftovers, was 530 and 933 entries). Deletes are one file at a time, only for paths in the marker,
  each checked to resolve inside the target; no `rm -rf`. Only a provably unmodified, shipped Perun copy is deleted: a backup or skill file is removed only when its hash is one install itself shipped, anything else is kept and listed as `kept: user content`, your pre-install copy is moved back, marker keys with `..`, absolute paths or the wrong shape abort the run, and symlinked paths are skipped and never walked. `docs/getting-started.md` now points at it.
- Hardening: the marker `files` and `agent.path` keys may only name files install itself writes (slash commands, `house-defaults.md`, settings `.bak`, `delivery-lane.md`), so a forged marker cannot delete `src/app.py` or `.git/config`; `.` and `..` are not valid skill or backup names; a marker without shipped hashes keeps every file; empty-dir sweeps never follow a symlink; and the identical-backup check compares every file, `__pycache__` included.

## [1.582.0] — 2026-10-16

### Fixed
- `mutation_changed.py` no longer reports a false "OK" when a test never executes the changed code. mutmut 3.x leaves those mutants "not checked", and 1.581.0 treated them as clean. They are now reported as `NOT_COVERED <file>:<line>: changed code no test executes`, and count as findings under `--strict`. On the Python half of the vacuous-test corpus (10 vacuous, 10 genuine tests), weak tests caught rose from 5/10 to 10/10, a post-hoc result measured on the same set that exposed the bug. False positives: 1/10 equivalent mutants; 4 more genuine tests are thin enough that mutants of their code really survive.

## [1.581.0] — 2026-10-16

### Added
- `scripts/mutation_changed.py` runs mutation testing on the lines a diff changed, using a mutation tool the project already has (mutmut 3.x for Python, verified against 3.8.0; Stryker for JS/TS, not yet verified). It prints `SURVIVED <file>:<line>: <mutation>` for changed code that no test catches. Advisory unless `--strict`; it never installs anything and prints `COULD_NOT_CHECK` with an install hint when no tool or config is present. Mutation testing caught 17 of 20 vacuous tests in the 2026-10-15 comparison, against 5 of 20 for the static pass, so this is the strong check where it matters. Real-tool smoke run (n=3): both vacuous tests left survivors on the changed lines, and the genuine test left none.

### Added
- `scripts/vacuous_test_gate.py` gains a static pass, ADVISORY by default (`--strict` makes it fail the gate). It reads each changed Python or JS/TS test file and prints `VACUOUS <path>:<line>: <pattern>` for a test that runs but cannot fail: a test that calls nothing beyond scaffolding, a constant or tautological assert, a mock asserted after the test itself called it, an assertion swallowed by try/except, an early return before the asserts, an empty `pytest.raises` block, or `expect()` with no matcher. Stdlib only, no model cost; the run-report check still gates exactly as before. Measured honestly: on a held-out set written without sight of the detector it catches 5 of 20 vacuous tests with 0 of 20 false positives, and on the test suites of three popular open-source projects it flags 0.22 per 100 tests (all weak, none wrong). That is level with eslint-plugin-jest (5/20) and ahead of ruff (3/20) on the earlier corpus, but far behind mutation testing (17/20). Use mutation testing on changed lines when catching vacuous tests matters. Development fixtures: 15/20 with 0/20 false positives (`scripts/test_vacuous_static.py`).

## [1.580.0] — 2026-10-16

### Added
- agentic-delivery: `destructive_guard.py`, a PreToolUse(Bash) hook wired by the operating layer. It is a best-effort, string-level check that catches common honest mistakes; it is NOT a security boundary. The OS sandbox is the boundary (operating-discipline item 8). It never runs the command; it unwraps `bash -c`, `env`, `sudo`, `xargs`, `timeout`, `flock`, `su -c`, `busybox`, `/bin/rm`, shell keywords and braces, `$(...)` and backtick bodies, heredocs and here-strings, then denies `rm -r` on variable, glob, `..`, root, home and system paths, `git reset --hard`, `git clean -f`, force/delete/mirror push, whole-tree `git checkout|restore`, `git branch -D`, `git stash drop|clear`, `git -c alias.*=` definitions of those, `find -delete|-exec rm`, `dd` to a device, `mkfs`, `chmod -R /`, `curl | sh`, text relayed into a shell or interpreter (`echo | sh`, `base64 -d | sh`, `bash <(...)`, `source /dev/stdin`), kill-by-pattern and interpreter one-liners that delete, each with a safe alternative. A parse failure falls back to a regex scan (block on a hit). On the 32-command bench corpus it blocks 30 (was 11) with 0 of 30 false positives. Tests: `scripts/test-destructive-guard.sh`.
- Known-uncovered: interpreter APIs (`subprocess`, `exec`), IFS and brace-expansion tricks, variables holding a command, aliases, scripts and exotic wrappers.
- There is deliberately no allow list or grant: anything an agent can write, an agent can forge. The block message tells the owner to run the command themselves with the `!` prefix in Claude Code.

Auto-update is no longer blocked by a merge, rebase or cherry-pick in progress in a *linked* worktree (each has its own checkout; in a busy fleet one is always in progress, which blocked updates indefinitely). A train lock under 24 hours old in a linked worktree, and any lock in the checkout's own git dir, still block.

### Fixed
- Auto-update no longer stalls for days on a leftover lock: a `MERGE_HEAD`/rebase/train lock in a linked worktree older than 24h is ignored (logged as `ignoring stale <lock> in <dir>`); fresh locks and locks in the repo's own git dir still block. Tracked-modified managed files whose hash already matches the install marker (an install over an older commit) no longer count as uncommitted changes; user edits and `settings*.json` changes still block. After 3 consecutive skips for the same reason, `behind_warn` (session brief and operating selfcheck) adds `auto-update skipped N runs in a row: <reason>`.

## [1.565.0] — 2026-10-13

### Changed
- README and bench-results now report the 2026-10-12 paired strict-MCP benchmark (n=39, n=34 vs /code-review) with intervals and caveats; unsupported earlier claims removed.

- Benchmark reviewers now run with `--strict-mcp-config`: account-level claude.ai connectors otherwise attached about 140k input tokens to every reviewer call ($0.585 vs $0.002 for the same one-line read), which swamped review cost and made arms incomparable.

### Fixed
- agentic-delivery: test-result parsers fail closed. `train_flake.sh` exits 2 with `could not check` when its failed-ids file is missing (it used to read as "no REAL failures", exit 0); `train_land.sh` no longer treats a `GREEN` log line as a pass when the verify step exited non-zero (for example SIGKILLed after printing it). Tests: `scripts/test-train-failclosed.sh`.
- agentic-delivery: a failed `gh pr list` in `land_train.sh` no longer reads as "no stacked children" (the merge would close them); it prints `could not check: ...` and exits 1. `train_land.sh` does the same for a failed PR base read, and its no-GREEN line shows the verify step's rc and last output line. `land_train.sh` names the failing step (line and command) instead of exiting silently.
- `_lock.sh`: a busy lock reports holder alive/dead/unknown and age; a waiter says who it waits on and a dead holder still stops the wait with the exact hand-reclaim command (nothing deleted).
- New `gh_rest.py`: one shared curl fallback for `gh api` when gh fails TLS in a macOS sandbox (`x509: OSStatus -26276`); used by `board_common`, `surface_check`, `merge_train` and as the default `GH` of the train and cleanup scripts. `gh pr ...` has no fallback and fails with the cause named. Tests: `scripts/test-delivery-friction.sh`. `gh_rest.py` sends POST when `--input` is given without `-X` (as `gh api` does) and passes the token to curl on stdin, not argv.
- `clean_finished.sh`: an `lsof` error or unavailable result now counts as "in use / could not check": the worktree is skipped with the reason printed, not removed.
- `clean_finished.sh`: `SCRATCH` paths are deleted only when they resolve strictly inside `$TMPDIR`; anything else is skipped with a message.



### Added
- release-engineering: gate-tooling rule that a zero failure count needs exit status and a summary line first (a killed run parses as zero failures), with an eval.

### Fixed
- Field logs showed hundreds of daily host refusals (`Blocked: sleep N`, "names git in a form too complex to verify"). A fixed two-line `HOST_RULES` block (never `sleep N` to wait; plain separate git commands from the worktree root, no `cd X &&` chains or loops) is now always injected by `session_brief.py` at SessionStart and by `subagent_start_inject.py` at SubagentStart, even when `house-defaults.md` is missing; both read one constant.
- `heavy_gate.py` kept a stateless deny that contradicted the lane preamble's "retry at most 3 times, then proceed". It now keeps a ledger and allows the command with a WARN after 3 denies of the same command in the same cwd within 30 minutes.
- The operating-layer template no longer sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE`; it keeps the `sonnet` default, and `FORCE` was overriding the Opus high-stakes review pass.

### Added

Adds owner-format regression fixtures and one failing fixture per rule.

## [1.557.0] — 2026-10-09

### Changed
- idea-critic (Veles): tightened the calibration rule. REVISE or HOLD now requires a concrete failure scenario tied to the proposal (named condition, bad outcome, why the stated evidence and kill criterion do not cover it); generic "may", "might" and "consider X" risks and "can't re-verify" become non-blocking notes under PASS_TO_USER; evidence cited with provenance is taken as given. Diagnosis of the prior runs: the over-rejections came from the critic distrusting stated evidence and raising speculative risks that the proposal's own observation and kill criterion already covered. Refs #1380.
- idea-critic evals: six new PASS controls and two new must-HOLD cases (tuning set), plus a frozen held-out file `evals/heldout.json` (6 sound PASS proposals, 4 must-HOLD/REVISE) written before scoring.
- Live A/B (claude -p, sonnet, no tools, 3 replicates, keyword objection predicates, 95% bootstrap CI). **In-sample (tuning set, 19 cases)**: the rule wording and three controls were tuned on these cases using critic output (earlier iterations scored PASS accuracy 0.60 and 0.70), so treat as optimistic. PASS accuracy: plain 0.23 [0.10-0.40], Veles before 0.70 [0.53-0.87], Veles after 0.87 [0.73-0.97]; HOLD/REVISE accuracy before 0.96, after 1.00; objection recall before 0.85 [0.70-0.96], after 0.93 [0.81-1.00].
- **Held-out (10 cases, n=18 PASS runs, n=12 HOLD/REVISE runs)**: PASS accuracy: plain 0.22 [0.06-0.44], Veles before 0.33 [0.11-0.56], Veles after 0.50 [0.28-0.72]; HOLD/REVISE accuracy: plain 1.00, before 1.00, after 1.00 (all [1.00-1.00]); objection recall (loose keyword predicate, weak signal) 1.00 for all arms. Held-out cases were written without reading the rule wording but the author had seen earlier critic output on the tuning set. Verdict: held-out PASS accuracy rose (CIs overlap) and HOLD/REVISE accuracy did not drop, but held-out PASS accuracy is 0.50, below the 0.8 absolute bar; the improvement is directional, not established.

- Review benchmark harness: every `bench_corpus.py run` now writes a fresh run dir `runs/<arm>-<rep>-<timestamp>/` made with `mkdir` (a second driver that picks the same name is refused), with a `manifest.json` (model, skill SHA-256, settings) and a `COMPLETE` marker; `verify` and `report` read exactly one complete run dir. Previously arms shared one `--out` dir, so a stray driver overwrote finished records mid-analysis.

## [1.549.0] — 2026-10-09

### Added
- Review benchmark corpus expanded from 18 to 90 held-out TEST cases (Go 31, Python 25, JS 19, shell 15) and from 9 to 44 TRAIN cases. The 62 newest cases come from permissive-licence public repositories through the existing builder and filters (introducing-commit diff of at most 600 lines, non-trivial fix, ground truth inside the diff, no duplicate of an existing case). TEST answers, patches and SHAs stay out of the repository exactly as before; the committed manifest carries hashed TEST ids, language, repository URL and licence only. TRAIN fixtures and upstream licence texts are committed under `scripts/eval-fixtures/bench/`. New check: `scripts/test_bench_corpus_90.py`.

No-Mechanism-Reason: data and test-only change; no SKILL.md or references file touched.

## [1.548.0] — 2026-10-09

### Added
- idea-critic: standing skeptic checks for self-proposed work (user value vs replay, verify operational advice against host docs, who is worse off by a new default, simpler safe-by-design alternative, restate the real constraint), plus six eval fixtures for real decision misses and two PASS controls. Refs #1380.

- idea-critic: calibration rule (named evidence + measured kill criterion + safe rollback + no concrete flaw = PASS_TO_USER with at most one note) and four PASS controls.
- Live A/B (claude -p, sonnet, no tools, 3 replicates, 11 cases, keyword predicates because idea-critic binds no eval_predicates; 95% bootstrap CI): plain vs skill verdict accuracy 0.70 [0.55-0.85] vs 0.85 [0.73-0.97]; miss-case accuracy 0.90 vs 0.95; PASS-control accuracy 0.33 [0.08-0.58] vs 0.67 [0.42-0.92]; objection recall 0.57 [0.38-0.76] vs 0.86 [0.71-1.00]. Point estimates favor the skill on every metric; CIs overlap on accuracy, so the accuracy gain is not statistically established. Skill still returns REVISE on 4 of 12 PASS-control runs.

## [1.547.0] — 2026-10-09

### Changed

- Repo-scanning gates now enumerate git files instead of walking the filesystem: `ci-gates.sh privacy` and `size`, the `land-release.sh` size-row regen and `perun_doctor.py` read `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard` at a git work-tree root, so nested worktrees and gitignored build directories are never scanned (a planted violation there no longer fails every push). `find`/full walk remains only outside a git root. Pinned by `scripts/test_scan_tracked_only.py`. The other `os.walk` users (lint/test scanners over caller-named paths, transcript walks) take explicit paths and are unchanged.

### Added

- Per-PR independent review gate (warn-first). `agentic-delivery/scripts/review_gate.py`, called per member PR by `land_train.sh` (so `train_land.sh` inherits it), looks for a review receipt (`.perun/reviews/<pr>.json`, written by `review_gate.py receipt`) or a `perun-review` PR comment marker from a reviewer other than the author, for the exact head being merged. New policy key `review_gate`: `warn` (default), `enforce`, `off`. **Warn-only for this release**: a PR with no receipt prints a WARN and still lands; `enforce` skips it; `review_gate=off` opts out. The gate proves an independent review run on the current head (reviewer run id differs from the author's), not a different human; an unexpected error in warn mode warns and never blocks. Expect `enforce` to become the default in a later release. Routed from `agentic-delivery/SKILL.md`; tested by `scripts/test_review_gate.py`.

## [1.543.0] — 2026-10-08

### Fixed

New `scripts/test-no-hang-without-pgrep.sh` asserts the SKIP and prompt return.

## [1.542.0] — 2026-10-08

- Installed Perun now updates itself. The operating layer adds a SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hook (`perun_auto_update.py`) that, at most once every 6 hours per project and in a detached background process, checks the newest `vX.Y.Z` release tag on the recorded remote and re-applies the recorded install flags from it through `scripts/update-installed.sh`. Your settings still win and backups are written. It skips, and logs why, while a merge or train lock exists or a Perun-managed file was edited; every run appends one line to `~/.cache/perun/auto-update.log`. Turn it off with policy key `auto_update: "off"` in `.perun/policy.json` or `install.sh --no-auto-update`. No session restart is needed: skills and settings live-reload, and only a model change waits for the next session.

## [1.518.0] — 2026-10-07

### Added
- `deep-code-review/templates/perun-review.yml`: opt-in reusable GitHub workflow for PR-native review. Job 1 runs the review headless and read-only (`contents: read`, read-only tools, per-run spend cap) and uploads a findings artifact; job 2 (`pull-requests: write`, `checks: write`, base checkout, no model key) runs `post_review.sh --post`, replaces its prior pending review on re-push, and updates one sticky comment and one check run with severity counts. `pull_request` only; fork PRs are skipped. `install.sh` never writes it.

The post job sanitizes model output (severity enum, commit pinned to the PR head, size caps) and dry-runs `post_review.sh` before deleting the prior pending review. The dead grounding step is removed. Prerequisites now include a non-empty `.banlist.txt`.

## [1.488.0] — 2026-10-06

### Added
- `agentic-delivery/scripts/clean_finished.sh`: removes your own worktrees whose PR is merged or closed or whose lane handed back, and your own scratch. A dirty worktree is archived first (`git diff HEAD` plus the untracked list). It skips a worktree a process uses or that has unpushed commits.
- `reap_own.sh`: kills are verified (`kill -0`, SIGKILL after 5 seconds), the default idle cutoff is 2 hours, and `--report` is a read-only cross-session mode (orphans by worktree path, free RAM, `FINDING hot` for high CPU over 2 hours).
- `train_land.sh`: optional `CLEAN_ROOT` runs both scripts at train start. `lane-preamble.md`: teardown step with the `orphans=0` hand-back check. Rules in `merge-operations.md` (#1324). Tests in `scripts/test-train-scripts.sh`.

## [1.472.0] — 2026-09-30

### Added
- Design port takes content from real source-of-truth data, never the mockup's sample fixture (`deep-code-review`'s `rendered-parity.md`): a production module importing a design-sample/fixture module is a finding on its own, and a parity scorer treats a sample-vs-real text diff as harness noise, not a mismatch (#1249).
- Parity tolerances are narrow and self-tested, never a blanket percentage (`rendered-parity.md`): scope each tolerance to a region/selector/viewport with a bound, reason, and decision reference, proven by a self-test that a fresh diff in that region still fails (#1250).
- A copy-on-write dependency clone inherits its source's corruption silently (`agentic-delivery`'s `dev-env-ownership.md`): validate the clone against a known corruption pattern, or clean-install, before trusting it for a release-gating check (#1251).
- A bypassed local gate with no committed record is a finding, not a silent exception (`deep-code-review`'s `branch-and-merge-hygiene.md`): an untraced `--no-verify` is reported; a logged bypass still doesn't clear the required forge check (#1252).
- An outward effect (send/charge/publish/delete/webhook) reporting success after a swallowed or unawaited failure is a finding (`reliability-error-handling.md`, pointed at from `billing-correctness.md`) (#1253).
- Orchestration-cost checklist for multi-agent delivery runs (`agentic-delivery`'s `cost-quality-guardrails.md`): event-driven wakes over timed check-ins, an always-loaded rule-size budget, no leaked background shells, per-lane token budgets, model-tier routing (#1254).
- Merge-train robustness: per-PR-and-pair bisect over full-train re-runs, behavior-change PRs port their own specs, committed generated docs don't survive a train, capability-gated UI needs an explicit test stub (`deep-code-review`'s `merge-operations.md`) (#1255).
- Release PRs never use the integration branch as head when head branches auto-delete on merge (`merge-operations.md`) (#1256).
- Committed UX evidence and harness-isolated worktrees both need the repo's own sparse-checkout discipline, not ad hoc growth (`agentic-delivery`'s `merge-queue-worktrees.md`); a refused cross-branch push stays refused when routed through a peer (`multi-session-coordination.md`); an owner's multi-part request becomes a tracked checklist immediately so a compaction can't silently drop part of it (`unattended-trackers.md`) (#1257).
- 9 new evals (6 deep-code-review, 3 agentic-delivery), one per lesson above.

## [1.470.0] — 2026-09-28

### Added
- Liveness/status derived from the signal's date, with a verified terminal state override (`data-freshness.md`): compute an active/live bucket from age-of-latest-signal, never assert it free-text; distinguish signal TYPE (a real release vs. a CMS-edit/fork-sync/archival commit/bot mirror) so a weak signal never reads as thriving; and a human-verified terminal state (wound-down/acquired/ceased) overrides the date bucket outright (#1232).
- Enrichment-pilot gating on verified-correct-entity rate (`data-quality.md` §11): a pilot's headline metric is the verified-correct-entity rate cross-checked against an independent source, not raw hit-rate or cost — resolve a strong key first, cross-check-and-discard on any name-search fallback (#1233).
- Quality-score ruler naming (`data-scoring.md`, cross-referenced from `rendered-parity.md`'s flag-set-pinning section): every reported quality/coverage/audit score states its ruler (tolerance count, exclusions) beside the number, and a ruler change gets a one-time old-ruler/new-ruler dual report on the same head so the delta is attributable to the ruler, not the product (#1234).
- Away-mode decision holding (`unattended-operating-mode.md`): while the owner is away, decisions are deferred to the ledger, never posted as a message; the owner's next message is answered first, then the full pending batch is appended once; an answered item drops from the pending batch; peer sessions route through the conductor's ledger, never message the owner directly (#1235).
- Link-to-human verification by rendered content (`verification-handback.md`): a link handed to a human is probed at the exact URL (no extra query parameters/cookies), asserted on a content marker unique to the real page (never HTTP status alone), with the environment's flag state stated in the same message (#1238).
- Merge-train cheap-checks-first and defect-list open-PR coverage (`merge-operations.md`, `unattended-trackers.md`): run cheap, union-only checks (a ratchet, a lint pass) before the full aggregate gate; and before fanning a computed defect list out to fix lanes, tag each remaining defect with the open PR that already covers it or re-measure on a union including ready PRs (#1240).
- 3 new evals (deep-code-review) for the liveness, enrichment-pilot, and ruler-naming lessons; 2 new evals (agentic-delivery) for the link-verification and merge-train lessons; 1 new eval (agentic-ceo) for the away-mode decision lesson.

## [1.469.0] — 2026-09-28

### Added
- Multi-replica hazard for in-process coordination (`concurrency-shared-state.md`): a mutex, an idempotency-key set, or an event emitter built from in-process state gives its guarantee on one replica only and silently gives none once a second instance joins, verified by driving the same idempotent request and lock-guarded section from two independent instances at once (#1225).
- Throughput-benchmark methodology (`testing-situational.md`): a single-process throughput ceiling measured on a shared, unrecorded host with a client timeout shorter than the server's real response time is untrustworthy — requires a recorded/confirmed-quiet host and failures broken out by client-timeout vs. server-error, verified by comparing a benchmark run with and without competing background load (#1226).
- Fork/clone stale-brief and fileless single-flight lock (`multi-session-coordination.md`): a forked agent inherits its parent's entire prior context, so a narrower fork-time instruction doesn't erase an earlier broader one — verified by checking the fork's actual tool calls, not its summary; and the same atomic-claim-token mechanism extends to expensive shared measurement work with no file of its own, keyed by the measurement's identity rather than a path (#1227).
- Shared-quota outage recovery (`multi-session-coordination.md`): recovering a fleet that shares one account's usage limit needs a self-scheduled wake tied to the stated reset time, resuming from every known worktree before dispatching new lanes, and re-discovering peer identity rather than assuming a stable name survived the gap (#1228).
- Parallel-lane SSRF guard version drift, hand-rolled fetch-replacement footguns, and a Next.js instrumentation Edge-compile trap (`security-appsec.md`, `lang-js-ts.md`): a diff reusing an "existing" guard can be routing through a stale pre-hardening copy a concurrent lane extracted; a hand-rolled `fetch` replacement re-introduces classic 204/205/304, streaming, abort, content-encoding, and Happy Eyeballs bugs plus an identity-based opt-out footgun; and a negative early-return guard in `instrumentation.ts` still pulls a server-only module into the dev Edge compile (#1231; the stacked-PR base-branch-deletion lesson in the same issue was already covered in `merge-operations.md`).
- 7 new evals (deep-code-review), one per lesson above; 3 new evals (agentic-delivery) for the fork/single-flight and outage-recovery lessons.

## [1.468.0] — 2026-09-28

### Added
- Change-history table with no reachable UI view (`ux-interaction.md`): recording who/what/when history to a table or append-only log does not satisfy an audit-trail requirement without a reachable control (a panel, tab, or expandable section) rendering it on the record's own surface, verified as a regular user of the running product, not by a database query or export (#1212).
- Load/swarm harness failure classification (`testing-situational.md`): a load-generating harness's own failure modes (client-pool exhaustion, a harness-side concurrency bug, contended resources) can produce a signal indistinguishable from a real bug, requiring a direct store/API state check plus a decorrelated second pass, and a four-way classification (acked-but-missing / stored-but-not-shown / harness-misread / never-acked) before scoping any fix (#1215).
- Load/soak/swarm harness authentication and read-back trust (`testing-situational.md`): a harness whose simulated writes aren't authenticated like a real client, or whose end-of-run existence check reads the store once with no retry, reports numbers that aren't real in both directions (false success on a silently-dropped write, false failure on a not-yet-visible one); requires real auth, a per-write store-level ack check, retry-with-backoff on the recheck, and a per-category dispatched-action count (#1224).
- Fan-out cost calibration and lane-weighting (`model-tiering.md`): pacing a multi-agent run against a shared quota needs the estimate calibrated against at least one real quota-remaining reading per session, and a fan-out plan sized by summed tier-weighted lane cost, not lane headcount (#1217).
- Shared-branch rebase/force-push detection (`branch-and-merge-hygiene.md`): validated commands to detect a branch is shared (more than one contributor's commits ahead of the target, or checked out in another worktree) before treating a rebase-then-force-push as safe; merge the base in instead (#1223).
- Cosmetic ratchet-gaming split (`method-situational.md`): a size/line-count/complexity ratchet gate made to pass by mechanically splitting a file with no coherent internal boundary is a gamed proxy, not a fix; a genuine split follows a nameable seam and doesn't leave the two files tightly mutually coupled (#1223).
- 7 new evals (deep-code-review), one per lesson above (two for the load/swarm harness lessons).

## [1.467.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- Flag-swap render-tree parity (`release-engineering.md`): a feature flag that swaps a production route's rendered content must render the same component tree the reviewed preview route was measured through, including every layout wrapper or context provider, verified by diffing the flag-on route's component tree against the preview route's rather than trusting a matching screenshot (#1206).
- Theme-attribute scope mismatch (`ux-components.md`): a dark-mode/theme stylesheet scoped to a data attribute or class is only conformant once checked against where the toggle actually writes that attribute in the live DOM, not merely that the CSS rule and the toggle both exist, verified by driving the real control and inspecting computed styles rather than code presence (#1207).
- Hardcoded live-looking count badge (`ux-dataviz.md`): a UI literal that reads as live/social-proof data (a viewer/online/activity count, an "as of"/"last updated" string) is a release-blocking data-honesty defect, not a style nit, verified by tracing the literal back to a real fetch/computation (#1209).
- Ported Tab-handler keyboard trap (`a11y-focus.md`): a keyboard handler ported from a reference implementation that unconditionally captures Tab is a WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap violation once the widget has nothing left to cycle to, verified by a full keyboard-only Tab/Shift+Tab sweep through every internal state (#1210).
- Optimistic input-clear before write resolves (`ux-writes.md`): a write fired without awaiting its result that clears the input immediately loses the user's draft silently on failure, verified by forcing the write to reject and confirming the typed content and a visible error both survive (#1211).
- 5 new evals (deep-code-review), one per lesson above.

## [1.466.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- Client-gate-to-server-recheck authorization tracing (`appsec-design.md`): a client-side permission/state gate is UX, not a security boundary, until traced to the server endpoint(s) it calls and confirmed each independently re-derives the condition from server-trusted data, verified by calling the endpoint directly with the request the UI would never construct (#1202).
- Shared-endpoint hardening scoping (`appsec-design.md`): moving a client-only check onto a shared server endpoint must be scoped to the caller/flow that needed it (enumerate every caller first) rather than blanket-applied, since the strictest caller's rule can break other legitimate callers' looser cases (#1203).
- Client-vs-server-truth cross-reference (`frontend-security.md`): one bullet pointing to `appsec-design.md`'s new authorization-tracing procedure from the frontend/UX review angle (#1202).
- Multi-backend TOCTOU re-check mirroring (`concurrency-shared-state.md`, DB / store TOCTOU): an ownership/permission re-check landed inside a locked write on one storage backend is unproven until confirmed on every backend implementing the same write path, verified by a concurrent-request test run against each backend the codebase ships (#1204).
- Multi-step move (create-then-delete) idempotency (`reliability-error-handling.md`): a move/promote/publish operation built from create-then-delete needs an idempotency key or equivalent marker, a delete gated on confirmed create commit, and an idempotent create, verified by fault-injecting the response after create and confirming a retry lands exactly one copy (#1205).
- Demo/sample-mode write isolation (`release-engineering.md`): every write must route through one shared guard that checks demo/sandbox mode, rather than trusting each call site to remember the check, verified by an instrumentation test asserting zero real-store writes across every write path with the mode active (#1208).
- 5 new evals (deep-code-review), one per lesson above.

## [1.465.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- `parity_differ.py` enforces the flag/option-set pin and the served-design-bundle checksum in the tool itself, not only in doctrine (`rendered-parity.md`, `migration-parity.md`): `--baseline`'s fingerprint now pins `style`/`min_pairs`/`style_min_pairs`, so a re-invocation under a different combination is `COULD_NOT_CHECK`, never silently scored or misread as a `REGRESSION`; new `--design-bundle-dir`/`--design-checksum` refuses to score against a served bundle whose files don't match a recorded `sha256sum`-format manifest (#1237).
- `agentic-delivery`'s standing modes (terse reports, minimal-code bias) are enforced at the host's `SubagentStart` event: `scripts/subagent_start_inject.py` injects one project-owned house-defaults file into every newly-spawned subagent's context, dropping `MINIMAL-CODE:`-tagged lines for agent types in `HOUSE_MINIMAL_CODE_EXEMPT_TYPES` (design-port/design-alignment lanes) and stripping the tag for everyone else (`host-enforcement.md` "Standing modes at SubagentStart", `multi-session-coordination.md`) (#1218).
- `scripts/host_probe.py` computes the fan-out spawn/hold predicate as one script: swap-trend and free-RAM-as-veto, the paired load+CPU-idle brake for `cpu`-lane types, free disk against a measured per-lane footprint, the live-lane cap, and a gate-latency canary (`--canary CMD --baseline-file F`, ~2x baseline holds) — prints `SPAWN`/`HOLD <reason>`/`COULD_NOT_CHECK <what>`, never a spawn on a could-not-check (`fanout-host-sizing.md` "Gate on free RAM and the swap trend") (#1220).
- `model-tiering.md` "Route delivery lanes by work type and stage": routes a delivery lane's executor (not just review strictness) by work type — cheapest/low-effort for fully specified mechanical steps, mid for build/fix/audit, top/high-effort for security re-review and hard design decisions — with riders against tiering dedupe/classification work to the cheapest tier and against a per-lane stronger-model consult tool in a quota-bound fleet (spend multiplies by lane count) (#1221).
- `agentic-delivery/references/operating-discipline.md`: the always-on operating layer's one entry point, one line per item pointing at the section that owns the depth (communication/minimal-code modes, hand-back caps, model/effort routing, fan-out probing, usage pacing, conductor rules, cross-session coordination, safety rules); `install.sh --with-operating-layer` writes a `settings.operating-layer.json.new` snippet (the `SubagentStart` injector, two-tier `SubagentStop` cap, subagent model pin) to merge by hand; `scripts/operating_selfcheck.py` reports each item `PRESENT`/`MISSING`/`COULD_NOT_CHECK` (#1222).
- 4 new evals (deep-code-review, model-tiering work-type routing).

## [1.464.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- Regression-test proof discipline (`testing-and-evals.md`): a fix's regression test must show an executed red-then-green transition (a pre-fix run, or a fix-logic-only revert-and-rerun) — reading the diff and reasoning "this would have failed" is never sufficient (#1201).
- Orchestration-layer verify-don't-trust (`parallel-audit.md` section 4): a lane's causal claim about a failure or a fix needs the same independent re-verification against actual evidence as a review finding before a conductor acts on it; a gate passed via an override/escape-hatch is a distinct, lower-trust status that must be disclosed, never folded into an undifferentiated "passed" (#1213).
- Confirmed-merge gate on issue closing (`merge-operations.md` §6 continued): merge automation closes the linked issue only once the target branch's head commit is confirmed to contain the merged change (commit ancestry), never on "the merge command returned success" alone (#1214).
- Held-lane message discipline (`multi-session-coordination.md` "Bridge in-flight agents"; `unattended-operating-mode.md` run-start checklist; `templates/lane-preamble.md`): any message resumes a held/idle lane with its full context, so a new standing rule reaches held lanes through the shared record they re-read on resume, never a broadcast; a run-start checklist item lists held lanes before any broadcast (#1219).
- Attended-to-unattended profile switch (`host-enforcement.md`, a Host-enforced instance): one environment variable read by a `SubagentStart` hook selects the house-default profile file injected into every new spawn (#1219).
- Default autonomous-run profile (`unattended-operating-mode.md` "What it composes"): an unattended grant carries terse chat/minimal-code/critical-work-only defaults without the owner restating them, propagated the same way as any other standing default and verified in a spawned subagent's own context; a decision that would otherwise wait on the owner is attacked by `idea-critic` before the reversible-choice default is taken, with only irreversible/shared-state/Human-gate items still parked (#1230).

## [1.460.0] — 2026-09-25

### Added
- Delivery, from field feedback: lanes bootstrap gitignored assets into a fresh worktree before judging lint or types. A brief never asks a read-only agent type to write a file. Plans classify each feature as provider or consumer before lanes start. One browser-test run per worktree, with a lock and a timeout. A moved base is merged, never rebased, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` exposes a rewrite. Two stacked lanes may share a file when their changed files don't overlap, or when the parent lane is frozen.
- Review: filters on unauthenticated paths are allowlists. Never suggest a command that prints a secret into the session. An authenticated load test proves its identity resolved before measuring, and the harness itself fails closed on an auth failure. Perf gates cover every production storage adapter and judge heap slope. Leak and perf gates run the deploy's runtime major. Streaming heap-snapshot analysis is doctrine — guidance for a multi-GB snapshot; no analyzer ships with the skill. Request-scoped fire-and-forget async pins memory. Lint counts compare full scope against the base head, and a cap is never raised in a feature change. e2e uses real pointer input, not programmatic clicks. Tests mock system probes and pin commit samples.
- `reaper_lint.py` `ENV_OPTION_AFTER_ASSIGNMENT`: `env A=1 -u B cmd` exits 127 on BSD/macOS. Per `lang-shell.md` guidance, a harness that boots a child fails fast on its early exit and prints the child's log tail.

### Changed
- The skip-CI marker is keyed to the CI state. The commit-body cap exempts required trailer keys only. A check that cannot run locally is an evidenced, logged skip that stays UNVERIFIED, and the deploy gate blocks release until it passes.
- 20 new evals (agentic-delivery 9, deep-code-review 11).

## [1.459.0] — 2026-09-25

### Added
- Owner-facing delivery: a deferred ask is named to the owner, with a reason, in the cycle it was deferred, and a standing "currently deferred" list is part of routine status (#1187). An orchestrator reports backlog closed against total, not lanes or merges (#1181). A complaint is restated as a scoped ask, not auto-spawned into lanes (#1182). A measurement lane needs a named pending decision (#1184). Status gives the exact number against its target (#1185).
- Delivery mechanics: recurring loops read the delta since the last tick, replacing the "re-read each turn" default (#1186). Fan-out width is min(host headroom, editable seams) (#1183). Confirm an observed gap in code before briefing a fix lane (#1172). Release-proving tooling is versioned, not left in scratch (#1173). CI that cannot block merges is switched off, with a local receipt bound to the head SHA (owner authorization still required). Worktree hygiene and a safe prune. An empty gate baseline reports UNVERIFIED, not a pass.
